23.en: **Two nations.** An angel revealed to Rebekah something of the future of the two sons soon to be born (PP 177). Already, it seemed, they were struggling for the supremacy. The angel’s prediction was fulfilled in the later history of Esau’s and Jacob’s descendants, the Edomites and the Israelites. These two brother nations were ever enemies, Israel usually proving to be the stronger of the two. David subjugated the Edomites (2 Sam. 8:14; 1 Kings 11:16), and King Amaziah later defeated them (2 Kings 14:7; 2 Chron. 25:11, 12). The Hasmonaean king John Hyrcanus I finally brought their independence to an end in the year 126 .., when he forced them to accept the rite of circumcision and the law of Moses, and to submit to a Jewish governor. God’s insight into the respective characters of Esau and Jacob and His foresight into their future made possible His selection of Jacob as inheritor of the birthright and progenitor of Christ even before his birth (Rom. 8:29; 9:10–14).

25.zh:
先產的身體發紅，渾身有毛，如同皮衣，他們就給他起名叫以掃【就是有毛的意思】。

紅（`admoni），以東這個名字可能源於此詞（另見30節）。該希伯來詞還用來描述大衛的相貌（撒上16:12；17:42）。該詞的意思與拉丁語Rufus（魯孚）相似，這是新約時代兩個人的名字（可15:21；羅16:13）。以掃毛髮的過度生長，在醫學上被稱為多毛病。其症狀在出生時就已經十分顯著了，後來成為其外貌最明顯的特徵。
**他們就給他起名叫以掃。**父母二人都認為這個名字很恰當。上下文的內容使某些學者認為這個名稱來源於一個表示“多毛”的未知詞根。但我們無法依據現有的信息來確定其含義。
25.en:
**Red.** Heb. ’admoni, probably the root from which the name Edom was derived (see also v. 30). The same Hebrew word is used to describe David’s appearance (1 Sam. 16:12; 17:42). It is similar in meaning to the Latin Rufus the name assigned to two men of NT times (Mark 15:21; Rom. 16:13). Esau’s excessive growth of hair, known medically as hypertrichosis, already noticeable at birth, later became the most significant feature of his physical appearance.
**They called his name Esau.** Both parents agreed upon the appropriateness of this name. The context has led some scholars to suggest its derivation from an unknown root signifying “to be covered with hair.” Its meaning, however, cannot be determined from available information.

26.zh:
隨後又生了以掃的兄弟，手抓住以掃的腳跟，因此給他起名叫雅各【就是抓住的意思】。利百加生下兩個兒子的時候，以撒年正六十歲。

“腳跟”一詞的希伯來原文`aqeb，與動詞`aqab，“抓住腳跟”有關，喻指“欺騙”。“ 雅各”的意思是“他抓住腳跟”或“他欺騙”。因此，這是最為恰當的。它不僅使人想起在他出生時所發生的事，也是對他品格和命運的預言。關於以撒在兩個兒子出生時的年齡，見19-21節註釋。
26.en: **His name was called Jacob.** The Hebrew word for “heel,” ‘aqeb, is related to the verb ‘aqab, “to take by the heel,” figuratively, “to deceive.” The personal name Jacob, meaning “he grasps the heel” or “he deceives,” was therefore most appropriate. It was not only reminiscent of the incident at his birth, but prophetic of his character and destiny. On the age of Isaac at the time of the birth of his two sons, see on vs. 19-21.

27.zh:
兩個孩子漸漸長大，以掃善於打獵，常在田野；雅各為人安靜，常住在帳棚裡。

**以掃善於打獵。**隨著兩個孩子的成長，他們品格上的巨大的差別顯現了出來。以掃性情粗暴，喜歡田野和叢林中任性和冒險的生活（見創27:3）。
**雅各為人安靜。**“安靜”的希伯來語tam，表示親切、虔誠和有教養的個性。家庭穩定生活的責任在以掃看來是極其單調和令人煩躁，但對於“為人安靜，常住在帳棚裡”的雅各來說卻如魚得水。以掃從未擺脫青春期身體和情感上的浮躁不安，而雅各卻隨著自己的成熟而培養出堅定的品格和良好的判斷力。
27.en:
**Esau was a cunning hunter.** As the two boys grew up a great difference in character became evident. Esau displayed a rough, capricious disposition, and reveled in the wild, adventurous life of field and forest (see ch. 27:3).
**Jacob was a plain man.** The Hebrew word tam, here translated “plain,” suggests an amiable, pious, and cultured personality. The duties and responsibilities of settled family life, so monotonous and irritating to Esau, came naturally to Jacob, “a plain man, dwelling in tents.” Whereas Esau never outgrew the physical and emotional restlessness of adolescence, Jacob developed the stability of character and soundness of judgment that should come with maturity.

28.zh:
以撒愛以掃，因為常吃他的野味；利百加卻愛雅各。

以撒盲目地偏愛長子，而不顧兒子擔任一家之主的品格條件，給家庭造成了紛爭，導致了弟兄之間以及他們的後代之間多世紀的冤屈、痛苦與不公。以撒對以掃的偏愛，似乎是由於、或至少部分是由於他對野味的喜好。先祖讓他的愛，他的正義感，和他的虔誠受制於他的食慾，實在令人吃驚和失望。他的經歷也是對我們的一種警告。偏愛一個孩子過於另一個孩子，無疑地會造成嫉妒、紛爭、怨恨和痛苦。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》177。
28.en: **Isaac loved Esau.** Isaac’s blind partiality for his first-born, irrespective of the son’s character qualifications for family leadership, brought division into the family. As a result, wrong, misery, and injustice marked relations between the brothers and their posterity for centuries. Isaac’s preference for Esau seems to have been based, in part at least, on his love for venison. The extent to which the patriarch let his love and his sense of justice and piety be controlled by his appetite is surprising and disappointing. His experience is, furthermore, a warning to us. To prefer one child above another inevitably creates jealousy, division, bitterness, and misery.

9.en:
**Another dream.** If Joseph’s first dream had pointed only to supremacy over his brothers, the second extended it to the entire family. That Joseph should have related this dream to his brothers, after seeing how they had reacted to the first one, reveals a decided immaturity of judgment. This dream could only intensify their envy and hatred. Joseph, however, seems to have felt a certain satisfaction in telling his dreams and watching his brothers’ envy and anger. Jacob, who was present upon this occasion, administered him a sharp rebuke, partly, perhaps, in surprise, and partly to disavow any collusion on his own part. Though Jacob disapproved of the narration of the dream, he could not avoid being impressed by the way in which it reflected his own thoughts.
Some have questioned the divine origin of the second dream, inasmuch as it seems to have met but partial fulfillment. Neither Rachel nor Leah lived to see the rulership of Joseph’s in Egypt (chs. 35:19; 49:31). It is sufficient to note that even Jacob did not take every detail of the dream thus literally, since Joseph’s mother was already dead at the time (v. 10). Jacob apparently understood the dream as representative of Joseph’s supremacy in a general sense.
9.zh:
後來他又做了一夢，也告訴他的哥哥們說：看哪，我又做了一夢，夢見太陽、月亮，與十一個星向我下拜。

約瑟的第一個夢只是說他要高於他的兄弟，第二個夢則是說要高於整個家族。約瑟看到他們對第一個夢的反應之後，依然把第二個夢告訴他們，這說明他思想的幼稚。這個夢只會加深他們的嫉妒和仇恨。但約瑟似乎樂於講述他的夢並看他到兄弟的嫉妒和忿怒。在場的雅各嚴厲地責備了他，一方面可能出於驚奇，一方面是為了否認自己與這事有份。雅各雖然不贊成把這個夢說出來，但他卻不由得因該夢反映了他自己的想法而吃驚。
有人懷疑第二個夢的神聖起源，因為它似乎只有部分地應驗。拉結和利亞都未能活著見到約瑟在埃及為尊（創35:19；49:31）。其實連雅各也沒有這麼刻板地理解夢的每個細節，因為約瑟的母親此時已經去世了（第10節）。雅各顯然將這個夢理解為象徵約瑟在一般意義上為尊的地位。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–11節）**。《救贖的故事》101。

5.en: **Joseph dreamed a dream.** The coat implied Jacob’s intention of making Rachel’s older son his heir; now, Joseph’s dream was taken as an expression of his own intentions in the matter. They hated him, not only because of the dream, but also for his boldness in telling them about it (v. 8). Though it is not stated that Joseph’s dreams were of God (chs. 20:3–7; 28:12–15), the subsequent history of his life makes it virtually certain that this was so, and that they were not the reflection of any personal ambition on his part. Joseph’s dream shows that Jacob did not limit his pursuits to cattle and sheep raising, but was also engaged in agriculture, as his father Isaac had been before him (ch. 26:12). Such activity had been implied in Isaac’s paternal blessing (ch. 27:28).
5.zh:
約瑟做了一夢，告訴他哥哥們，他們就越發恨他。

綵衣透露了雅各立拉結的長子為嗣的想法。現在約瑟的夢則被視為他自己有這樣的願望。他們恨他不僅是因為夢本身，而且是因為他膽敢將這個夢告訴他們（第8節）。聖經雖然沒有說明約瑟的夢來自上帝（創20:3-7；28:12-15），但他人生以後的歷史證明這確實是出於上帝，而不是他個人野心的反映。約瑟的夢說明雅各不但牧養牛羊，也像他父親以撒一樣務農（創26:12）。以撒的祝福也曾反映這種活動（創27:28）。

1.zh:
雅各住在迦南地，就是他父親寄居的地。

這句話引出了以撒去世以後的時代。雅各繼承了先祖的福氣與應許。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–36節）**。《先祖與先知》208-214:《救贖的故事》100-101。
1.en: **Jacob dwelt in the land.** This statement introduces the period after Isaac’s death. Jacob was now heir to the blessings and promises that accompanied the patriarchal succession.

2.zh:
雅各的記略如下。約瑟十七歲與他哥哥們一同牧羊。他是個童子，與他父親的妾闢拉、悉帕的兒子們常在一處。約瑟將他哥哥們的惡行報給他們的父親。

**雅各的記略。**這裡開始了一個新的階段（見創5:1；6:9等）。雖然這個標題只提雅各的名字，但正如隨後幾章所顯示的，這顯然是指其家族的歷史。在他的有生之年，他家族成員的任何經歷都是其家族記錄的一部分。
**約瑟十七歲。**接下來所要描述的事件發生在雅各從哈蘭回來大約十一年以後。那時他已有108歲了（見創30:25和創27:1註釋）。
**與闢拉……的兒子們常在一處。**約瑟與闢拉和悉帕的兒子們比較親密，因為他們的年齡與他的年齡比較接近，而且他們可能沒有利亞的兒子們那麼傲慢。闢拉曾是他母親拉結的使女，很可能是在拉結死後照看約瑟。
**他們的惡行報給。**約瑟既報告了自己所看到的，也轉述了他所聽到有關他兄弟的事。他的兄弟開始憎恨他。約瑟心懷高尚的理想，對兄弟的惡行十分反感。他向雅各報告這些事情，肯定以為他父親的影響會使他們改變做法，免得家族的名聲受到羞辱，就像當年對示劍人的屠殺那樣。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》30。
2.en:
**The generations of Jacob.** Here opens a new section (see chs. 5:1; 6:9; etc.). Although the name of Jacob alone is mentioned in this title, the history of his family is clearly implied, as the following chapters show. During his lifetime whatever experiences came to members of his family are considered part of his family record.
**Joseph, being seventeen.** The events about to be described took place some 11 years after Jacob’s return from Haran, when he had reached the age of 108 years (see ch. 30:25 and on ch. 27:1).
**With the sons of Bilhah.** Joseph was more closely associated with the sons of Bilhah and Zilphah, who stood nearer to him in age, and who were perhaps less haughty than those of Leah. It may be that Bilhah, who had been his mother Rachel’s maid, cared for Joseph after Rachel’s death.
**Their evil report.** Joseph either reported what he had observed personally or repeated what he had heard about his brothers. This marks the beginning of the bitter hatred that his brothers felt toward him. Joseph was actuated by high ideals, and his sensitive conscience rebelled against the evil deeds of his brothers. His report of these things to Jacob was doubtless with the thought that his father’s influence might lead them to change their ways, lest dishonor come to the family name as it had in the massacre of the Shechemites.

3.zh:
以色列原來愛約瑟過於愛他的眾子，因為約瑟是他年老生的；他給約瑟做了一件綵衣。

雅各特別喜歡約瑟陪伴。他的和善與想法與兄弟們迥然不同。約瑟出生時雅各已經91歲了，過了幾年便雅憫才出生，所以他將約瑟視為“他年老生的”。
**一件綵衣。**雅各偏愛約瑟最招人注目的做法，就是給他做了一件特殊的外衣。“彩”字（passim）原意不明。該詞在撒下13:18,19中用來描述大衛王的女兒他瑪的衣服。希臘文七十士譯本、拉丁文通行本和敘利亞文譯本都譯為“彩色的”，成了大多數現代聖經譯本的依據。埃及貝尼哈桑一個貴族的墳墓中有一幅亞伯拉罕時代的壁畫，描繪了一群亞細亞族的男女老少，其中一些人只圍著雙色的纏腰帶，有些人身穿過膝的束腰外袍，但裸露著一個肩膀。這些衣袍有些是純白色的，其他的則帶有蘭色和紅色的圖案。酋長的外衣色彩特別美麗，其精美的圖案是與眾不同的。雅各給約瑟的可能就是這樣的外袍。passim一詞起源不詳，很有可能是pas（四肢）的複數形式。如果真是這樣的話，那就是指手和腳。在但5:5,24節中，pas一詞被譯為“指頭”。所以約瑟的外衣應是一件長袖的，一直垂到腳的衣服。這樣的衣服不適勞動的時穿，是貴族孩子的衣服。英文RSV版譯為“帶袖的長袍”。希伯來語的語法結構暗示雅各不僅為約瑟做了一件這樣的外衣，而且“常常為他做”。不管是哪種情況，這件外衣都會使人懷疑雅各想越過大的兒子們而將長子的名分授予約瑟。難怪他的兄弟都恨他（《祖》209頁）！
3.en:
**Israel loved Joseph.** Jacob found particular satisfaction in the companionship of Joseph, whose amiability and ideals made him so different from his brothers. Since Jacob had been 91 years old at the birth of Joseph, and Benjamin was not born till a number of years later, he considered Joseph “the son of his old age.”
**A coat of many colours.** Jacob’s preferential treatment of Joseph reached a climax in the special coat, or tunic, he made for him. The meaning of the word passim, “of many colors,” is uncertain. It is used also in 2 Sam. 13:18, 19 to describe the dress of Tamar, the daughter of King David. The LXX, Vulgate, and Syriac rendering, “colorfully dyed,” forms the basis of the translation found in most modern Bibles. A painting on the wall of a nobleman’s tomb at Beni Hasan in Egypt, dating from the time of Abraham, depicts a group of Asiatic men, women, and children, of whom some wore nothing but two-colored loincloths, and some, tunics that reached to the knee but left one shoulder bare. Some of these were of plain white material, but others had blue and red designs. The chief’s garment was especially colorful, and is distinguished from the others by a beautiful design woven into the fabric. The tunic Jacob gave to Joseph may have resembled this one. As pointed out here, however, the word passim is of uncertain origin. If, as seems probable, it is the plural of pas, “extremity,” it would refer to the hands and the feet. In Dan. 5:5, 24, pas is the word translated “part.” Accordingly, then, Joseph’s coat, or tunic, would be one with long sleeves, and one which also reached to his feet. Such a garment would not be suitable to wear while working, and was, furthermore, the kind worn by children of noble rank. The RSV reads, “a long robe with sleeves.” The Hebrew grammatical construction suggests the idea that Jacob not only made one such coat for Joseph but “used to make” them for him. In either case this coat excited the suspicion that Jacob intended to pass by this older children and bestow the birthright upon Joseph. Little wonder that his brothers all hated him (PP 209)!

4.zh:
約瑟的哥哥們見父親愛約瑟過於愛他們，就恨約瑟，不與他說和睦的話。

雅各對約瑟的寵愛是很自然的，因為他不僅是他所愛的拉結所生，而且品格出眾，與他其他兒子的敗壞生活形成了鮮明的對比。許多象雅各那樣偏愛一個孩子勝過另一個孩子的父母，雖然在他們內心深處感到這種偏愛是完全有理的，但至少在表面上會盡量掩飾這種偏愛。雅各卻給了拉結的兒子一件昂貴奢華的外衣，明顯地表現出對他的偏心。這種偏愛的標誌果然引起其他的兒子的嫉恨。如果約瑟沒有良好的品格根基，這樣做對他本人也是有害的。
4.en: **They hated him.** Jacob’s fondness for Joseph was natural, perhaps, since he saw in him not only the child of his beloved Rachel but also an excellence of character which stood in marked contrast to the notorious lives of some of his other sons. Many parents who find themselves in Jacob’s position, drawn to one child more than to another, at least put forth the effort to conceal the preference, which in their inmost hearts they probably feel is wholly justified. But with inordinate and obvious partiality, Jacob made evident his preference for Rachel’s son by presenting him with an expensive and princely garment. As expected, such a mark of esteem was distasteful to his other sons and, had it not been for Joseph’s fundamentally sound character, might have been injurious to Joseph himself.

8.zh:
他的哥哥們回答說：難道你真要作我們的王嗎？難道你真要管轄我們嗎？他們就因為他的夢和他的話越發恨他。

**懷愛倫註釋（8–10節）**。《先祖與先知》210。

12.zh:
約瑟的哥哥們往示劍去放他們父親的羊。

雅各的眾子似乎每年都要進行長途遷徙，從一個草場轉到另一個草場，正如今日的情況那樣。示劍位於希伯侖以北約96公里的地方，而多坍（第17節）則在示劍西北26公里以外。使用北方草場說明當時正是夏季或初秋。旱季從四月開始，一直持續到十月（見第24節）。在示劍放牧的原因可能是因為雅各家擁有當地的部分土地，有些是買來的（創33:19），有些可能是征戰獲得的（創34:27）。雅各的眾子似乎感到無須畏懼周圍的居民（創35:5）。這些人從未因他們對示劍人的屠殺而進行報復。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–18節）**。《先祖與先知》210。
12.en: **His brethren went.** The sons of Jacob seem to have made rather long annual migrations from one pastureland to another, as is often necessary even today. Shechem lies 60 road mi. north of Hebron, and Dothan (v. 17) another 16 mi. to the northwest of Shechem. Use of the northern pasturelands implies that the season was summer or early fall. The dry season began in April and lasted till October (see v. 24). The reason for pasturing the flocks at Shechem may have been the fact that Jacob’s family owned property there, secured partly by purchase (ch. 33:19) and perhaps partly by conquest (ch. 34:27). Jacob’s sons seem to have felt that they had nothing to fear from the surrounding population (ch. 35:5), who had never taken revenge for their massacre of the Shechemites.

13.zh:
以色列對約瑟說：你哥哥們不是在示劍放羊嗎？你來，我要打發你往他們那裡去。約瑟說：我在這裡。

雅各顯然不知道他的兒子們對約瑟有多麼仇恨，因為他們沒有讓他發現。所以他打發約瑟單獨一人去看望他們。後來他們向他報告約瑟失蹤的事時，他也根本沒有懷疑是他們乾的。雅各所牽掛的是其眾子長期未歸，擔心示劍人的同胞會報復他們的屠殺，或阻礙他們放牧牲畜。
13.en: **I will send thee unto them.** Jacob was apparently unaware of how keenly his sons hated Joseph, a fact they had been at pains to hide from him. This is evident not only from the fact that he sent Joseph alone to visit them but also from his reaction to their story of this disappearance. He seems never for a moment to have suspected foul play on their part. Jacob’s concern for his sons was probably due not alone to their long absence but also to fear that fellow countrymen of the Shechemites may have either taken revenge for the massacre or hindered them in the pasturing of their flocks.

17.zh:
那人說：他們已經走了，我聽見他們說要往多坍去。約瑟就去追趕他哥哥們，遇見他們在多坍。

多坍位於撒瑪利亞以北約20公里，朝斯德倫的方向，坐落在從北方前往埃及的商隊大道上。它位於一個長橢圓形的平原之上，擁有迦南最好的牧場之一，因此被雅各的眾子選中。它至今仍沿用古代的名稱多坦（Dotan）。在以利沙的年代，這裡曾發生一個大神蹟（見王下6:13-19）。
17.en: **Let us go to Dothan.** Lying about 12 mi. north of Samaria, in the direction of Esdraelon, Dothan was situated on the great caravan road from the north to Egypt. It lay in an oblong plain containing one of the best grazing areas of Canaan, and was therefore well chosen by Jacob’s sons. It still bears its ancient name, Dôtân. In the time of Elisha it was the scene of a great miracle (see 2 Kings 6:13–19).

19.zh:
彼此說：你看！那做夢的來了。

**懷愛倫註釋（19–28節）**。《先祖與先知》211。

20.zh:
來吧！我們將他殺了，丟在一個坑裡，就說有惡獸把他吃了。我們且看他的夢將來怎麼樣。

他們曾屠殺整個城市的男丁，殺害一個人根本算不了什麼。他們心中滋長的仇恨，已經到了要殘害親兄弟的程度。他們遠離家園，不受約束。企圖拋屍的“坑”是一個巴勒斯坦常見的貯水池。他們打算向父親編造的故事是完全可信的，因為巴勒斯坦在公元前二千年時是十分荒涼的，獅子、熊和其他野獸四處遊蕩（見士14:5；撒上17:34）。
20.en: **Let us slay him.** To men who had slain the males of a whole city, the murder of a single individual could hardly seem a grievous sin. Hatred had developed in their hearts to the point that they were ready to kill their own brother in cold blood. They were far from home and its restraining influences. The “pit” into which they intended to cast his body was one of the cisterns common in Palestine. The story they proposed to tell their father would be entirely credible, for Palestine was a wild country during the second millennium .., and lions, bears, and other animals roamed at will (see Judges 14:5; 1 Sam. 17:34).

21.zh:
流便聽見了，要救他脫離他們的手，說：我們不可害他的性命；

流便自己雖然缺點很大（見創35:22），卻不像他兄弟們那樣心地剛硬。作為長子，他感到對他弟弟有特殊的責任，決定儘可能地將他從他們手中解救出來。即將成為兇手的兄弟們暫時聽從了流便的建議。流便儘管軟弱猶豫（創49:4），但他似乎是約瑟的兄弟中唯一沒有完全喪失兄弟情義的人。他雖然缺乏公開反對他們強烈意願的勇氣，卻至少懦弱地試圖搭救約瑟的性命。流便的計劃雖是值得讚許的，但沒有成功，因為他缺乏決心和警覺。
21.en: **Reuben heard it.** Though Reuben had been far from perfect himself (see ch. 35:22), his heart was not so hard as theirs. As the eldest son, he felt a special responsibility for his younger brother, and determined, if possible, to save him from them. The would-be murderers were content, for the moment, to follow Reuben’s suggestion. Weak and vacillating though he was (ch. 49:4), Reuben appears to have been the only one of Joseph’s brothers in whom the natural affection of a brother was not completely lost. Though he lacked the courage to resist openly their stronger wills, he at least made a timid attempt to save Joseph’s life. Reuben’s plan was commendable as far as it went, but it failed because of his lack of determination and vigilance.

24.zh:
把他丟在坑裡；那坑是空的，裡頭沒有水。

更有甚者，他們還剝去約瑟的衣服，把他丟在附近一個乾涸的貯水池中。貯水池似乎經常有這樣用的（見耶38:6）。讓他活活餓死顯然滿足了他們的報仇心，他們根本不理睬他可憐的哀求（創42:21,22）。
24.en: **Cast him into a pit.** Adding insult to injury, they stripped Joseph and threw him into a dry cistern nearby. It seems that cistern were often put to such a use (see Jer. 38:6). The thought that he would die a painful death by starvation apparently satisfied their vindictiveness, and they paid no heed to his piteous appeals (ch. 42:21, 22).

25.zh:
他們坐下吃飯，舉目觀看，見有一夥米甸的以實瑪利人從基列來，用駱駝馱著香料、乳香、沒藥，要帶下埃及去。

這些喪失天良的兄弟坐下吃飯時心中即使不是狂喜，也是帶著一種滿足感和麻木感。
**一夥米甸的以實瑪利人。**“一夥”就是一隊旅行者，特別是商隊。以實瑪利的後代阿拉伯人佔據了埃及東面的阿拉伯沙漠地區，並且朝亞述的方向向北擴張。聖經和其他文獻記載阿拉伯人與埃及人進行了積極的貿易。以實瑪利的一些後裔此時已經成為商人，這並不奇怪，因為現在離以實瑪利出生已有近180年了，他的家族一定已經有了迅速的發展。
**從基列來。**多坍位於貿易要道上，自然會有許多商隊不時經過。這條商道始於約但河東岸的基列，在以斯德倫谷東端的伯善附近穿越約但河，沿著該谷到詹寧，然後向南越過迦密山脈，經過多坍平原以後，繼續向南沿著拉姆勒和迦薩一直到埃及。
**香料。**有些學者認為“香料”是黃芪膠，它是從黃芪屬（Astragalus）灌木的樹液中提煉出來的。還有人認定它為一種植物的紅色乾花，或巖薔薇/石玫瑰的樹脂。不論“香料”或樹膠源於何物，都可能用作聖香或作化妝品的原料。
**乳香。**原文可能指乳香脂樹和篤耨香樹的樹膠。
**沒藥。**含義不明。一般認為它是一種從巖薔薇樹葉中提煉出來的芳香樹脂（labdanum），或者現今所說的沒藥。有些學者認為這是乳香脂樹含脂質的樹皮。
25.en:
**Sat down to eat.** Perhaps with a secret feeling of satisfaction, if not of exultation, and with infinite indifference, the heartless brothers sat down to eat.
**A company of Ishmeelites.** The word translated “company” in the KJV means a band of travelers, especially of merchants, and may therefore appropriately be translated “caravan.” The Arabs, descending from Ishmael, occupied the desert regions of Arabia east of Egypt and northward in the general direction of Assyria. Biblical and secular records reveal that the Arabs carried on a flourishing trade with Egypt. That some of Ishmael’s descendants had already become a trading people is not surprising, for it was now about 180 years since Ishmael’s birth, and his family had no doubt grown rapidly.
**From Gilead.** Inasmuch as Dothan lay on a major trade route, it was only natural that caravans should pass by from time to time. The route from Gilead in Transjordan crossed the Jordan in the neighborhood of Beth-shan, at the eastern end of the Esdraelon valley, followed the valley to Jenin, then turned south to cross the Carmel range. Passing through the plain of Dothan, it continued southward by way of Er Ramle and Gaza toward Egypt.
**Spicery.** The word translated “spicery” is understood by some to be tragacanth gum, which is obtained from bushes of the genus Astragalus. It has also been identified with the dried red blossoms of the naqawa plant, or the resin of the cistus, or rockrose. Whatever the origin of the “spicery,” or gum, it was probably used either as an ingredient of incense or as a cosmetic.
**Balm.** The Hebrew word translated “balm” probably refers to the gum of the mastic tree and the terebinth.
**Myrrh.** The meaning of the word thus translated is uncertain. It is usually understood to refer to labdanum, an aromatic gum exuded by the leaves of the cistus, or to what is known today as myrrh. Others think it to be the resinous bark of the mastic tree.

26.zh:
猶大對眾弟兄說：我們殺我們的兄弟，藏了他的血有什麼益處呢？

猶大把以實瑪利商隊的出現看作一個不用殺人就可以永遠清除約瑟的機會，使他不可能再競爭長子的名分。兄弟們無疑認為約瑟對家庭的財富毫無貢獻，沒有理由繼承他們勞動所得的財產。猶大的建議得到了兄弟們的一致同意。他們反思了自己起初的殺機，覺得有點不願親手加害約瑟了。
26.en: **Judah said.** Judah saw in the appearance of the Ishmaelite caravan a means for permanently disposing of Joseph without taking his life. This would effectively eliminate him from further competition in the contest for the birthright. The brothers reasoned, no doubt, that Joseph had done little to increase the family fortune, and they saw no reason why he should fall heir to the wealth their hands had produced. Judah’s proposal proved to be a most welcome one to all the brothers, who by now, after reflecting upon their original impulse to kill Joseph, found themselves somewhat reluctant to lay their own hands upon him.

28.zh:
有些米甸的商人從那裡經過，哥哥們就把約瑟從坑裡拉上來，講定二十舍客勒銀子，把約瑟賣給以實瑪利人。他們就把約瑟帶到埃及去了。

**商人。**在第25,27,28節中稱為“以實瑪利人”，在第28和36節中稱為“米甸人”。這個商隊可能是由兩群人組成的，或者這兩個名稱一般被用作同義詞。反正只有一個商隊參與了這次交易（見《祖》211頁）。
**二十舍客勒銀子。**約瑟二十塊或二十舍客勒銀子的售價要遠低於一個奴僕的平均價格。根據出21:32節，似乎應是三十舍客勒。也就是以實瑪利人在埃及出售約瑟時所希望得到的價格。他們當然會低價購買他。二十舍客勒大約是8盎司（228克）（見創20:16節註釋）。
約瑟的被賣公然地違犯了上帝的原則，即人無權強迫他人為奴（參利25:39-43）。這充分說明約瑟的兄弟道德敗壞的程度。出賣約瑟表明他們天良喪盡。約瑟的被賣是聖經中所記載的第一例奴隸交易。
奴隸販子所犯的罪，沒有約瑟兄弟的罪那麼殘忍，因為他們所賣的不僅是同胞，，而且是親兄弟。儘管如此，天意掌管了這些心地剛硬之人的邪惡企圖。商隊此時的出現是上帝用來拯救約瑟脫離他們害命的惡毒陰謀。這件事後來又反過來救了他們的性命（創45:4,5）。
儘管約瑟當時不知道，天意卻一直在引導他的腳步。人生最黑暗的道路往往會通向最光明的前途。不論上帝領我們到哪裡去，願我們都永遠樂意跟隨（見羅8:28,35-39）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五321。
28.en:
**Merchantmen.** The traders are called “Ishmeelites” in vs. 25, 27, and 28, and “Midianites” in vs. 28 and 36. This has been explained by assuming that both groups were represented in the caravan, or that the two names were used synonymously in common parlance. In either case, only one caravan was involved in the transaction (see PP 211).
**Twenty pieces of silver.** The price paid for Joseph, 20 pieces or shekels of silver, was much less than the average price of a slave. According to Ex. 21:32, this price seems to have been 30 shekels, in all probability the retail price of the Ishmaelites expected to receive for Joseph in Egypt. Naturally, they would pay less for him. Twenty shekels would be approximately 8 oz. (228 gr.) of silver (see on ch. 20:16).
The selling of Joseph was an overt violation of the principle that no man has the right to subject another to involuntary servitude (cf. Lev. 25:39–43). It demonstrates clearly the extent of moral perversion that had taken place in the hearts of Joseph’s brothers. Those who sold Joseph demonstrated thereby that they had utterly lost all natural affection. Joseph’s sale into slavery is the first recorded example in the Bible of such a transaction.
Slave dealers have imitated but seldom surpassed the cruelty of which Joseph’s brothers were guilty, for it was not simply a fellow creature they sold, but their own brother. Nevertheless, divine Providence overruled the evil designs of these calloushearted men. The coming of the caravan at this precise time was Heaven’s appointed means of saving Joseph from their malicious plot on his life, and the saving of his life became, in turn, the means by which their lives were saved (ch. 45:4, 5).
Though Joseph could not know at the time, Providence was guiding his footsteps. How often life’s darkest roads lead to its brightest prospects! Let us ever be willing to follow on wherever God may lead (see Rom. 8:28, 35–39).

29.zh:
流便回到坑邊，見約瑟不在坑裡，就撕裂衣服，

整個交易是在流便缺席不知情的情況下進行的。在說服了其兄弟同意將約瑟活著丟在坑中之後，他沒等約瑟來便離開了他們，免得他們察覺他想要將約瑟帶回到他父親那裡的意圖（《祖》211頁）。撕裂衣服是古代表示憂傷和悲哀的一種習俗（見創37:34；44:13；撒下13:31；王下18:37；伯1:20）。
**懷愛倫註釋（29–35節）**。《先祖與先知》212。
29.en: **Reuben returned.** The whole transaction took place in Reuben’s absence and without his knowledge. Having persuaded his brothers to consent to cast Joseph alive into a pit, he had left them before Joseph arrived, lest they should discern his intention to restore Joseph to his father (PP 211). The rending of one’s clothing was an ancient custom expressive of grief and sorrow (see Gen. 37:34; 44:13; 2 Sam. 13:31; 2 Kings 18:37; Job 1:20).

30.zh:
回到兄弟們那裡，說：童子沒有了。我往哪裡去才好呢？

流便無奈的呼喊表明他想要救約瑟。他作為長子不知道該如何向雅各交代約瑟的失蹤。
流便的意圖是值得讚許的，他的計劃也是周密的，但是他失敗了。有朝一日流便的兄弟們將被迫聽他對這一罪惡時刻及其醜惡行為的斥責（創42:22）。約瑟將會得到釋放，但不是藉著流便。他必須先通過苦難清除生活中的渣滓（參來2:10），然後才能享受上帝為他預定的尊榮。根據上帝的天意，冠冕之先必有十架。個人之所以遭遇苦難，是為了讓許多人受益，使上帝仁慈的旨意最終實現。
30.en:
**The child is not.** Reuben’s helpless outcry revealed his secret intention to save Joseph. Now he was at a loss to know how he, as the eldest, was to give an account to Jacob for the disappearance of Joseph.
Reuben’s intentions were commendable and his plan well laid; nevertheless he failed. Eventually, however, the day came when Reuben’s brothers were forced to listen to his vivid reproof for this evil hour and its hideous deed (ch. 42:22). Joseph was to be delivered, but not by Reuben. The dross must be purged from his life through suffering (cf. Heb. 2:10) ere he might enjoy the honor for which Heaven destined him. In the providence of God, the cross must often precede the crown, and affliction become the lot of individuals in order that many may benefit and that the gracious purpose of God may finally prevail.

31.zh:
他們宰了一隻公山羊，把約瑟的那件綵衣染了血，

流便悲痛不已，不知所措。但他那些殘忍狠毒的兄弟們卻沒有忘記想出一個辦法。他們顯然不敢親自實施他們的騙局，也沒有勇氣面對他們父親痛苦的首次爆發。因此他們另安排了一個人，可能是一個除了傳遞的信息以外一無所知的奴僕，讓他將那沾滿鮮血的外衣帶給住在希伯侖的雅各，這樣就不會暴露他們的秘密了。
**懷愛倫註釋（31–33節）**。《先祖與先知》238。
31.en: **They took Joseph’s coat.** Though Reuben was beside himself with grief and perplexity, his ruthless and unrelenting brothers were at no loss for a plan. Apparently, however, they had neither the brazen boldness to carry through their scheme in person nor the courage to witness their father’s first outburst of grief. Hence they arranged for another, probably a slave, who knew nothing more of the matter than what he was told, and so could not reveal their dark secret, to carry the bloody coat to Jacob in Hebron.

33.zh:
他認得，就說：這是我兒子的外衣。有惡獸把他吃了，約瑟被撕碎了！撕碎了！

雅各的兒子們不僅用血塗抹那外衣，而且肯定將它撕碎，使約瑟厄運的證據顯得更為逼真，並使他們的謊言更為可信。這件撕裂的外衣充分地證明了這個青年人突然遭遇的厄運。這個表現雅各對約瑟不智之偏愛的物品，現在成了父子二人不幸的象徵。
33.en: **Rent in pieces.** Jacob’s sons had not only besmeared the coat with blood but had also doubtless torn it to shreds to make the evidence of Joseph’s misfortune more vivid and their story more credible. All too eloquently the rent coat bore its mute testimony to the fate that had presumably overtaken the youth. The object that once symbolized Jacob’s unwise favoritism for Joseph now came to represent the undoing of both father and son.

34.zh:
雅各便撕裂衣服，腰間圍上麻布，為他兒子悲哀了多日。

雅各在確鑿的證據面前相信了約瑟的死訊，就按古代的習俗開始了正式的哀悼。他撕裂衣服，穿上哀悼者的通常穿戴的麻衣（撒下3:31；尼9:1；斯4:1）。這是一種用來製作麻袋的粗布。在創42:25節中，該詞譯為“口袋”。在極度憂傷的情況下，“麻布”是貼身而穿的（王上21:27）。
34.en: **Mourned for his son.** Convinced of Joseph’s death by the undeniable evidence presented, Jacob entered upon a period of mourning, according to the custom of ancient times. His ordinary garments rent, he dressed in sackcloth, the usual garb of mourners (2 Sam. 3:31; Neh. 9:1; Esther 4:1). This was a coarse, thick haircloth, of which corn sacks were also made. In Gen. 42:25 the same word is translated “sack.” In cases of extreme mental distress the “sackcloth” was worn next to the skin (1 Kings 21:27).

35.zh:
他的兒女都起來安慰他，他卻不肯受安慰，說：我必悲哀著下陰間，到我兒子那裡。約瑟的父親就為他哀哭。

當雅各為約瑟的哀哭超過了慣例，而且他極度的悲傷似乎又無法得到緩解時，他的兒子們便開始擔心起來了。於是無情的罪犯變成了溫和的安慰者，未遂的兇手們試圖平息他們殘酷地加在他們父親身上的悲傷。
雅各除了底拿以外顯然還有其他的女兒，除非這裡所指的是兒媳（參得1:11,12）。由於古希伯來語家庭關係的詞彙通常比現在籠統，所以我們往往不知道“兒子”、“女兒”究竟指什麼。但根據創46:7，這裡似乎是雅各親生的“女兒”。
**陰間。**（She`ol）是希伯來文特有的詞彙，在任何相關的閃族語中都找不到。該詞來源不詳，一直用來表示死人所去之處。
35.en:
**Rose up to comfort him.** When Jacob had mourned for Joseph longer than was customary, and his intense grief seemed unassuaged, his children became concerned. The callous criminals became tender comforters, and the would-be murderers sought to mollify the grief they had cruelly brought upon their father.
It is apparent that Jacob had other daughters besides Dinah, unless daughters-in-law- are meant here (cf. Ruth 1:11, 12). Since Hebrew terms designating family relationships are often used in a more general sense than is true today, it is often uncertain what the words “son,” “daughter,” etc., really mean. It seems clear from Gen. 46:7, however, that these were Jacob’s own “daughters.”
**The grave.** She’ol. This word is peculiar to Hebrew, is not found in any related Semitic language, and is of unknown origin. It is invariably used to designate the place to which the dead go.

36.zh:
米甸人帶約瑟到埃及，把他賣給法老的內臣─護衛長波提乏。

關於在這裡和第25,27,28節中的米甸人和以實瑪利人名稱的互換使用，見第28節註釋。
**波提乏。**這個名字雖然一直被埃及學家認為是很好的埃及人名，但直到1930年代才在紀念碑上被發現。它在埃及文中的拼法是P'a-di-p'a-Re`，含義是“銳[神]所給予者”，類似於希伯來人名以利拿單（`Elnathan，“上帝已給予”）和約拿單（Yonathan，“耶和華已給予”）。
**內臣。**希伯來原文是saris，其主要含義是“太監”。東方統治者用太監擔任許多重要的職務，特別是作為主管後宮的官長。有人認為波提乏已婚的事實證明saris不僅指嚴格意義上的“太監”。可能是這樣，但沒有證據，因為即使太監也可能結婚。
關於“法老”，見創12:15註釋。
**護衛長。**“護衛”的希伯來原文是tabbachim。以單數形式出現時，其含義為“屠夫”或“廚師”，象徵著一個宰殺、烹飪和上菜的人（見撒上9:23,24）。在這裡，該詞以複數形式出現，指劊子手。“護衛長”波提乏可能就是劊子手的首領，或者是法老的警衛。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》214。
36.en:
**The Midianites sold him.** On the interchangeable use of the terms “Midianites” and Ishmeelites here and in vs. 25, 27, and 28, see on v. 28.
**Unto Potiphar.** This name, though long recognized by Egyptologists to be a good Egyptian personal name, was not found until the 1930’s on the monuments, where it appears, in Egyptian, as P’a–di–p’a–Re‘. It means “the one whom [the god] Re‘ has given,” and is comparable to the Hebrew personal names ’Elnathan, “God has given,” and Yonathan, “Jehovah has given.”
**An officer of Pharaoh.** The Hebrew word translated “officer” is saris, meaning, first of all, “eunuch.” Oriental rulers made use of eunuchs in various important positions, especially as officers in charge of the royal harem. The fact that Potiphar was married has been taken as evidence that the term saris means more than “eunuch” would imply in the strict sense of the word. This may be true, but stands without proof, since even eunuchs may have been married.
Regarding the title “Pharaoh,” see on ch. 12:15.
**Captain of the guard.** The word translated “guard” is from the Hebrew ṭabbachim. In the singular it means “butcher” or “cook,” and signifies the one who slaughters, cooks, and serves the food (see 1 Sam. 9:23, 24). Here, in the plural, it refers to executioners. Potiphar, the “captain,” was probably chief of the executioners, or perhaps of the bodyguard of Pharaoh.

16.en:
**The Angel.** Here placed on an equality with God, “the Angel” could not possibly be a created being, but must be the “Angel of God,” meaning God manifested in the form of an angel (see Ex. 32:34; Isa. 63:9; 1 Cor. 10:4). To the more fully developed revelation of the writers of the NT, He is the “Word,” the “Shepherd,” and the “Redeemer,” Jesus Christ. Both Jacob and Job (Job 19:21) reveal acquaintance with this Divine One, who delivered them from ill, both temporal and spiritual, and who would complete His work of liberation by freeing them from the power of the grave. The Redeemer to whom Jacob and Job looked forward, and of whom both Moses and the prophets testified, was Christ Jesus (1 Cor. 10:4; Gal. 3:13; Titus 2:14; 1 Peter 1:18).
**Let my name.** By this Jacob meant that Ephraim and Manasseh were to be counted as Jacob’s sons. Thus they would become in a special sense recipients of the blessings promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
16.zh:
救贖我脫離一切患難的那使者，賜福與這兩個童子。願他們歸在我的名下和我祖亞伯拉罕、我父以撒的名下。又願他們在世界中生養眾多。

“那使者”在這裡與上帝同等，不可能是受造者，而是“上帝的使者”，即上帝以天使的形像顯現（見出32:34；賽63:9；林前10:4）。在新約作者更全面的啟示中，祂是“道”、“牧人”、“救主”和耶穌基督。雅各和約伯（伯19:21）都認識聖者。祂拯救他們脫離屬世和屬靈的疾病，以及陰間的權勢而完成其拯救的大工。雅各和約伯所期盼的、摩西和其他先知所見證的救贖主就是基督耶穌（林前10:4；加3:13；多2:14；彼前1:18）。
**歸在我的名下。**即以法蓮和瑪拿西將被算作雅各的兒子。從特殊的意義上來說，他們將成為應許亞伯拉罕、以撒、和雅各之福氣的承受者。

15.en: **He blessed Joseph.** By the imposition of hands Jacob transferred to Joseph, through his sons, the blessing he besought for them from God.
15.zh:
他就給約瑟祝福說：願我祖亞伯拉罕和我父以撒所事奉的神，就是一生牧養我直到今日的神，

雅各借著按手禮，通過約瑟的兒子，將他從上帝那裡為他們求來的福氣傳給了約瑟。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–16節）**。《教育論》147；《先祖與先知》234。

1.zh:
這事以後，有人告訴約瑟說：你的父親病了。他就帶著兩個兒子瑪拿西和以法蓮同去。

在約瑟上次的探訪中，雅各為自己的後事做了安排。此後不久，有人告訴約瑟，他的父親病重快死了。他立即帶著兩個兒子瑪拿西和以法蓮前去。他們的年齡在19至25歲之間（見第5節；創47:28；41:50；45:6）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–22節）**。《先祖與先知》234-235。
1.en: **Thy father is sick.** Not long after the visit of Joseph, at which Jacob made arrangements for his burial, Joseph was informed of his father’s final illness. He immediately went to him with his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, who were between 19 and 25 years of age (see v. 5; chs. 47:28; 41:50; 45:6).

2.zh:
有人告訴雅各說：請看，你兒子約瑟到你這裡來了。以色列就勉強在床上坐起來。

這裡的名字從雅各轉換到以色列和創45:27,28中的轉換一樣重要。年邁體衰的勇士雅各鼓足他剩餘的力量，要執行一項他作為以色列，上帝仁慈應許的傳承者所要完成的任務。
2.en: **And Israel.** The change of name from Jacob to Israel is significant here as it was in ch. 45:27, 28. Jacob, the human warrior enfeebled with age, gathered together his remaining strength for a task he was about to perform as Israel, bearer of the gracious promises of God.

3.zh:
雅各對約瑟說：全能的神曾在迦南地的路斯向我顯現，賜福與我，

作為下文的引言，雅各談到了他早年的經歷，特別是在他從巴旦亞蘭回來後上帝在路斯或伯特利的顯現（見創35:9-15）。使用“全能的上帝”這一聖名，追述上帝的顯現，以及雅各講述不同應許的順序，表明他不是指他在去哈蘭的路上所做的夢，而是指他回迦南後在同一地點所見到的異象。
3.en: **God Almighty appeared unto me.** By way of an introduction to what was to follow, Jacob related experiences of his earlier days, particularly the divine appearance at Luz, or Bethel, after his return from Padan-aram (see ch. 35:9–15). Use of the sacred name, “God Almighty,” the account of the appearance, and the sequence of the different promises related by Jacob show that he did not refer to his dream there on the way to Haran, but to the later vision at the same place after his return to Canaan.

5.zh:
我未到埃及見你之先，你在埃及地所生的以法蓮和瑪拿西這兩個兒子是我的，正如流便和西緬是我的一樣。

雅各將上帝在伯特利的應許解釋為上帝授權他收養約瑟的兒子，並給予他們親生兒子一樣的地位。因為上帝曾應許他後裔增多並得到迦南為業，所以他覺得讓以法蓮和瑪拿西與他親生的兒子一樣，各得一份所應許的產業乃是合情合理的。這樣，“約瑟”將享有雙份的產業。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》234。
5.en: **Ephraim and Manasseh.** Jacob interpreted God’s promise at Bethel as empowering him to adopt the sons of Joseph and give them the same status as his own children. Since God had promised the increase of his seed, and Canaan as their possession, he felt justified in granting to Ephraim and Manasseh each a share in the promised inheritance equal to that of his own sons. Thus “Joseph” would enjoy a double portion.

6.zh:
你在他們以後所生的就是你的，他們可以歸於他們弟兄的名下得產業。

這一特權僅限於約瑟的頭兩個兒子。約瑟其餘的兒子在聖經中沒有提到，但如果有的話，他們的後代後來也包括在以法蓮和瑪拿西支派中，正如雅各所預言的那樣。就產業的份額而言，雅各對這兩個兒子的收養使約瑟處於長子的地位。
6.en: **Which thou begettest after them.** This privilege was to be restricted to the first two sons of Joseph. Other sons of Joseph are not mentioned in Scripture, but if there were any, their descendants were later included in the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, as Jacob predicted. The adoption of his two elder sons placed Joseph in the position of the first-born, so far as the inheritance was concerned.

7.zh:
至於我，我從巴旦來的時候，拉結死在我眼前，在迦南地的路上，離以法他還有一段路程，我就把他葬在以法他的路上（以法他就是伯利恆）。

約瑟早已去世的母親，也因雅各收養他這兩個大兒子，而得到遲來的尊崇。所以雅各在這裡提到他心愛的拉結。他的話似乎表達了一種沒有說出來的願望：要是她能活著看到她的長子在當時世界上最偉大的帝國中被尊為首相，成為其父家的拯救者，那該多好啊。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》206。
7.en: **Rachel died by me.** Joseph’s mother, who had died so early, was also honored, posthumously, in the adoption of Joseph’s two elder sons. This accounts for the allusion made here by Jacob to his beloved Rachel. His words seem to express an unspoken wish that she might have lived to see her first-born son exalted to lordship over the world’s greatest empire of the time, and thereby in a position to become a savior to his father’s house.

8.zh:
以色列看見約瑟的兩個兒子，就說：這是誰？

可能是先祖視力的減退（見第10節），令他未能即時認出他的孫子。他開始不知道他們在場。這說明收養的舉動不是因看見少年人才心血來潮的，而是出於上帝的靈在他心中的感動。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–10節）**。《先祖與先知》234。
8.en: **Who are these?** The failing sight of the patriarch (see v. 10) was probably the reason why Jacob did not recognize his grandchildren sooner. The fact that he was not at first aware of their presence shows that the act of adoption was prompted, not by beholding the youths, but by the inward promptings of the Spirit of God.

10.zh:
以色列年紀老邁，眼睛昏花，不能看見。約瑟領他們到他跟前，他就和他們親嘴，抱著他們。

衰弱的先祖幾乎雙目失明瞭。他可能好幾年沒見以法蓮和瑪拿西了，所以當他們再次出現在他面前時，他竟沒能認出。
10.en: **The eyes of Israel.** The feeble patriarch, almost blind, may not have seen Ephraim and Manasseh for some years, so that he did not recognize them now that they were once more in his presence.

13.zh:
隨後，約瑟又拉著他們兩個，以法蓮在他的右手裡，對著以色列的左手，瑪拿西在他的左手裡，對著以色列的右手，領他們到以色列的跟前。

在他父親面前俯伏於地的約瑟，既可能是出於孝道，也可能是意識到他父親是在上帝的啟示之下說話，就把他的兩個兒子從以色列的兩膝之間領出來。以色列一直坐著將兩個孩子放在兩膝之間抱著他們。約瑟右手拉著次子以法蓮，左手拉著長子瑪拿西拉，使以法蓮面對雅各的左側，瑪拿西面對他的右側。
13.en: **Joseph took them both.** Joseph, who had prostrated himself before his father, either in filial reverence or in the realization that his father was speaking under inspiration, now took his two sons from between the knees of Israel, who had been sitting with the youths between his knees and embracing them. He took Ephraim, the younger, on his right hand, and Manasseh, the elder, on the left, so that Ephraim stood at Jacob’s left hand and Manasseh at his right.

14.zh:
以色列伸出右手來，按在以法蓮的頭上（以法蓮乃是次子），又剪搭過左手來，按在瑪拿西的頭上（瑪拿西原是長子）。

這是聖經第一次記載以按手作為祝福的標誌。該動作對於祝福本身雖不重要，卻是看不見之事實的合適象徵。所以成了傳授屬靈能力或恩賜的公認形式。這一形式在舊約時期中用於約書亞的就職禮上（民27:18,23；申34:9），正如在新約教會時代用於神職人員的按立儀式上（徒6:6；8:17；提前4:14；提後1:6）以及許多神蹟的施行過程中（可6:5；8:23,25；徒9:17；19:6；28:8）。
14.en: **His right hand.** This is the first Scriptural record of the imposition of hands being a symbol of blessing. Though not essential to the transmission of blessing, the act is not without an appropriate fitness as being a symbol of the invisible fact. Accordingly, it became the recognized mode of conveying spiritual powers, or gifts. This procedure was employed in the OT period for the dedication of Joshua (Num. 27:18, 23; Deut. 34:9), as in the time of the NT church for the ordination of officers (Acts 6:6; 8:17; 1 Tim. 4:14; 2 Tim. 1:6), and in the performance of many miracles (Mark 6:5; 8:23, 25; Acts 9:17; 19:6; 28:8).

18.zh:
約瑟對他父親說：我父，不是這樣。這本是長子，求你把右手按在他的頭上。

雅各向約瑟保證，長子瑪拿西也將成為一個大族，同時他強調以法蓮將更加強大，成為“多族”，原文為“完滿的多族”。這一祝福從士師的時代開始逐漸地應驗。以法蓮支派的規模和勢力急劇增長，以致在北方的十個支派中處於領導地位，其名稱獲得了與以色列同等的重要性（見賽7:2；何4:17；13:1等）。在摩西的時代，瑪拿西支派的人口比以法蓮的多兩萬（民26:34,37）。隨後的歷史證明這一應許乃是出自於上帝，雅各的祝福不是一位臨終祖父的一廂情願，而是實際給與具有確定預言意義和效力的祝福。
18.en: **Not so, my father.** Assuring Joseph that Manasseh, the elder of the two, would also become a great nation, Jacob stated emphatically, however, that Ephraim would become even greater, a “multitude of nations,” or, more literally, a “fullness of nations.” This blessing began to meet its fulfillment from the time of the judges onward, by which time the tribe of Ephraim had so increased in extent and power that it took the leadership among the northern ten tribes, and its name acquired equal importance with the name Israel (see Isa. 7:2; Hosea 4:17; 13:1; etc.). At the time of Moses, Manasseh numbered 20,000 more than Ephraim (Num. 26:34, 37). Subsequent history shows that this promise was from God, and that the blessing of Jacob was not merely the pious wish of a dying grandfather but the actual bestowal of a blessing of definite prophetic significance and force.

21.zh:
以色列又對約瑟說：我要死了，但神必與你們同在，領你們回到你們列祖之地。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》235。

22.zh:
並且我從前用弓用刀從亞摩利人手下奪的那塊地，我都賜給你，使你比眾弟兄多得一分。

“份”的原文shekem與示劍是同一個詞。雅各曾在示劍城附近買過一塊地（創33:18,19）。雅各的兩個兒子曾屠殺了那城的居民。Shekem的意思是“肩”或“脊”。約瑟後來被安葬在示劍（書24:32），在基督的時代仍有一塊靠近敘加或示劍的地被人們視為雅各分給他兒子約瑟的（約4:5），故雅各將一塊土地贈與約瑟時所說的話很可能是一語雙關。雅各所擁有的那塊地在示劍，可能是一個山脊，或者外貌象個肩頭，所以雅各稱之為shekem（“肩”或“脊”）。Shekem表示“份”的意思，唯一的依據就是聖經的古本。Shekem也可譯為“山坡”（英文RSV版）。
**用弓用刀。**這是唯一一處提到雅各征戰的舉動。其他提到雅各給約瑟那塊地的經文都說是買來的（創33:18,19；書24:32）。由於這些經文肯定指雅各所說用弓用刀征服的土地。他離開示劍地區以後（創35:4,5）亞摩利人一定奪走了雅各的財產。儘管他們因恐懼沒有進攻雅各為示劍人的報仇，但他們似乎奪走了雅各的地產，所以先祖在一段時期之後被迫以武力重新奪得他的財產。這種解釋似乎要比把雅各的話解釋為約書亞時代征服巴勒斯坦更為合理。
22.en:
**One portion above thy brethren.** The word translated “portion,” shekem, is the same as the name of the city of Shechem, in whose neighborhood Jacob had bought a piece of land (ch. 33:18, 19) and whose population two of Jacob’s sons had massacred. The word shekem means “shoulder” or “ridge.” Since Joseph was later buried at Shechem (Joshua 24:32), and there was a piece of land near Sychar, or Shechem, in the time of Christ which was still considered as that portion which Jacob had given to his son Joseph (John 4:5), it is very probable that this statement of Jacob, by which he presented a piece of land to Joseph, was a play on words. The piece of land that Jacob owned was at Shechem, and was perhaps a ridge or had the appearance of a shoulder, for which reason Jacob called it a shekem, a “shoulder” or “ridge.” The meaning “portion” for shekem is otherwise unattested, and is based entirely on the ancient versions. Shekem may appropriately be rendered “mountain slope” (RSV).
**With my sword and with my bow.** This is the only place reference is made to warlike acts on the part of Jacob. All other texts referring to the piece of land that Jacob gave to Joseph speak of it as purchased (Gen. 33:18, 19; Joshua 24:32). Since these texts must refer to the same piece of land that Jacob mentioned as having conquered with sword and bow, it must be that Jacob’s property had been taken away from him by the Amorites after he had left the Shechem region (Gen. 35:4, 5). Although the “terror of God” prevented them from attacking Jacob and avenging the massacre of the Shechemites, they seem to have taken Jacob’s estate, so that the patriarch was forced at some later time to rreconquer his property by force of arms. This explanation seems to be more reasonable than that of some commentators who wish to see in Jacob’s utterance a prophecy referring to the future conquest of Palestine in the time of Joshua.
ELLEN G. WHITE COMMENT 1-22PP 234-235 5 PP 234 7 PP 206 8-10PP 234 15, 16 Ed 147; PP 234 21 PP 235

29.en: **Fell on his neck.** The expression “presented himself,” generally used only of the appearance of God, here suggests the glory in which Joseph came to meet his father. This meeting brought the lives of both men to a climax. How earnestly they had yearned to see each other is a matter for the imagination, not for description. Their great love, each for the other, overflowing in the joy of their hearts, was poured out in tears, which could no longer be kept back. These were tears of joy, that came after many tears of bitterness shed during their long separation.
29.zh:
約瑟套車往歌珊去，迎接他父親以色列，及至見了面，就伏在父親的頸項，哭了許久。

“見了面”的說法原文通常只用於上帝的顯現，在這裡暗示約瑟迎見其父親時的榮耀。這次相會將兩人的人生都帶到了高潮。我們只能想象而無法用言語表達他們曾多麼熱切地渴望能夠相見。他們彼此的摯愛，洋溢於內心的喜樂中，通過抑制不住的淚水流淌出來。這是喜悅的淚花，是在他們長期分離的苦澀之後流出來的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五125。

1.zh:
以色列帶著一切所有的，起身來到別是巴，就獻祭給他父親以撒的神。

雅各安營在希伯侖可能已有多年了（創35:27；37:14）。這裡是他爺爺亞伯拉罕、父親以撒和家族其他成員的安葬地。雅各可能從這裡出發。在前往埃及的路上，雅各在迦南南部邊境的城市別是巴停了下來。亞伯拉罕（創21:33）和以撒（創26:25）曾在這裡向耶和華立祭壇。雅各經過這個神聖的地方，可能看到其父親祭壇的遺蹟。於是他停下來向那位如此恩待他的上帝獻祭。這可能是因為聽到有關約瑟的好消息而獻上的感恩祭。雅各也可能想求問上帝有關去埃及的行程，上帝給亞伯拉罕的異象曾提到在埃及的苦難（創15:13），故他對這次行程可能有不祥的預感。所以雅各肯定在這裡將自己和家人都交託在上帝的照顧。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–34節）**。《先祖與先知》232-233。
1.en: **Came to Beer-sheba.** Jacob’s camp had probably been at Hebron for many years (chs. 35:27; 37:14), the place where his grandfather Abraham and his father Isaac were buried, together with other members of the family. This was probably the place of departure. On his way to Egypt, Jacob halted at Beersheba, on the southern borders of Canaan, where Abraham (ch. 21:33) and Isaac (ch. 26:25) had erected altars to Jehovah. When Jacob passed this sacred place, and saw, possibly, the remains of his father’s altar, he stopped to offer sacrifices to God, who had dealt with him so graciously in the past. These sacrifices were probably thank offerings for the good tidings concerning Joseph. Jacob may also have desired to consult with God concerning his journey to Egypt, which may have occasioned gloomy forebodings in view of the scenes of affliction revealed to Abraham (ch. 15:13). It is certain that Jacob here commended himself and his family to the care of God.

2.zh:
夜間，神在異象中對以色列說：雅各！雅各！他說：我在這裡。

這顯然是多年來給雅各的第一個異象。先前的許多啟示都是在夜間主要以異夢的形式賜給他的（創28:12；31:11；32:30），這一次卻不是睡覺時的異夢，而是一個異象。
上帝稱他為雅各而不是以色列，可能是為了提醒他過去的為人，因為他已看到他自己先前的品格已清楚地反映在他眾兒子身上。他曾一度矇騙他的父親和哥哥；他的兒子們關於約瑟的事竟騙了他二十二年之久才真相大白。他無疑地多次希望他能在眾子身上看到更高尚的特性，但這隻能使他回想起自己多年所擁有的未悔改的品格。
2.en:
**God spake unto Israel.** This was apparently the first vision accorded Jacob for many years. Several of the previous revelations had come during the night, mostly in the form of dreams (chs. 28:12; 31:11; 32:30). This one is not called a dream, which would have come during sleep, but a vision.
**Jacob, Jacob.** That God called him Jacob instead of Israel may have been to remind him of what he had been, since he had seen his own former character clearly reflected in that of his sons. Once he had deceived his father and cheated his brother; his own sons had deceived him concerning Joseph for 22 years ere the truth came out. Many times he no doubt wished he might see nobler traits in his sons, only to think of the unregenerate character he himself had possessed for so many years. Route of Joseph and Kindred to Egypt

3.zh:
神說：我是神，就是你父親的神。你下埃及去不要害怕，因為我必使你在那裡成為大族。

上帝的勸勉表明雅各擔心去埃及可能是在做錯事。他渴望見到他失去已久的兒子約瑟，但他也想到亞伯拉罕去埃及的不良後果（創12:14-20），以及上帝曾在一次饑荒中禁止以撒到那裡去（創26:2）。先祖心裡所想的一個重大問題，是他的行程能否得到上帝的認可。現在上帝表示了認可，並給了他明確的應許。像以前出發去巴旦亞蘭時一樣，在前往埃及的路上雅各又一次得到保證，上帝將與他同去。上帝關於其後裔的應許依然有效，遷入埃及並不意味著永久放棄應許之地。
3.en: **Fear not.** This divine admonition reveals the fact that Jacob had feared he might be doing wrong in going to Egypt. He yearned to see Joseph, his long-lost son; but he also remembered the evil consequences of Abraham’s journey to Egypt (ch. 12:14–20), and that God had once forbidden Isaac to go there during a famine (ch. 26:2). Whether his journey would meet God’s approval may have been a serious question in the patriarch’s mind. Now God expressed approval of the journey and gave him reassuring promises. As formerly, when setting out for Padan-aram, so now in departing for Egypt, Jacob received the assurance that God would go with him, that the divine promise concerning his posterity was still valid, and that the move into Egypt would not mean the permanent abandonment of the Land of Promise.

4.zh:
我要和你同下埃及去，也必定帶你上來；約瑟必給你送終【原文作將手按在你的眼睛上】。

從狹義上說，這一應許在雅各本人身上應驗了，他的遺體後來被運回迦南安葬。而從廣義上說，雅各之後代在大約215年後出離埃及，完全地應驗了這一應許。
約瑟和以色列家族的人前往埃及的路線
（見創37—47章）
從別是巴到埃及有三條路線：
A．始於巴勒斯坦的大道，經過約但河東岸到亞喀巴，穿過沙漠到達蘇伊士和埃及。
B．始於加利利的海邊道路，經過米吉多、沙崙平原和非利士地。
C．途經希伯侖和別是巴的書珥路線。
1．雅各的眾子走的應是書珥路線。
2．在約瑟的時代，即第十二王朝時期（按照長紀年學），埃及的首都可能是伊思特維。
3．在（根據以公元前十五世紀作為出埃及的年代而推算出來的）希克索斯時期，約瑟時代的埃及可能還有一個首都，那就是阿瓦里斯。從希伯侖到埃及的路程很長，約有三四百公里。（關於出埃及的年代，見第188-195頁）
4.en: **Bring thee up again.** In a limited sense this promise was fulfilled to Jacob personally, when his body was returned to Canaan for interment, but fully in the exodus of Jacob’s descendants from Egypt some 215 years later.

6.zh:
他們又帶著迦南地所得的牲畜、貨財來到埃及。雅各和他的一切子孫都一同來了，

雅各被夜間異象中上帝的應許所鼓舞，帶著他的兒孫進入埃及。
許多註釋家注意到埃及本尼哈桑的一幅陵墓壁畫，作為雅各遷居埃及的對照。在敘述亞伯拉罕早先遷居埃及的時候曾提到這幅壁畫（見創12:10註釋）。它描繪了公元前十九世紀第十二王朝時，一批閃族人來到尼羅河谷的景象。這至少要比雅各移居埃及早兩個世紀，因此不可能作為本章事件同時代的參照物。儘管如此，此壁畫對於理解雅各的遷居仍是十分重要的，因為它表現了閃族男女攜帶用驢馱著的貨物和驢背上用柳條編成的筐子裡的孩子。該壁畫顯示了他們富有色彩的服飾，以及他們的外袍、鞋子、武器、甚至一種樂器（八弦里拉琴）的樣式（見本書160頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–7節）**。《救贖的故事》147。
6.en:
**All his seed.** Strengthened and encouraged by the divine promises again vouchsafed to him in the nightly vision, Jacob went into Egypt, accompanied by his children and grandchildren.
Many commentators have drawn attention to a tomb picture from Beni Hasan in Egypt, as a parallel to Jacob’s migration to Egypt. This picture, already described in connection with Abraham’s earlier journey to Egypt (see on ch. 12:10), depicts the arrival of Semites in the Nile valley in the 19th century .., at the time of the Twelfth Dynasty. This would be at least two centuries before Jacob’s journey to Egypt, and the picture therefore cannot be taken as a contemporary illustration of the event under discussion. It is, nevertheless, important to an understanding of Jacob’s migration, because it shows Semitic men and women with their goods loaded upon asses and their children in wicker baskets on the backs of asses. It shows their colorful dress, and the style of their garments, shoes, weapons, and even a musical instrument, a lyre (see p. 160).

8.zh:
來到埃及的以色列人名字記在下面。雅各和他的兒孫：雅各的長子是流便。

第一次出現以色列人的說法，說明了那將要成為大國的雅各家族的規模。他正是帶著上帝應許應驗的盼望進入埃及的。該名單不僅包括以色列的兒子，而且包括先祖本人以及約瑟和他的兩個兒子。這兩個兒子都是在雅各到埃及前出生的。
8.en: **The children of Israel.** First occurrence of this expression. The size of Jacob’s family, which was to grow into a great nation, is given here, in evident allusion to the fulfillment of the divine promise with which he went into Egypt. The list of names includes not merely the “sons of Israel” in the stricter sense, but also the patriarch himself, and Joseph, with his two sons, who were born before Jacob’s arrival in Egypt.

9.zh:
流便的兒子是哈諾、法路、希斯倫、迦米。

在流便的四個兒子中，最後兩個一定還只是他們母親懷中的嬰孩，因為流便第一次從埃及回來時只有兩個兒子（創42:37）。哈諾（“以諾”的變體）的意思是“獻身者”，這也是該隱之長子（創4:17）和先祖以諾的名字（創5:19）；法路的意思是“分開的”；希斯倫的意思是“圍牆”；迦米的意思是“葡萄整枝工”或“我的葡萄園”。
9.en: **The sons of Reuben.** Of the four sons of Reuben, the last two mentioned must have been mere babes in the arms of their mother, since Reuben had had only two sons at the time of his first return from Egypt (ch. 42:37). Their names mean: Hanoch (a variant of “Enoch”), the name also of Cain’s first-born (ch. 4:17), and of the patriarch Enoch (ch. 5:19), means “dedicated”; Phallu, “separated”; Hezron, “enclosure”; and Carmi, “vinedresser” or “my vineyard.”

10.zh:
西緬的兒子是耶母利、雅憫、阿轄、雅斤、瑣轄，還有迦南女子所生的掃羅。

耶母利的意思是“上帝的日子”；雅憫的意思是“右手”；阿轄的意思是“聯合的”；雅斤的意思是“他[上帝]建立”；瑣轄的意思就是“潔白”或“光明”；掃羅的意思就是“求來的”。
**迦南女子。**西緬的一個兒子被稱為“迦南女子所生的”，暗示雅各的眾子一般不從迦南人中娶妻。他們通常都是從美索不達米亞的父系親屬、以實瑪利、基土拉之子、或以掃的家族中娶妻的。似乎只有西緬和猶大（創38:2）娶了迦南女子為妻。
10.en:
**The sons of Simeon.** Jemuel means “day of God”; Jamin, “right hand”; Ohad, “united”; Jachin, “he [God] establishes”; Zohar, “whiteness” or “brilliance”; and Shaul, “asked for.”
**Canaanitish woman.** The reference to one of the sons of Simeon as “the son of a Canaanitish woman” implies that it was not the custom of the sons of Jacob to take wives from among the Canaanites. As a rule they were chosen from the paternal relatives in Mesopotamia, the families of Ishmael, the Keturah sons, or Esau. Only Simeon and Judah (ch. 38:2) seem to have had Canaanite wives.

11.zh:
利未的兒子是革順、哥轄、米拉利。

革順的意思是“驅逐”或“勒索”；哥轄的意思是“集會”；米拉利的意思就是“苦”。
11.en: **The sons of Levi.** Gershon means “expulsion” or “extortion”; Kohath, “assembly”; and Merari, “bitter.”

12.zh:
猶大的兒子是珥，俄南、示拉、法勒斯、謝拉；惟有珥與俄南死在迦南地。法勒斯的兒子是希斯倫、哈母勒。

關於法勒斯和謝拉的意思見創38:29,30註釋。死於迦南的珥和俄南未算在內。但法勒斯已經有了兩個兒子：希斯倫，意思是“圍牆”（見第9節），和哈母勒，意思是“蒙憐憫者”。
12.en: **The sons of Judah.** On the meaning of the names of Pharez and Zarah see on ch. 38:29, 30. Er and Onan, who died in the land of Canaan, are not counted, but Pharez already had two sons, Hezron, meaning “enclosure” (see v. 9), and Hamul, “one who has received mercy.”

13.zh:
以薩迦的兒子是陀拉、普瓦、約伯、伸崙。

陀拉的意思是“蠕蟲”或“猩紅色”，普瓦的意思是“口”。約伯似乎是雅述的縮寫（民26:24；代上7:1），意思是“轉動自己”，而伸侖的意思就是“守護”。
13.en: **The sons of Issachar.** Tola means “worm” or “scarlet,” and Phuvah, “mouth.” Job, which seems to stand for the unabbreviated form Jashub (Num. 26:24; 1 Chron. 7:1), means “turning oneself,” and Shimron, “watch.”

14.zh:
西布倫的兒子是西烈、以倫、雅利。

西烈的意思是“敬畏”；以倫的意思是“橡樹”；雅利的意思是“等候上帝”。
14.en: **The sons of Zebulun.** Sered means “fear”; Elon, “oak”; and Jahleel, “wait for God.”

15.zh:
這是利亞在巴旦亞蘭給雅各所生的兒子，還有女兒底拿。兒孫共三十三人。

**底拿。**由於她在示劍的不幸遭遇，顯然還沒有出嫁，因此這裡作為雅各家的一個單獨成員被提到。
**三十三人。**可能排除珥和俄南而包括雅各和底拿，也可能包括珥和俄南而排除雅各和底拿。利亞的六個兒子、二十三個（還活著的）孫子、兩個曾孫（法勒斯的兒子）和一個女兒加起來一共是三十二個人，再加上雅各就是三十三個人。
15.en:
**Dinah.** Apparently unmarried since her misfortune in Shechem, and therefore mentioned here as an independent member of Jacob’s family.
**Thirty and three.** This number is reached either by excluding Er and Onan and including Jacob and Dinah, as is most likely correct, or by including Er and Onan and excluding Jacob and Dinah. The 6 sons of Leah, 23 grandsons (who were still alive), 2 great-grandsons (sons of Pharez), and 1 daughter, add up to 32 persons, or with Jacob, 33.

16.zh:
迦得的兒子是洗非芸、哈基、書尼、以斯本、以利、亞羅底、亞列利。

洗非芸的意思是“指望”；哈基的意思是“喜慶的”；書尼的意思是“安靜”；以斯本的意思是“勞苦”；以利的意思是“護衛”；亞羅底的意思是“駝背的”；亞列利的意思是“上帝的獅子”。
16.en: **The sons of Gad.** Ziphion means “expectation”; Haggi, “festive”; Shuni, “quiet”; Ezbon, “toiling”; Eri, “guarding”; Arodi, “hunch-backed”; and Areli, “lion of God.”

17.zh:
亞設的兒子是音拿、亦施瓦、亦施韋、比利亞，還有他們的妹子西拉。比利亞的兒子是希別、瑪結。

音拿的含義不明。亦施瓦和亦施韋的意思相同，就是“他是平等的”，比利亞的意思是“恩賜”。他們的妹子西拉的意思是“豐富”。希別的意思是“朋友”或“同伴”，瑪結的意思是“上帝的王”。
在雅各的孫輩中，提到了51個孫子的名字，而只提到一個孫女，就是亞設的女兒。她被提到很可能是因為她象底拿一樣（第15節），還沒有出嫁。她也不象雅各其他的女兒和孫女那樣嫁到另一個家族。那些女子都隨他們的丈夫回他家了。
17.en:
**The sons of Asher.** The meaning of Jimnah is uncertain. Ishuah and Isui both have the same meaning, “he is equal,” and Beriah means “gift.” Their sister Serah’s name means “abundance.” Heber means “friend” or “fellow,” and Malchiel, “king of God.”
It is inconceivable that of Jacob’s grandchildren, of whom 51 grandsons are enumerated by name, only 1 girl should have been born, the daughter of Asher. She is probably mentioned because, like Dinah (v. 15), she remained unmarried. She had not gone over to another family, like the other daughters and granddaughters of Jacob, who had followed their husbands to their homes.

18.zh:
這是拉班給他女兒利亞的婢女悉帕從雅各所生的兒孫，共有十六人。

悉帕的兩個兒子、十一個孫子、一個孫女和兩個曾孫加起來一共是十六個人。
18.en: **Sixteen souls.** Zilpah’s 2 sons, her 11 grandsons, 1 granddaughter, and 2 great-grandsons make up the number 16.

21.zh:
便雅憫的兒子是比拉、比結、亞實別、基拉、乃幔、以希、羅實、母平、戶平、亞勒。

比拉的意思是“貪食的”，比結的意思是“公駱駝崽”。亞實別、基拉、母平、亞勒的含義不明。乃幔的意思是“愉快”；以希的意思是“我的弟兄”；羅實的意思是“頭”；戶平的意思是“覆蓋物”。
在民26:40便雅憫的家譜中，乃幔和亞勒被當作比拉的兒子，即便雅憫的孫子。一種合理的解釋是便雅憫的這兩個兒子，乃幔和亞勒，沒有生育後代就死了，而比拉又以他兩個已故兄弟的名字給他的兒子命名。這樣，他們不僅將獲得他們叔叔的名字，還將取得他們在支派中的地位，成為家族的首領。比結、基拉、羅實可能也因未生育便早年去世，而在民26章的名單中省略了。
21.en:
**The sons of Benjamin.** Belah means “devouring,” and Becher, “young male camel.” Ashbel, Gera, Muppim, and Ard are of uncertain meaning. Naaman means “pleasantness”; Ehi, “my brother”; Rosh, “head”; and Huppim, “coverings.”
In Benjamin’s genealogical list of Num. 26:40 Naaman and Ard are given as the sons of Bela, that is, the grandsons of Benjamin. A reasonable explanation is that the two sons of Benjamin, Naaman and Ard, died without offspring, and that Bela called his sons after the names of his two deceased brothers. In this way they would take not only their uncles’ names but also their position in the tribe, and become heads of families. The names of Becher, Gera, and Rosh may likewise have been omitted from the list in Num. 26 for the reason that they had died early without offspring.

22.zh:
這是拉結給雅各所生的兒孫，共有十四人。

拉結的兩個兒子和她的十二個孫子加起來一共十四個人。
22.en: **All the souls were fourteen.** Rachel’s 2 sons and her 12 grandsons make up the number of 14.

23.zh:
但的兒子是戶伸。

戶伸的含義不明。
23.en: **The sons of Dan.** Only one son of Dan is listed. The plural form “sons” is used as a stereotype phrase, whether one or several sons are named. Another example of this custom is v. 15, where the term “daughters” is used, although only one, Dinah, is mentioned. Hushim’s name is of uncertain meaning.

24.zh:
拿弗他利的兒子是雅薛、沽尼、耶色、示冷。

雅薛的意思是“上帝所分配的”，沽尼的含義不確定。耶色的意思是“形象”或“框架”，示冷的意思是“報償”。
24.en: **The sons of Naphtali.** Jahzeel means “allotted by God,” but Guni is of uncertain meaning. Jezer means “image” or “frame,” and Shillem, “recompense.”

25.zh:
這是拉班給他女兒拉結的婢女闢拉從雅各所生的兒孫，共有七人。

指闢拉的兩個兒子和五個孫子。
25.en: **All the souls were seven.** Bilhah’s two sons and five grandsons make up this number.

26.zh:
那與雅各同到埃及的，除了他兒婦之外，凡從他所生的，共有六十六人。

這一數字只包括移遷居埃及時還活著的雅各後代，不包括兒媳和已嫁的女兒及家人（如果這些人也和他一起下到埃及的話），因為他們已成為其他部族的成員了。六十六的數字是這樣組成的：
雅各的十一個兒子和一個未婚的女兒      12
流便的兒子                  4
西緬的兒子                  6
利未的兒子                  3
猶大的三個兒子和兩個孫子           5
以薩迦的兒子                 4
西布倫的兒子                 3
迦得的兒子                  7
亞設的四個兒子，一個女兒和兩個孫子      7
但的兒子                   1
拿弗他利的兒子                4
便雅憫的兒子                10
總人數：                  66
26.en:
**All the souls.** This figure includes only descendants of Jacob who were still living at the time of the migration to Egypt, but not his sons’ wives, or his married daughters and their families, if such came down with him to Egypt, since they had become members of other tribes. The number 66 is constituted of the following parts: Jacob’s 11 sons and 1 unmarried
daughter euben’s sons imeon’s sons evi’s sons udah’s 3 sons and 2 grandsons sachar’s sons ebulun’s sons Gad’s sons Asher’s 4 sons, 1 daughter, and 2 grandsons Dan’s son Naphtali’s sons enjamin’s sons
Total 66

27.zh:
還有約瑟在埃及所生的兩個兒子。雅各家來到埃及的共有七十人。

摩西在六十六個雅各的後代上又加上了雅各、約瑟、和他的兩個兒子，得出了雅各全家定居埃及的數字七十。司提反提到的總數是七十五人（徒7:14）而不是七十人，可能是由於他作為一個說希臘話的猶太人使用的是舊約的希臘譯本。該譯本經常在新約中被引用（見徒6:1註釋）。該譯本增加了五個其他（後來的）的後代（見第20,27節，希臘文七十士譯本）。
27.en: **Threescore and ten.** Moses adds Jacob, Joseph, and his 2 sons to the 66 descendants of Jacob, giving 70 as the total of Jacob’s family that settled in Egypt. Stephen’s total of 75 (Acts 7:14), instead of 70, is probably due to his being a Greek-speaking Jew who used the Greek OT version, often quoted in the NT (see on Acts 6:1). This version includes 5 other (later) descendants of Joseph (see vs. 20, 27, LXX).

28.zh:
雅各打發猶大先去見約瑟，請派人引路往歌珊去；於是他們來到歌珊地。

在記錄了雅各家的名單之後，就敘述他們到達埃及。猶大在上一次的埃及之行中表現出了卓越的領導才幹，因此自然被推為年邁先祖的代表，去傳報他的來到。他也將從約瑟那裡獲得有關定居地點的必要指示，然後回來率隊前往歌珊（見創45:10註釋）。猶大執行這一使命的事實，暗示著他已經被雅各選為長子名分的繼承人。便雅憫雖然為父所愛，但年輕而且缺乏經驗，正如後來的情況所證明的，他沒有領導的才幹。便雅憫只是一隻“狼”，而猶大卻是一頭“獅子”（創49:9,27）。
28.en: **He sent Judah before him.** The list of the house of Jacob is followed by an account of the arrival in Egypt. Judah, having shown remarkable qualities of leadership on their previous trip to Egypt, was naturally selected to represent the aged patriarch and announce his arrival. He would also obtain from Joseph necessary instructions as to the place of their settlement, and then return to guide the caravan to Goshen (see on ch. 45:10). The fact that Judah performed this task suggests that he had already been selected by Jacob as inheritor of the birthright. Benjamin, though beloved, was young and lacking in experience, and, as later circumstances proved, he lacked qualities of leadership. Benjamin was only a “wolf,” but Judah was a “lion” (ch. 49:9, 27).

30.zh:
以色列對約瑟說：我既得見你的面，知道你還在，就是死我也甘心。

雅各並不是想死，而是說他現在完全滿足了。他親眼看到了約瑟，確知他愛子的幸福，感到人生沒有比這更快樂的了。他心中最後一個屬世的願望已經完全得到滿足。無論何時，只要上帝看為合適，他都願意放下自己的生命。
30.en: **Now let me die.** Not that Jacob wished to die, but that he was now completely satisfied. Having seen Joseph with his own eyes, and knowing that his beloved son’s happiness was assured, he felt that life could offer him no greater joy. The last earthly longing of his heart was completely satisfied, and he was ready to lay down his life whenever and wherever God saw fit.

33.zh:
等法老召你們的時候，問你們說：你們以何事為業？

約瑟在迎接親人到埃及以後，首先要做的事情之一就是將父親和兄弟引見給國王。法老可能想委任他們當中一些人擔任官員，認為他們可能也會象約瑟一樣對他有用。但約瑟清楚地意識到埃及宮廷生活的誘惑，以及他兄弟的軟弱品格，惟恐他們會很快屈服於試探，忘記了他們將來在上帝計劃中的位置。所以約瑟強調，如果他們被問及自己的職業時應說是牧人，這樣就意味著他們不適於宮廷的生活。
33.en: **When Pharaoh shall call you.** One of the first things Joseph purposed to do, after welcoming his relatives to Egypt, was to introduce his father and brothers to the king. Pharaoh might have intended to appoint some of them as officers, thinking they might be as useful to him as Joseph. But Joseph, well aware of the allurements of Egyptian court life, and the weak characters of his brothers, feared that they might soon succumb to temptation and lose the vision of their future part in God’s plan. This way why Joseph emphasized that they should state, if asked, that their occupation was that of shepherds, so implying that they were unqualified for court life.

34.zh:
你們要說：你的僕人，從幼年直到如今，都以養牲畜為業，連我們的祖宗也都以此為業。這樣，你們可以住在歌珊地，因為凡牧羊的都被埃及人所厭惡。

歌珊在尼羅河三角洲的東部，很適合羊群和牛群。雖然離首都近（創45:10），卻可以與埃及人分開，過自己的生活，延續自己的文化，事奉他們自己的上帝而不至於得罪他人。另外，他們也離迦南近一些，在危急之時比較容易離開。約瑟在這裡顯示出他對自己民族命運的遠見。他顯然意識到他們遲早會離開。
**凡牧羊的，都被埃及人所厭惡。**很可能這不是約瑟的話，而是史學家摩西的話，為要解釋約瑟的建議和行動。如果他的兄弟們表示他們想繼續放牧的話，國王肯定會同意讓他們在歌珊定居。這將使他們與尼羅河谷以及大多數的埃及人隔開。摩西所說埃及人對牧人的態度被後來的希臘作者（希羅多德，第二卷第47,164章）和約瑟夫（《上古史》第二卷第7章第5節）所證實，也為以前的壁畫和浮雕的畫面所確證。牧人經常被描繪為可憐人，骯髒而不修剪髮須，赤身而處於半飢餓狀態，往往瘸腿或有其他殘疾。
34.en:
**The land of Goshen.** Goshen, in the eastern Delta region, was admirably suitable for flocks and herds. Though near the capital (ch. 45:10), it would isolate them from the Egyptians, and would permit them to live their own lives, continue their own culture, and serve their own God without offense to others. Furthermore, they would be comparatively near to Canaan, and could easily leave in a time of emergency. Joseph thus revealed insight into the destiny of his people, apparently realizing that the time would come when they would have to leave.
**Every shepherd is an abomination.** These are probably not the words of Joseph, but of Moses, the historian, given in explanation of Joseph’s advice and action. If his brothers should voice a desire to continue their occupation as shepherds, the king would most likely consent to their settling in the region of Goshen, which would isolate them from the valley of the Nile and most Egyptians. Moses’ evaluation of the Egyptian attitude toward shepherds is corroborated later by Greek writers (Herodotus, ii. 47, 164) and by Josephus (Antiquities ii. 7. 5), as earlier by pictorial representations in paintings and reliefs. Shepherds are frequently represented as miserable creatures, dirty and unshaven, naked and half starved, and often either lame or deformed.

19.en:
**For I know him.** Abraham could be trusted; he would not betray God. Happy tribute to the aging patriarch! The intelligent discharge of his divinely appointed task required that he share in a knowledge of God’s purposes. Abraham’s posterity must also understand, lest they share the fate of Sodom and Gomorrah. It was to be his duty to pass on to future generations what he knew of God’s dealings with the human race. God’s moral and ceremonial laws were also part of the sacred heritage he was to transmit to future generations. Abraham not only prayed with and before his family, but interceded for them as priest, a practice followed by other patriarchs and holy men of old (see Job 1:5). As a prophet he instructed his family in both the theory and the practice of religion, with emphasis on the practical virtues. He taught his family not only to know these things but to do them as well. A benevolent husband, father, and supervisor, he gave positive direction to the social and religious life of his vast family.
God could trust Abraham, for he would “command” his family, not by dictatorial methods, but by clear precept and consistent example. In training children, every word, look, and act has its effect. In many homes, there is little training by way of either instruction or example. Parents are held accountable for the sacred trust of children and should therefore combine firmness with love, as did Abraham. This task of training up children in the way they should go cannot be delegated to another, custodian or teacher, without grave danger of loss. The influence of godly teachers should not be expected to supplant, but rather to supplement, home training. Each has its place, and is incomplete without the help of the other to aid and reinforce it.
19.zh:
我眷顧他，為要叫他吩咐他的眾子和他的眷屬遵守我的道，秉公行義，使我所應許亞伯拉罕的話都成就了。

亞伯拉罕是值得信賴的，他不會背叛上帝。這是對這位逐漸年邁的先祖美好的稱讚。他需要了解上帝的旨意，才能聰明地履行上帝所指定的任務。亞伯拉罕的後裔也必須明白這一點，免得遭遇所多瑪與蛾摩拉的厄運。他有責任將他對上帝與人類交往的知識傳給後代。上帝的道德律和儀文律法也是他要傳予後代的神聖遺產之一。亞伯拉罕不僅在他的家人面前和他們一起祈禱，也像一位祭司一樣為他們代求。這個習俗被其他先祖和古代聖人所沿用的（見伯1:5）。作為一個先知，他向他的家人傳授了宗教的理論與實踐，特別強調實際的德行。他不僅教導他的家人知道這些事情，而且教導他們照著去行。作為一位仁慈的丈夫、父親和監督人，他給予其龐大家族的社會和宗教生活積極的引導。
上帝信任亞伯拉罕，因為他“吩咐”家人，不是用專制的方法，而是憑藉清楚的訓誡和言行一致的榜樣。在教育兒童方面，每一個字，每一個眼神，每一個動作都有其影響。在許多的家庭中，很少有憑藉言傳身教來進行教育的。父母應對上帝託付給他們的兒童負責，因此要象亞伯拉罕所那樣，將堅定和慈愛結合在一起。教養兒童所當行之路的任務是絕對不可委託他人的，不論是監護人還是老師，否則必招致重大的損失。家長不應期待以敬虔教師的影響來取代家庭的教育，這只是一種補充。兩者各有其功用，不可偏廢。如果沒有一方的幫助來協助和鞏固的話，任何一方的努力都是不完全的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》133；《復臨信徒的家庭》184，317；《安息日學訓言》50；《教育論》187；《基督教育原理》286；《服務真詮》390；《今日的生活》124；《先祖與先知》140，142，144，575；《論節制》290；《給傳道人的證言》342；《證言》卷一118，218，405；《證言》卷五214，424，494，499，547；《證言》卷七91，148，196，211；《證言》卷八189；《證言》卷九283。

6.en: **Make ready quickly.** Like a Bedouin sheik of the present day, Abraham directed his wife to take three “measures,” se’im (or about 20 qts.), of fine meal and bake cakes. The baking was done upon hot stones. The “butter” was curded milk, considered a delicacy in many Oriental lands even today. The menu listed in this and the next two verses provided a bountiful and satisfying meal. Abraham gave them the best he had.
6.zh:
亞伯拉罕急忙進帳棚見撒拉，說：你速速拿三細亞細麵調和做餅。

就像今日貝都因人的酋長那樣，亞伯拉罕吩咐他的妻子去取三“細亞”，se`im（約22升）的細面烙餅。餅是在熾熱的岩石上烙成的。“奶油”是凝乳狀的牛奶，至今仍在許多東方地區被視為佳餚。在本節和下面兩節經文中的食物構成了豐盛可口的一餐。亞伯拉罕將他最好的食物給了他們。

1.en:
**The Lord appeared unto him.** This must have occurred but a short time after the experience of ch. 17, since both events took place approximately one year prior to Isaac’s birth (see chs. 17:21; 18:10, 14). For the “plains of Mamre,” meaning the grove of Mamre near Hebron, see on ch. 13:18.
Throughout the narrative of the 18th chapter, note that whereas Moses consistently refers to Abraham’s divine visitor as “LORD” (KJV), Yahweh, “Jehovah,” Abraham always addresses Him as “Lord,” ’Adonai, “Sir” (see on v. 3).
**The heat of the day.** This expression probably designates noontime (see 1 Sam. 11:11), and the “cool of the day,” literally, the “wind” of the day (Gen. 3:8), refers to late afternoon or evening. The usual Hebrew term for noon is ṣohorayim (ch. 43:16), a dual form meaning literally, the time of “double,” that is, “greatest” light. A poetical expression refers to noon as, literally, “the height of the day” (Prov. 4:18), because the sun has then reached the zenith. We speak of “high noon.” Upon this occasion Abraham had perhaps dined and was resting, for upon the arrival of his visitors it was necessary to begin preparations for their entertainment.
1.zh:
耶和華在幔利橡樹那裡向亞伯拉罕顯現出來。那時正熱，亞伯拉罕坐在帳棚門口，

這件事一定是在創17的經歷稍後，因為這兩件事都是在以撒出生近一年前發生的（見創17:21；18:10,14）。“幔利橡樹”靠近希伯侖，見創13:18節註釋。
在整個第十八章的敘述中，注意摩西稱亞伯拉罕的神聖來訪者為“耶和華”（Yahweh），亞伯拉罕卻總是稱呼祂為“主”（`Adonai，見第3節註釋）。
**那時正熱。**可能是中午（見撒上11:11），而“天起了涼風”（創3:8）指的是傍晚或晚上。希伯來文一般用sohorayim來表示中午（創43:16），採用雙數形式，意思就是“雙倍”，即“最亮”的時候。對於中午的詩歌表達方式“日午”（箴4:18），直譯為“日之頂點”，因為此時太陽達到了天頂，就像我們常說“正午”一樣。在時亞伯拉罕可能已經吃過飯了，正在休息。因為客人來到時，他需要預備食物接待他們。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–33節）**。《先祖與先知》138-144。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–7節）**。《今日的生活》192。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–8節）**。《先祖與先知》138，《證言》卷六341。

17.en: **Shall I hide from Abraham?** Abraham is called in the Scriptures the friend of God (2 Chron. 20:7; Isa. 41:8). Since he stood so high in the divine favor and fellowship, God saw fit to impart to him a more intimate knowledge of His works and ways. Similarly, He has entrusted messages to the prophets, concerning whom He says that they stand in His counsel, or “secret” (Jer. 23:18–22; Amos 3:7). It is particularly with reference to acts of judgment upon the earth that the Lord speaks thus.
17.zh:
耶和華說：我所要做的事豈可瞞著亞伯拉罕呢？

聖經稱亞伯拉罕為上帝的朋友（代下20:7；賽41:8）。由於他與上帝有很深的交情，因此上帝認為可以多告訴他一些祂的作為和手段。祂也曾如此將信息交託給眾先知，說他們站在祂的會中，參與其“奧秘”（耶23:18-22；摩3:7）。特別有關耶和華在地上施行審判的信息。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》139。

3.en:
**My Lord.** That Abraham directed his invitation to one of the strangers has been taken by some expositors as an indication that he already recognized Jehovah as one of them. It is probable that one of the three excelled the others in appearance or that one stepped forward as spokesman for the group, with the result that Abraham directed his remarks to that one. It should be noted, furthermore, that the Hebrew word here translated “Lord” is not the sacred Yahweh, but ’adonai, equivalent, to “sir,” a respectful form of salutation.
**If now I have found favour.** This expression was frequently used by one person in talking to another of higher rank, or to one whom he desired particularly to honor. It does not imply that Abraham had recognized one of the men to be God. Laban thus addressed Jacob (ch. 30:27), Jacob, Esau (chs. 32:5; 33:8, 10, 15), Shechem, Jacob (ch. 34:11), the Egyptians, Joseph (ch. 47:25), and Jacob, Joseph (ch. 47:29). Many other examples show this to have been a common formula.
**Pass not away.** With typical Oriental charm and hospitality Abraham invited the strangers to pause long enough to refresh themselves. Abraham was apparently one of those who “entertained angels unawares” (Heb. 13:2). This experience shows that Abraham habitually practiced hospitality toward strangers. Although these persons were at first entirely unknown to him, his greeting was as respectful as if a messenger had arrived in advance to announce their identity and their intention of paying him a visit. Those who hold themselves in readiness to show kindness to strangers and travelers may unexpectedly be favored with the presence of guests in whose power it is to confer special blessing (see Luke 24:29).
3.zh:
說：我主，我若在你眼前蒙恩，求你不要離開僕人往前去。

**我主。**有些解經家將亞伯拉罕向其中的一位陌生人提出邀請，視為是他已經認出耶和華是其中之一的證據。很可能這三位當中的一位相貌出眾，或者其中的一位作為三者的代言人從中站了出來，以至亞伯拉罕向那一位說話。另外，值得注意的是這裡所說的主在希伯來原文中不是神聖的Yahweh，而是`Adonai，是一種致意的尊稱，相當於“先生”。
**我若在你眼前蒙恩。**這種表達方式常用於向上司或特別尊敬的人說話。這並不是說亞伯拉罕已經認出三人當中有一位是上帝。拉班對雅各（創30:27）、雅各對以掃（創32:5；33:8,10,15）、示劍對雅各（創34:11）、埃及人對約瑟（創47:25）、以及雅各對約瑟（創47:29）都曾這樣說過。許多其他的例子表明這是一種常用的表達方式。
**不要離開。**亞伯拉罕帶著典型的東方人的熱情與好客將這些陌生人請進家中，讓他們得到充分的休息。亞伯拉罕顯然是那些“不知不覺就接待了天使”（來13:2）之人中的一位。這件事表明亞伯拉罕慣於款待陌生人。儘管他最初完全不認識這些人，但他的問候是如此的恭敬，就像有人事先通告給他有關他們的身份和他們來探訪他的用意一般。那些隨時準備著要向陌生人和客旅表示友善的人，可能會在無意之中有幸接待那些將要憑其權柄而將特殊福氣授予他們的賓客（見路24:29）。

4.en: **Wash your feet.** Abraham first mentioned water to wash the feet of the tired travelers, a necessary aspect of hospitality in some Eastern countries to the present day. While they rested under a tree he would prepare a meal for them. After this they could depart in peace and continue their journey.
4.zh:
容我拿點水來，你們洗洗腳，在樹下歇息歇息。

亞伯拉罕首先提到要用水洗這些疲乏客旅的腳。這種做法至今仍在某些東方國家中作為好客的一種必要表現。當他們在樹下休息的時候，他會為他們去預備食物。然後他們可以平安地離去，繼續旅行。

18.en: **A great and mighty nation.** Referring to the first promises ever made to Abraham (ch. 12:2), God explains why it is fitting and proper to inform him as to the judgment about to be visited upon the cities of the plain. Theoretically, at least, all the land belonged to Abraham. If God, as senior partner to the covenant, proposed to take action affecting a certain part of it, Abraham as a proved and reliable junior partner should be informed thereof. It was essential, in fact, that Abraham should understand and approve of the action about to be taken, since it involved Lot and his family, some of whom were soon to lose their lives as a result.
18.zh:
亞伯拉罕必要成為強大的國；地上的萬國都必因他得福。

上帝提到祂原來向亞伯拉罕所發的應許（創12:2），解釋了為什麼要告訴他即將臨到平原諸城的審判。至少從理論上說，全地都屬於亞伯拉罕。如果上帝作為聖約中的主要一方要採取足以影響其部分地區的行動，祂理應告訴作為可靠的次要一方的亞伯拉罕。事實上，讓亞伯拉罕理解和認可即將發生的事件是非常重要的，因為這一行動將影響到羅得和他的全家。其中一些人不久就要喪失他們的性命。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》368。

8.en: **They did eat.** Abraham’s heavenly visitors actually ate the food he had prepared for them, as Christ in His risen and glorified form later did to prove the reality of His resurrection (Luke 24:21–43). The acceptance of Abraham’s hospitality on the part of Christ and the angels was perhaps to prove to Abraham that their visit to his tent at Mamre was not a dream or a vision but a genuine experience.
8.zh:
亞伯拉罕又取了奶油和奶，並預備好的牛犢來，擺在他們面前，自己在樹下站在旁邊，他們就吃了。

亞伯拉罕的天外來客真的吃了他為他們所預備的食物，正如基督在復活並得榮耀以後為要證明祂復活的真實性所做的那樣（路24:21-43）。基督和天使接受亞伯拉罕的熱情款待，可能是要向亞伯拉罕證明，他們對幔利帳棚的探訪並不是一個異夢或異象，而是一個真實的經歷。

2.en:
**Three men stood by him.** Thus opens the account of the Lord’s sixth appearance to Abraham (see on ch. 17:1). Some expositors have taken the three “men” to be the three persons of the Godhead. This view seems unwarranted, since two of the three are referred to as angels (Gen. 19:1, 15; Heb. 13:2), and as men (Gen. 19:10, 12, 16). It seems best, therefore, to see in the three “men” the Lord and two angels.
**When he saw them.** Abraham was not yet aware of their identity. He saw only three travel-weary strangers looking for rest and food. With true Oriental courtesy he ran toward them to offer the facilities of his home, bowing down before them in harmony with Eastern custom. This form of greeting in no way indicates that Abraham recognized Jehovah as one of the three. He did the same in the presence of his Hittite neighbors (ch. 23:7, 12). Similarly, Jacob bowed down before Esau (ch. 33:3), Joseph before his father (ch. 48:12), Solomon before his mother (1 Kings 2:19), and the sons of the prophets before Elisha (2 Kings 2:15).
2.zh:
舉目觀看，見有三個人在對面站著。他一見，就從帳棚門口跑去迎接他們，俯伏在地，

**見有三個人在對面站著。**耶和華第六次向亞伯拉罕顯現的記錄就是這樣開始了（見創17:1節註釋）。有些解經家將這三個“人”視為神格中的三個位格。這種觀點似乎是毫無依據的，因為三者中的兩位後來被稱為天使（創19:1,15；來13:2）和人（創19:10,12,16）。因此，這三個“人”最好被視為耶和華和兩個天使。
**他一見。**亞伯拉罕還沒有認出他們的身份。他只看到了三位旅途勞累的陌生人到這裡來尋求歇息與食物。他按照東方傳統的禮節向他們跑去，用他家中所有的來招待，並依照東方人的習俗在他們面前下拜。這一問候的形式絕不是說亞伯拉罕認出了耶和華是三位當中的一員。他在赫人鄰居面前也是如此行的（創23:7,12）。同樣，雅各也在以掃面前下拜（創33:3），約瑟在他的父親面前下拜（創48:12），所羅門在他的母親面前下拜（王上2:19），眾先知的兒子們也在以利沙面前下拜（王下2:15）。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–8節）**。《善惡之爭》631，。

9.zh:
他們問亞伯拉罕說：你妻子撒拉在哪裡？他說：在帳棚裡。

他們吃飯的時候，亞伯拉罕站著（第8節）等候。吃完了，他們便問起撒拉。這種詢問與東方的習俗是完全不符的。陌生人絕可能認識他人的妻子，或直呼其名。他們對她名字的瞭解可能使亞伯拉罕意識到他的來客不是凡人，而且他們的詢問暗示著他們的來訪與她有關。接著的對話表明了他們的身份。通過重申應許，亞伯拉罕確認這就是曾經五次向他顯現的上帝。這是撒拉第一次親身見證了她丈夫所說上帝顯現。亞伯拉罕已經知道並且相信了（羅4:19,20）。從這些事實以及創18:9-15節的記載來看，這次來訪是為了預備撒拉經受她一生中最重要的經歷而安排的，就是她頭生的也是獨生兒子的降生。
9.en: **Where is Sarah?** Abraham stood (v. 8), and waited upon them while they ate. Having eaten, they asked for Sarah. Such a request was decidedly out of keeping with Oriental custom; strangers should neither know nor use a wife’s given name. Their knowledge of her name probably suggested to Abraham that his guests were more than men, and their request implied that their visit had to do with her. The ensuing conversation made their identity clear, and from the promise now repeated, Abraham certainly recognized the One who had appeared to him five times previously. This was the first occasion on which Sarah had personally witnessed one of the divine manifestations accorded her husband. Abraham already knew and believed (Rom. 4:19, 20). From these facts, and from Gen. 18:9–15, it appears that this visit was designed to prepare Sarah for the supreme experience of her life—the birth of her first and only son.

10.zh:
三人中有一位說：到明年這時候，我必要回到你這裡；你的妻子撒拉必生一個兒子。撒拉在那人後邊的帳棚門口也聽見了這話。

這可能是指一年，正如羅9:9節所示。希臘文七十士譯本也是如此翻譯的。也可以是指懷孕的正常週期──九個月。不論是哪種意思，都是說到時撒拉要生一個兒子。
撒拉正站在帳棚的幔子後面，正如阿拉伯婦女從古至今的習俗那樣。貝都因婦女至今仍不能隨意地和男人交往，其中包括男性客人，特別是生人。儘管如此，她們卻對他們的交談有著極其濃厚的興趣。因此，她們經常躲在帳棚口附近有遮掩的地方。她們雖然不會被人看見，卻能聽見客人所說的一切話語並能嚴密地觀察他們。提及她的名字的一定使她和亞伯拉罕一樣大吃一驚。當她聽到自己將有一個兒子時，她必定懷著極大的興趣凝神傾聽。
10.en:
**The time of life.** This may indicate a year, as implied by Rom. 9:9 and so rendered in the LXX, or it may perhaps refer to the normal period of pregnancy, nine months. In either case, Sarah was to give birth to a son by that time.
**Sarah heard it.** Sarah was standing behind the tent curtains, as has been the custom of Arab women since ancient times. Forbidden to mingle freely with menfolk, including male guests, especially if they are strangers, but nevertheless intensely interested in their conversations, Bedouin women, now as then, are usually to be found close to the opening of the tent but just out of view. Although they themselves cannot be seen, they usually hear everything spoken by visitors and observe them closely. The mention of her name must have surprised Sarah as well as Abraham. With what intense fascination and rapt attention she must have followed the announcement that she was to have a son.

11.zh:
亞伯拉罕和撒拉年紀老邁，撒拉的月經已斷絕了。

就像前一次啟示時的亞伯拉罕一樣，撒拉現在也無法相信上帝的應許真地會實現。在過去的二十五年裡，她不斷地聽到這個應許的重申，她覺得她的年齡已經超過了使她信靠的限度。亞伯拉罕的每一個異象似乎都落了空。前一次的啟示（創17）使亞伯拉罕的疑惑變為信心。這一次，他沒有表現出任何的疑惑，正如保羅所明確指出的（見羅4:19,20）。
11.en: **Abraham and Sarah were old.** Like Abraham at the previous revelation, Sarah could not now believe that the promise made would ever come true. For 25 years she had heard it reiterated, but to her the days had been prolonged beyond credibility, and each of Abraham’s visions in turn had apparently failed. As a result of the previous revelation (ch. 17) Abraham’s doubt had been turned to faith, and on this occasion there is no evidence of doubt on his part, as Paul pointedly observes (see Rom. 4:19, 20).

12.zh:
撒拉心裡暗笑，說：我既已衰敗，我主也老邁，豈能有這喜事呢？

在前一次啟示時，亞伯拉罕笑了（見創17:17節註釋）。現在撒拉也笑了，可能是對自己命運的苦笑，或是對局面轉變的懷疑。帶著一種半挖苦半愁悶的笑，她所表達的意思就是:“哪有這麼好的事啊！”（見結12:22-28）。
**我主。**撒拉雖然有明顯的缺點，但她對亞伯拉罕的尊重和順服卻是值得稱道的。即使是跟自己說話，她也稱他為“我主”。所以新約稱讚她是基督徒妻子美德的典範（彼前3:6）。
12.en:
**Sarah laughed.** On the occasion of the previous divine revelation Abraham had laughed (see on ch. 17:17). Now Sarah laughed, probably expressing bitterness at her lot and incredulity that circumstances should ever be otherwise. By a half-sarcastic, half-wistful laugh she gave expression to the thought, “That is too good to be true!” (see Eze. 12:22–28).
**My Lord.** In contrast to Sarah’s obvious faults, her deferential submission to Abraham is praiseworthy. Even when talking to herself she referred to him as “my lord,” for which the NT commends her as an example of Christian wifely virtue (1 Peter 3:6).

14.zh:
耶和華豈有難成的事嗎？到了日期，明年這時候，我必回到你這裡，撒拉必生一個兒子。

耶和華現在公開了自己的身份。值得一提的是，上帝的這次顯現雖然很可能主要是為了撒拉而不是為亞伯拉罕，因為他已經瞭解並且相信了，但撒拉若不先開口，祂就不直接同她說話。祂沒有與撒拉說話，而是問亞伯拉罕:難道耶和華還會有什麼難成的事嗎。上帝如此說是為了糾正撒拉的不信並堅固她的信心。當人的智慧和力量不能達到的時候，當生命力衰退、缺乏作為的能力時，上帝仍具有完全的支配權，能使事情按照祂自己神聖旨意的計劃發生。事實上，祂經常允許人的境遇陷入僵局，以便使人的無能與祂的全能產生明顯的對比。
14.en: **Is any thing too hard?** The veil of anonymity was now thrown completely aside, and the speaker unmistakably identified Himself as the Lord. It is interesting to note that although this divine appearance was perhaps intended more for Sarah’s benefit than for Abraham’s, since he already knew and believed, the Lord did not address Sarah directly until she had first spoken to Him. Instead of speaking to Sarah, He asked Abraham whether anything could be too difficult for the Lord. It was primarily to correct Sarah’s unbelief and to strengthen her faith that God spoke thus. Where human wisdom and strength fail, and where nature, enfeebled, lacks ability to act, there God still has full sway and brings things to pass according to the counsels of His own divine will. In fact, He often permits circumstances to reach an impasse so that human impotence may stand forth in striking contrast to His omnipotence.

15.zh:
撒拉就害怕，不承認，說：我沒有笑。那位說：不然，你實在笑了。

撒拉的否認顯明她的笑和12節所說的話都是無聲的。就算是有聲的話，也是極其輕微的，她以為沒有人能聽得見。她此時直接與陌生人說話，既可能仍然躲在帳棚幔子的後面，也可能是從幔子後面走出來。她的否認一方面是怕得罪客人，另一方面也是怕暴露她心理的活動。突然的暴露感使她一時陷入慌亂之中，於是她想用撒謊的來躲避。
**你實在笑了。**就像對待伊甸園中的第一對犯錯者一樣，上帝用簡潔的話語嚴肅地指出她的否認與事實不符。撒拉接下來的沉默表明她承認了上帝的話，而她懷上以撒的事實說明她的悔改和得蒙寬恕。
15.en:
**Sarah denied.** Sarah’s denial shows that her laugh and remark of v. 12 were scarcely audible, if even that, and that she did not think either had been heard. Now she spoke directly to the strangers, either remaining behind the tent curtains or stepping out into the open. Fear of offending the guests and of having her secret feelings revealed led to denial. The sudden consciousness of detection forced her into a moment of confusion from which she sought escape by the route of falsehood.
**Thou didst laugh.** With terse directness resembling that with which He had addressed the first culprits in Eden, God solemnly and unequivocally declared her denial to be false. The subsequent silence of Sarah is evidence of conviction, whereas her eventual conception of Isaac implies repentance and forgiveness.

16.zh:
三人就從那裡起行，向所多瑪觀看，亞伯拉罕也與他們同行，要送他們一程。

三位天國的來客休息並吃喝了，便準備繼續他們的旅程。他們的目的地這時才首次提到。如果所多瑪等城邦坐落於構成現在的死海南部的平原的話（見創14:3節註釋），那麼它們距離希伯侖約有40公里──約有一整天的路程。由於亞伯拉罕的客人是在中午來到的，而且他們無疑地和他在一起花費了好幾個小時才走，所以他們離去的時間很可能是在傍晚。
**亞伯拉罕也與他們同行。**按照一種一直延續至新約時代的表達友情的古老習俗（羅15:24；林前16:11；徒20:38；約叄6），亞伯拉罕陪同他的客人一同走了一小段路。在東方國家中，當客人要離去時，主人仍有送客的習慣。送客的路程的長短標誌著主人向客人所表示尊敬的程度。根據古老的傳說，亞伯拉罕一直送到迦法巴錄卡，這是位於希伯侖向東至東北有七、八公里路程的一個山地。從這裡，人們便可以看到死海。亞伯拉罕可能正是在這裡和他的客人們一起觀望平原上繁榮的城邦的。
16.en:
**The men rose up.** Rested and refreshed, the three heavenly visitants were ready to continue their journey. Their destination is now mentioned for the first time. If Sodom and its sister cities were in the valley that now forms the southern part of the Dead Sea (see on ch. 14:3), they were about 25 mi. from Hebron—a good day’s journey.
