這是聖經中第一次提到“非利士地”。大多數現代註釋家認為這是一位後來的作者所犯的歷史性錯誤。因為他們聲稱非利士人是在公元前十三世紀末才進入巴勒斯坦的，比亞伯拉罕的時代晚了好幾百年。但我們沒有任何理由懷疑先祖時期非利士人在巴勒斯坦的存在。在北敘利亞沿海城市烏加列所發現的公元前十五世紀前的文獻中就曾提到了他們。埃及的史料約於公元前1200年首次提到非利士人的事實並不能證明他們在此之前沒有在這裡定居。這隻表明他們當時並沒有扮演一種重要的角色，正如他們後來在拉美西斯三世的時代所做的那樣。當時他們和其他的“海上民族”人數極其繁多，甚至曾一度對埃及的王權造成了威脅（見出13:17）。
32.en:
**Land of the Philistines.** The statement that Abimelech and Phichol “returned into the land of the Philistines” after concluding a treaty with Abraham at Beersheba implies that the area around this city was outside the recognized boundaries of Philistia. At the same time it was probably under the control of the prince of Gerar in Abraham’s time; otherwise it is unlikely that the question over ownership of the well would have arisen.
This is the first Biblical mention of the “land of the Philistines.” Most modern commentators have seen in this statement the historical mistake of a late author, claiming as they do that the Philistines did not enter Palestine prior to the late 13th century .., long after Abraham’s time. There is, however, no reason to doubt the presence of Philistines in Palestine during the patriarchal period. They are mentioned in documents of the north Syrian coastal city of Ugarit before the 15th century .. That Egyptian sources mention the Philistines about the year 1200 .. for the first time does not prove their nonsettlement of Palestine prior to that time. It shows only that they did not play so prominent a role as they did later in the time of Ramses III, when they and other “peoples of the sea” were so numerous as to threaten for a time to overrun Egypt (see Ex. 13:17).

33.zh:
亞伯拉罕在別是巴栽上一棵垂絲柳樹，又在那裡求告耶和華─永生神的名。

垂絲柳樹讓人們想到巴勒斯坦是拜偶像之地（申16:21；士6:26等）。這似乎暗示亞伯拉罕種樹是要獻給真神。該詞的類似形式存在於南阿拉伯語、埃及語、亞述語和亞蘭語之中，指一種檉柳，是類似於灌木的樹，生長在南地這樣的半乾旱地區。這種樹木生長緩慢，但壽命很長。亞伯拉罕栽種這棵檉柳的目的可能就是為了紀念有關那井的交易。今日，人們仍經常栽種紀念樹。
**在那裡求告耶和華的名。**亞伯拉罕在這裡像在其他地方一樣舉行公眾禮拜（見創12:7,8；13:4,18），崇拜的對像是“永生上帝”。不象異教的神祗，只是崇拜者所製造（何8:6）。亞伯拉罕所崇拜的是聖約的永恆見證者，伴隨他一生的永恆福源，和永不使祂的兒女失望的永活之父。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷八270。
33.en:
**Abraham planted a grove.** The word “grove,” reminiscent of the idolatrous cult places of Palestine (Deut. 16:21; Judges 6:26; etc.), seems to imply that Abraham planted a similar sacred grove which he dedicated to the true God. But the translation “grove,” from ’eshel, is erroneous. The word ’eshel, found in similar forms in southern Arabic, Egyptian, Assyrian, and Aramaic, denotes a variety of tamarisk, a shrublike tree native to semiarid regions like the Negeb. It is slow of growth but long of life. Abraham probably planted this particular tree for no other purpose than to serve as a memorial of the transaction concerning the well. Commemorative trees are often planted today.
**Called there on the name of the Lord.** As elsewhere, Abraham here conducted public worship (see Gen. 12:7, 8; 13:4, 18). The object of his worship was “the everlasting God,” literally, “the God of eternity,” in contrast to the heathen deities, which are but the creatures of those who worship them (Hosea 8:6) Abraham worshipped the everlasting Witness of treaties, the eternal Source of the blessings that attended him throughout life, and the immortal Father who never fails His children.

34.zh:
亞伯拉罕在非利士人的地寄居了多日。

這似乎與第32節所暗示的別是巴不屬於非利士相矛盾。顯然要麼非利士在靠沙漠的一面沒有固定的邊界，而別是巴可能歸亞比米勒所有，要麼別是巴位於非利士的邊界，亞伯拉罕必須經常越境來放牧他的畜群。
34.en: **Sojourned in the Philistines’ land.** This seems to contradict the implication of v. 32 that Beersheba did not belong to the land of Philistia. Apparently, either (1) Philistia had no fixed boundary on its desert side, and Beersheba may have been claimed by Abimelech, or (2) Beersheba was situated on the border of Philistia, and Abraham must often have pastured his flocks across the border.

1.zh:
撒拉享壽一百二十七歲，這是撒拉一生的歲數。

作為所有信徒的母親（賽51:2；彼前3:6），撒拉是唯一一位在聖經中提到其壽數的女性。她去世時以撒37歲（創17:1,17；21:5）。
1.en: **The life of Sarah.** As the mother of all believers (Isa. 51:2; 1 Peter 3:6) Sarah is the only woman whose age at death is mentioned in Scripture. Isaac was 37 years old at the time of her death (Gen. 17:1, 17; 21:5).

2.zh:
撒拉死在迦南地的基列亞巴，就是希伯崙。亞伯拉罕為他哀慟哭號。

**基列亞巴。**亞伯拉罕搬回了他原前在希伯侖附近的住處（創13:18；18:1）。他在非利士地居住了近四十年之後（創20:1；21:31-34；22:19），又回到了迦南的腹地。摩西特別提到這件事。基列亞巴（書14:15；15:13；21:11）的意思就是“亞巴的城”，是由一位名叫亞巴的亞納族巨人修建的。希伯侖這個名稱是後來賦予的。
**為撒拉哀慟哭號。**這似乎是亞伯拉罕所參加的唯一葬禮。這句話可能是指正式的哀悼，即坐在地上，並在死人面前哭號。哀悼後演變成一套複雜的儀式，包括撕裂衣服、剃頭、披麻和蒙灰（撒下3:31；伯1:20；2:12）。
2.en:
**Kirjath-arba.** Abraham had moved back to his former place of abode, near Hebron (chs. 13:18; 18:1). Having lived for almost 40 years in the land of the Philistines (chs. 20:1; 21:31–34; 22:19), he now returned to Canaan proper, a fact Moses specifically notes. Kirjath-arba (Joshua 14:15; 15:13; 21:11), meaning “city of Arba,” was named for one of the giant Anakim, who apparently founded it. The name Hebron was given to the city at a later time.
**Mourn for Sarah.** Seemingly the only burial rite observed by Abraham. This probably refers to formal mourning—sitting on the ground and weeping in the presence of the dead. Mourning later developed into an elaborate ritual, including such ceremonies as rending the garments, shaving the head, wearing sackcloth, and covering the head with dust and ashes (2 Sam. 3:31; Job 1:20; 2:12).

3.zh:
後來亞伯拉罕從死人面前起來，對赫人說：

當地的居民在這裡被稱為赫的子孫或赫人（第10節）。亞伯拉罕第一次在此居住的時候，希伯侖為亞摩利人佔據（見創20:1節註釋）。批判者不承認赫人這麼早的時就在巴勒斯坦南部出現。他們的這種觀點並沒有被最新的考古發現所證實。
事實上，我們只有根據赫人的法律才能最合理地解釋這個故事中的一些細節。（見第11,17節，以及《美國東方研究院公報》第129期中M·R·列曼所著的文章，第15-18頁）。
3.en:
**Spake unto the sons of Heth.** The inhabitants of the region are here called the sons of Heth, or Hittites (v. 10). During Abraham’s first period of residence the Amorites had been in possession of Hebron (see on ch. 20:1). Critical objection to the presence of Hittites in southern Palestine at this early period is not confirmed by the latest archeological findings.
In fact it is in the light of the Hittite laws that some details connected with this story can best be explained. (See vs. 11, 17, and M. R. Lehmann in Bulletin of the American Schools of Oriental Research, 129 [Feb., 1953], pp. 15-18.

4.zh:
我在你們中間是外人，是寄居的。求你們在這裡給我一塊地，我好埋葬我的死人，使他不在我眼前。

**我是外人。**亞伯拉罕與赫人，即“本地人”，打交道時所表現出來的謙恭值得我們注意（第7,12,13節）。他坦然地承認自己寄居者的身份，不要求對任何土地的所有權（見來11:13）。上帝曾應許將整個迦南都賜給他。他曾率領幾百名家裡生養的壯丁打敗了來自美索不達米亞的聯合遠征部隊（創14）。赫人公認他是一位“尊大的王子”（創23:6）。但亞伯拉罕懷著謙卑的心沒有向他的鄰舍提出任何要求，只是請求擁有一塊田地，不是憑著權利，而是作為一種情面並且付上價錢。
**一塊（墳）地。**這是聖經中第一次提到墳地。許多古代異教民族實行火化，希伯來人卻喜歡土葬。各時代、各種族和各種文化程度的人都喜歡埋葬在自己的土地上。
4.en:
**I am a stranger.** Abraham’s courteous approach to the Hittites, the “people of the land,” is noteworthy (vs. 7, 12, 13). He frankly admitted his status as a sojourner and made no claim to any of the land by right (see Heb. 11:13). God had promised him all of Canaan. With hundreds of retainers he had defeated the allied expeditionary force from Mesopotamia (Gen. 14). These very Hittites recognized him as a “mighty prince” (ch. 23:6). Yet, in humility, Abraham did not present his neighbors with a demand; he requested permission to secure title to a piece of land, not by right, but as a favor and for a price.
**A buryingplace.** This is the first grave mentioned in Scripture. Cremation was practiced by many pagan nations of antiquity, but the Hebrews preferred interment. The desire to be buried on one’s own land is common to people of all ages, races, and levels of culture.

6.zh:
我主請聽。你在我們中間是一位尊大的王子，只管在我們最好的墳地裡埋葬你的死人；我們沒有一人不容你在他的墳地裡埋葬你的死人。

**你是一位尊大的王子。**赫人禮貌地答覆了亞伯拉罕謙恭的請求。他們謝絕他把自己當作“外人”，而稱他為“尊大的王子”，原意是“上帝的王子”。同樣，希伯來文詩36:6節中“高山” 的原意是“上帝的山”；詩80:10節中“佳美的香柏樹”原意是“上帝的香柏樹”。赫人稱亞伯拉罕為“一位尊大的王子”， 表明他們承認亞伯拉罕為上帝所喜愛的人。
**我們沒有一人不容你。**他們衷心贊同亞伯拉罕的請求。首先，他們將自己現有的墳地獻給他──一種真正謙恭的態度。
6.en:
**Thou are a mighty prince.** The Hittites replied obligingly to Abraham’s request, reflecting his courtesy. Declining to accept his own appraisal of his status among them, “a stranger,” they acknowledged him as a “mighty prince.” Literally, “prince of God,” which according to a familiar Hebrew idiom may legitimately be translated “mighty prince,” as in the KJV. In Hebrew, similarly, the “great mountains” of Ps. 36:6 are literally the “mountains of God,” and the “goodly cedars” of Ps. 80:10, the “cedars of God.” In designating Abraham as “a mighty prince,” the Hittites voiced their recognition of Abraham as a man whom God had favored.
**None of us shall withhold.** They heartily approved of Abraham’s request. To begin with they offered to make their own burial grounds available to him—a truly courteous gesture.

7.zh:
亞伯拉罕就起來，向那地的赫人下拜，

亞伯拉罕與赫人之間的交易過程，表現了東方人的謙恭、精明和逐步商議的程序。亞伯拉罕以下拜的方式表達了他的感激。這是東方人常用的表達感激的姿勢。亞伯拉罕見那籠統的提議既然未遭到反對，就提出了一個具體的方案。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》192。
7.en: **Abraham stood up.** Oriental courtesy, tact, and bargaining procedure are obvious in the arrangements between Abraham and the sons of Heth. Abraham expressed his appreciation by bowing, a common Oriental gesture of gratitude. Meeting no opposition to his rather vague suggestion, Abraham next advanced a concrete proposal.

8.zh:
對他們說：你們若有意叫我埋葬我的死人，使他不在我眼前，就請聽我的話，為我求瑣轄的兒子以弗崙，

按照典型的東方人做法，亞伯拉罕沒有直接向以弗侖本人提出請求，而是請城中的長老利用他們的影響力使他獲得那塊想要的地產。他們將作為他交易過程中的中間人。這樣做會更快地使雙方達成協議，避難不必要的誤會。全體公眾的好名聲將保證交易的公平性，並將保護亞伯拉罕和以弗侖免遭非難。
8.en: **Intreat for me.** In typical Oriental fashion, Abraham did not direct his petition to Ephron himself, but requested the elders of the city to use their influence in securing the desired property. They were to be his go-betweens in conducting the transaction. Such a procedure would result in concluding the agreement with greater dispatch, and would also avoid misunderstandings that might otherwise arise. The good name of the entire community would ensure a fair deal, and would protect both Abraham and Ephron from criticism.

9.zh:
把田頭上那麥比拉洞給我；他可以按著足價賣給我，作我在你們中間的墳地。

**麥比拉。**有好幾種解釋。有人將其視為專有名詞，還有人將其視為對洞穴某種特性的描述。該詞源於詞根kaphal“（雙倍），暗示它可能是一個雙洞，或有兩個入口的洞。第一種解釋似乎更為可取。在這個洞相繼安葬了撒拉、亞伯拉罕、以撒、利百加、利亞和雅各（創25:9；49:31；50:13）。在先祖大家族中的只有拉結不在其內（創35:19）。有兩個洞被認定為麥比拉洞，一個在另一個的上方，靠近希伯侖的一個山坡上修建的清真寺下面。數世紀以來，人們一直被禁止進入這裡。唯一的例外是英國後來的喬治五世和他的兄弟於1882年的來訪。第一次世界大戰以後，好幾位基督徒有機會參觀上層的洞穴。當中有刻著亞伯拉罕、撒拉、以撒、雅各、利百加和利亞名字的石碑。這些石碑被認為是他們真實墳墓的標誌，而真實的墳墓是在下方岩石中鑿出來的洞穴裡。但這一古老傳說是否真實，要等到允許在下層洞穴進行科學研究後才知道。
9.en: **Machpelah.** This name has been explained in various ways. Some have taken it as a proper name, others as descriptive of some peculiarity of the cave. It is from the root kaphal “to double,” suggesting that it may have been a double cave, or perhaps one with two entrances. The first interpretation seems preferable. In this cave were deposited, successively, the remains of Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, and Jacob. (chs. 25:9; 49:31; 50:13). Rachel alone, of the great patriarchal family, was absent (ch. 35:19). Machpelah has been identified with two caves, one above the other, beneath a Mohammedan mosque on a slope near Hebron. Access was forbidden for centuries, but an exception was made in 1882 for the future George V of England and his brother. Since the first world war several Christians have had the opportunity of visiting the upper cave, which contains stone markers bearing the names of Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Jacob, Rebekah, and Leah. These slabs are supposed to mark their actual tombs, in the rock-hewn cave below. Whether this very ancient tradition agrees with the facts cannot be determined until scientific study is permitted in the lower cave.

11.zh:
不然，我主請聽。我送給你這塊田，連田間的洞也送給你，在我同族的人面前都給你，可以埋葬你的死人。

所有這一類交易都是在城門口進行的（見創34:20；得4:1）。以弗侖顯然是在場的貴族之一。他說願將洞穴連田地都送給亞伯拉罕，似乎作為一個完全的禮物。這種饋贈遵從了一種東方人至今仍在某些地區實行的習俗。每個人當然都知道這個饋贈不是當真的。以弗侖是不願意光賣洞而不賣地。
以弗侖想連田一起出售是因為赫人的法律（第46,47條）。該法律規定只有在出賣整塊土地才能免除賦稅，分塊出賣售則不能免稅。如果亞伯拉罕只買洞的話，以弗侖的賦稅就得不到減輕。但亞伯拉罕若買下整塊田地，以弗侖的賦稅就轉到了購買者身上。
11.en:
**The field give I thee.** All such transactions were made at the city gate (see Gen. 34:20; Ruth 4:1). Ephron, who was obviously one of the nobility present, and was now mentioned by name, spoke. He offered Abraham the field containing the cave, ostensibly as an outright gift. This offer follows a good Eastern custom that has been kept alive in some places to the present day. Everyone knew, of course, that this offer was not meant seriously. Ephron was unwilling to sell the cave without the field.
The reason for Ephron’s eagerness to sell the whole property and not simply part of it, lies in the Hittite laws (Nos. 46, 47), which allow a release of feudal service only if a whole field is sold, but not if it is disposed of in pieces. Hence, if Abraham had bought only the cave Ephron’s tax burden would not have been lightened, whereas Abraham’s eventual purchase of the whole property transferred Ephron’s feudal obligations to the purchaser Abraham.
**I will give thee money.** Recognizing in Ephron’s answer his willingness to let him have the cave if he would purchase the field containing it, Abraham bowed again in gratitude. He, of course, declined to accept Ephron’s property as a gift, but asked the price by stating his desire to pay for it.

13.zh:
在他們面前對以弗崙說：你若應允，請聽我的話。我要把田價給你，求你收下，我就在那裡埋葬我的死人。

亞伯拉罕明白以弗侖要將土地和洞穴一起出售的意思，就再次下拜以示謝意。當然，他拒絕以饋贈的方式接受以弗侖的地產。他詢問了田地的價格願意支付。

15.zh:
我主請聽。值四百舍客勒銀子的一塊田，在你我中間還算什麼呢？只管埋葬你的死人吧！

**四百舍客勒。**約為116美元（見創20:16註釋）。以弗侖此時說出了價格，暗示這個價錢對於象亞伯拉罕這樣的有錢人來說算不得什麼。這個價錢按現代的的標準似乎很合理，但在亞伯拉罕的時代一定是過高了。巴比倫文獻顯示普通田地當時的價格為每公頃四舍客勒，最肥沃的園地為每公頃四十舍客勒。按照巴比倫人的標準，亞伯拉罕足可以用這筆錢購買一百公頃的田地。我們雖然不知道以弗侖的田地有多大，但摩西給我們留下的印象似乎是以弗侖利用了亞伯拉罕的困境為自己好好賺了一筆。否則以弗侖是不會將田地連同洞一起賣給亞伯拉罕的（見對11節註釋）。
15.en: **Four hundred shekels.** About $116 (see on ch. 20:16). Ephron now named his price, implying that it was a mere trifle for a rich man like Abraham. Although the price appears most reasonable in terms of modern values, in the time of Abraham it must have seemed exorbitant. Babylonian records reveal that average fields were then sold at 4 shekels an acre, and the most fertile gardens at 40 shekels an acre. According to the Babylonian standard Abraham should have been able to buy a field of 100 acres for his money. Though we do not know how large Ephron’s field was, Moses seems to leave the impression that Ephron took advantage of Abraham’s predicament to make a good profit for himself. Otherwise Ephron would not have offered Abraham the field in addition to the cave (see on v. 11).

16.zh:
亞伯拉罕聽從了以弗崙，照著他在赫人面前所說的話，把買賣通用的銀子平了四百舍客勒給以弗崙。

為了避免對立，亞伯拉罕作為一個閃族人沒有和赫人討價還價，而是很乾脆地支付了田價。討價還價在整個東方從古至今都十分流行，以弗侖無疑以為亞伯拉罕也會這樣做。但作為一位“尊大的王子”，一位富有的遊牧部落的酋長，亞伯拉罕可能覺得討價還價有失於他的尊嚴。他不願意留下過於精明的名聲。“買賣通用的銀子”說明他按照習慣的商業標準當場支付了所有的田價。
16.en: **Abraham weighed.** Desiring to avoid any feelings of enmity, Abraham as a Semite at the mercy of the Hittites, paid without question rather than bargain over the price. Then as now such a procedure was customary throughout the Orient, and Ephron undoubtedly expected Abraham to do accordingly. As a “mighty prince,” a wealthy nomad chief, Abraham may have felt that bargaining was beneath his dignity, or, perhaps, he deliberately chose to avoid a reputation for sharp dealing. He paid in full on the spot, according to customary commercial standards, as the phrase, “current money with the merchant,” indicates.

17.zh:
於是，麥比拉、幔利前、以弗崙的那塊田和其中的洞，並田間四圍的樹木，

這裡顯然以書面形式訂立合同更為詳盡的條款。從亞伯拉罕的故鄉吾珥以及美索不達米其他地方發現的當時許多類似合同，提供了為此類合同的詳細格式。亞伯拉罕的地契無疑準確描述了該地產及其地點，其中的樹木和其他從物。這份合同裡包括洞。如果不寫明樹木，以弗侖就可能每年來收果實了。
這又一個赫人交易的有趣細節，因為赫人商業文書的一個特徵，是在每一次出售房地產時都註明樹木的準確數目。
**幔利前。**就是“在幔利的東邊”（英文RSV版）。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–20節）**。《先祖與先知》169。
17.en:
**The field.** Some stipulations of the contract, no doubt found in even greater detail in a written deed, are here given. Numerous such contracts of that time from Abraham’s old home, Ur, and elsewhere in Mesopotamia, present a clear picture of the form of such a contract. Abraham’s title deed no doubt contained an exact description of the property and its location, and listed the trees and other accessory items on it, in this case including the cave. If, for instance, the trees had not been specifically included, Ephron could have specifically included, Ephron could have claimed the harvest from them every year.
This is once more an interesting detail proving that Hittites were involved in the transaction, since the listing of the exact number of trees at each real estate sale is a characteristic trait in Hittite business documents.
**Before Mamre.** That is, “to the east of Mamre” (RSV).

19.zh:
此後，亞伯拉罕把他妻子撒拉埋葬在迦南地幔利前的麥比拉田間的洞裡。（幔利就是希伯崙）。

**亞伯拉罕把撒拉埋葬。**此洞位於亞伯拉罕在以撒出生前居住過的幔利附近。亞伯拉罕將他親愛的妻子安葬在了這裡。這裡可以看到那曾經多年作為他們家園的小樹林。他們曾在那裡分享他們的喜樂與憂傷，失望與盼望。
**幔利前。**“前”字的希伯來原文常被理解為“在……的東邊”。在表示方向時，希伯來人慣於認為自己是面向東方站立的，因此東邊就成了在他“面前”（見亞14:8；珥2:20；申11:24）。幔利不是希伯侖的另一個名字，只是在那附近（見創13:18）。
**在迦南地。**就像第2節那樣，這句話強調撒拉在應許之地迦南找到了一塊屬於亞伯拉罕的土地作為她最後的安息地。
19.en:
**Abraham buried Sarah.** The cave was situated near Mamre, where Abraham had lived before the birth of Isaac. In sight of the grove that had been their home for so many years, where they had shared their joys and their sorrows, their disappointments and their hopes, Abraham laid his beloved wife to rest.
**Before Mamre.** The Hebrew expression here translated “before” is at times to be understood as “to the east of.” In giving directions a Hebrew customarily thought of himself as facing the east, which was thus “before” him (see Zech. 14:8; Joel 2:20; Deut. 11:24). Mamre was not another name for Hebron, but was simply in that vicinity (see Gen. 13:18).
**In the land of Canaan.** To emphasize, as in v. 2, that Sarah found her last resting place in a piece of ground belonging to Abraham in the promised land of Canaan.

1.zh:
以撒年老，眼睛昏花，不能看見，就叫了他大兒子以掃來，說：我兒。以掃說：我在這裡。

根據以下幾點推定，本章的事件發生時，以撒已經137歲了：以掃已經結婚（46節），當時以撒一百歲（見創26:34；25:26）。下面將會看到，本章的事件一定遲得多。雅各是130歲下到埃及去的（創47:9），當時他的兒子約瑟39歲。約瑟開始為法老服務是在30歲（創41:46），經過了七個豐年和兩個災年（創41:54；45:6）。這九年加上30歲，約瑟年齡應是39歲。雅各是91歲生約瑟的。那時雅各在拉班家剛服務完十四年（創29:18,27；30:25）。雅各是77歲逃往哈蘭的。雅各的逃亡很可能是在本章事件發生後不久，而他的父親以撒又是60歲時生的雅各（創25:26），所以創27章中以撒的年齡一定是137歲左右。以撒後來又活了43年，享年180歲（創35:28）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–46節）**。《先祖與先知》179-183；《救贖的故事》88-89。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–4節）**。《先祖與先知》179。
1.en: **When Isaac was old.** From the following considerations, Isaac must have been about 137 years of age when the incident narrated in this chapter took place. Esau was already married (v. 46). This occurred when Isaac was 100 years old (see chs. 26:34; 25:26). But, as will be seen, the events recorded here must have occurred at a much later time even than that. Jacob was 130 years old when he went down to Egypt (ch. 47:9), and his son Joseph 39. This is clear from the fact that the latter was 30 years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh (ch. 41:46), and that since that time 7 abundant and 2 lean years had passed (chs. 41:54; 45:6). These 9 years must be added to the 30, making Joseph 39 years of age. Jacob was consequently 91 years old when Joseph was born. This had taken place at the end of 14 years of Jacob’s service in Laban’s house (chs. 29:18, 27; 30:25); therefore Jacob was 77 years old when he fled to Haran. Since Jacob’s flight probably followed soon after the events of this chapter, and since his father Isaac was 60 years old when Jacob was born (ch. 25:26), Isaac’s age in ch. 27 must have been about 137 years. Isaac lived for another 43 years, to the ripe age of 180 (ch. 35:28).

4.zh:
照我所愛的做成美味，拿來給我吃，使我在未死之先給你祝福。

大他十四歲的同父異母的哥哥以實瑪利（創16:16；21:5）是在137歲時去世的（創25:17）。所以他自己體質的衰退使他感到了死亡的臨近。以撒一心偏愛以掃，不顧上帝在兩個兒子出生前所給予的指示，也不顧以掃出賣其長子名分和他與迦南人結婚的事實。他對野味的喜好加強了這種偏愛（創25:28）。他很自然要用“野味”來慶祝這一場合。
4.en: **That my soul may bless thee.** Since his half brother Ishmael, 14 years his senior (chs. 16:16; 21:5), had died at the age of 137 years (ch. 25:17), his own increasing infirmities of age may have suggested the thought of approaching death. Without regard to God’s instructions with reference to the two children before their birth, and without taking notice of Esau’s barter of his birthright and his Canaanite marriages, Isaac apparently persisted in his preference for Esau. This preference being strengthened by his taste for game (ch. 25:28), it was natural that he should call for “venison” to celebrate the occasion.

5.zh:
以撒對他兒子以掃說話，利百加也聽見了。以掃往田野去打獵，要得野味帶來。

是什麼動機促使使她這樣做呢？她覺得上帝對雅各的揀選似乎要受到阻撓。以撒的意圖是顯而易見的，是與上帝顯明的旨意相違背的。她認為沒有什麼理由或爭辯能改變他的主意。她覺得上帝需要她的協助。利百加將事情抓在自己手中，希望用一個錯誤來糾正另一個錯誤。這場危機在她看來既真實又緊迫。可以想象，以撒躺在臨終的床上，決心將長子權傳給以掃。他藉著打發以掃到野外去打獵，已經啟動了傳授的程序。這個程序一旦完成，將無可挽回。怎麼辦呢？只有她有能力阻止這個似乎無法挽回的錯誤。這是她行動的最後時機。如果她錯過了這個機會，所有的希望都沒有了。在她有能力挽救局面的時候卻袖手旁觀，而單單依靠上帝按祂自己的時間和方式來成就這一切，這似乎是不可能的事。她用這一連串的理由說服自己，為了達到目的可以不擇手段。難道她不是在幫助上帝實現祂親口傳達的旨意嗎？如果這樣做算犯罪的話，上帝難道不應該赦免她嗎？當人不顧公義的嚴格標準一意孤行時，他們愚昧的心就變得昏暗了。白的看起來象黑的，錯的看起來象對的。當上帝明說是完全錯誤的事情被當作完全正確時，試探者的誘惑就達到了完全的效果（創3:6；羅1:21,22；賽5:20；彌3:2）。
5.en: **Rebekah heard.** What motives impelled her to this course of action? It seemed to her that God’s choice of Jacob was about to be thwarted. Isaac’s intention was clear, and it was contrary to God’s revealed will. Apparently she concluded that neither reason nor argument would change his mind. Feeling that God desperately needed her help, Rebekah took matters into her own hands. She resorted to one wrong in the hope of righting another. To her the crisis seemed real and urgent. Isaac, supposing he was on his deathbed, had determined to transfer the birthright to Esau. By dispatching Esau to the field for game, he had initiated the process of transfer, which, when complete, would be irrevocable. What should she do? It was in her power to prevent what appeared to be an irrevocable wrong. This was her last chance to act, and should she let it slip, all hope would be gone. To refrain from action when it was in her power to remedy the situation, and simply trust God to work things out in His own good way and time, seemed impossible. By such a process of rationalization she sought to convince herself that any means to secure the desired end was justified. Was she not helping God to bring about His own clearly expressed purpose? And if in so doing she should commit sin, would God not be obliged to forgive her? When men set their hearts upon a course of action not in accord with the strictest standard of right, their foolish hearts grow dark. White looks black, and wrong looks right. And whenever what God has clearly said to be all wrong appears to be all right, the hypnotic power of the tempter is complete (Gen. 3:6; Rom. 1:21, 22; Isa. 5:20; Micah 3:2).

6.zh:
利百加就對他兒子雅各說：我聽見你父親對你哥哥以掃說：

**懷愛倫註釋**。《救贖的故事》88。

13.zh:
他母親對他說：我兒，你招的咒詛歸到我身上；你只管聽我的話，去把羊羔給我拿來。

雅各害怕一旦他父親發現了他的欺騙就會咒詛他。利百加說她將自己承受這個咒詛，從而解除了他的恐懼心理。她和以撒都各行其是。她決心不計代價獲得那即將失去的、在她看來最有價值的事物。目前只有一件事是值得考慮的。她對自己的計謀滿有把握，根本不擔心可能的咒詛。

14.zh:
他便去拿來，交給他母親；他母親就照他父親所愛的做成美味。

雅各接受母親的安排，取了羊來。這些羊不是普通的歐洲品種。因為歐洲羊的皮毛不適於進行這樣的騙局。這是東方的駝羊。其毛呈黑色，毛質如絲，有時被用作假髮。
雅各所提出的異議表明他所擔心的不是行為的錯誤而是被發現的危險。墮落的人性所在乎的不是罪而是其後果。惟有基督的靈能給人一顆痛悔認罪的心，敢於主持正義，並把後果交託上帝（見林後7:10；彌6:8）。多年以來，雅各一直想辦法得到這個福氣。現在，這個福氣快要從他手中溜走了。所以只要利百加稍加勸導，他就不再猶豫，馬上積極配合。他自己那不聖潔的慾望，使他一下子成為試探者誘惑的受害者。
14.en:
**He went.** Jacob acceded to her plan and fetched the goats. These were not the common European variety, whose skins would be quite unsuitable for any such deception. They were the camel goats of the Orient, whose black, silklike hair was sometimes used as a substitute for human hair.
Jacob’s objection makes it clear that he was not so much concerned with the wrong of the act as with the risk of discovery. Degenerate human nature is less concerned with sin than with its results. Only the Spirit of Christ can impart to man a contrite, repentant heart, bold to do right and willing to trust God for the results of such a course of action (see 2 Cor. 7:10; Micah 6:8). For years Jacob had schemed to obtain the coveted blessing, and now that it was about to slip from his grasp, but little persuasion on Rebekah’s part was necessary to transform his hesitancy into active cooperation. His own unsanctified desires made him an easy victim to the wiles of the tempter.

19.zh:
雅各對他父親說：我是你的長子以掃；我已照你所吩咐我的行了。請起來坐著，吃我的野味，好給我祝福。

讓父親相信不是一件容易的事。雅各來到父親跟前以後，面臨許多尷尬的問題。為要達到目的，他只好編造一個又一個的謊言。他說自己是以掃，羊羔的肉是野味，並說自己這麼快回來是因為上帝賜福。
19.en: **I am Esau.** The task of convincing his father was by no means easy or certain of success. Having announced his arrival, Jacob was confronted with several embarrassing questions. One deception after another was necessary to the accomplishment of his objective. He declared himself to be Esau and the kid’s meat to be venison, and attributed his speedy return to the presumed blessing of God.

24.zh:
又說：你真是我兒子以掃嗎？他說：我是。

以撒的觸覺一定因他的年老體衰受到嚴重的影響。但他的聽覺卻更敏銳了，所以對雅各的聲音產生了懷疑。可是他兒子手上的毛似乎又符合以掃衣物上所帶田野和叢林的氣味（第15節）。最終，“美味”（第9節）的香氣勾起了他的食慾，使他消除了他擔心。他看不見；但他的觸覺、味覺和嗅覺勝過了聽覺。這一騙局的發生，原先錯在以撒。他明知上帝的旨意卻一意孤行，要將長子的名分授予以掃，因此上帝就許可他受騙（見撒上28:6；王上14:1-6；徒5:1-11）。
24.en: **Art thou my very son Esau?** Isaac’s sense of touch must have been seriously affected by his infirmity or by his age. On the other hand, his sense of hearing was more acute, and made him suspicious of Jacob’s voice. But the scent of field and forest upon Esau’s garments (v. 15) seemed to confirm the touch of his son’s hairy hands. Finally, the fragrant aroma of “savoury meat” (v. 9) whetted his appetite, and he dismissed his fears. He could not see; but touch, taste, and smell prevailed over hearing. The original mistake that had led to this deception was Isaac’s own. Furthermore, he had deliberately gone forward with his plan to invest Esau with the birthright in the face of a divine command to the contrary, and God therefore permitted him to be deceived (see 1 Sam. 28:6; 1 Kings 14:1–6; Acts 5:1–11).

27.zh:
他就上前與父親親嘴。他父親一聞他衣服上的香氣，就給他祝福，說：我兒的香氣如同耶和華賜福之田地的香氣一樣。

在希伯來原文中，祝福之類的話（見創49；申33），都是以詩體表達出來的。這是由排比句所組成的。其詞彙和語法均專用於詩歌。雅各的衣服上所帶田野和叢林的香氣使先祖想到他兒子將來的繁榮。以撒似乎看到他擁有了應許之地，並充分享受隨之而來的福氣。其中特別提到了“天上的甘露”。因為在東方國家降雨量極少，甘露對於農作物的生長是至關重要的。甘露經常被當作一種福源（申33:13,28；何14:5；亞8:12）。
27.en: **And blessed him.** The blessing itself, as with all such pronouncements (see Gen. 49; Deut. 33), is in Hebrew poetic style. This consists of parallel clauses whose diction and grammar are peculiar to poetry. The scent of field and forest upon the clothing Jacob wore suggested to the patriarch’s mind a picture of his son’s future prosperity. Isaac seemed to see him in possession of the Promised Land and in the full enjoyment of its accompanying blessings. Special mention is made of the “dew of heaven” because in Eastern countries, where there is so little rain, the dew is indispensable to the growth of the fruits of the earth. It is often mentioned as a source of blessing (Deut. 33:13, 28; Hosea 14:5; Zech. 8:12).

29.zh:
願多民事奉你，多國跪拜你。願你作你弟兄的主；你母親的兒子向你跪拜。凡咒詛你的，願他受咒詛；為你祝福的，願他蒙福。

雅各不僅要超過他的兄弟，從更廣泛的意義上說，要超過他所有的親戚，而且要超過外邦的民族。這一祝福展望到世界的統一。這也正是上帝當初為以色列人所設的計劃（見申4:6；28:10；代下9:22,23；詩126:3；亞2:11；8:22,23；14:16；《路》第289,290頁）。
29.en: **Let people serve thee.** Jacob was to be pre-eminent, not only over his brethren, in the wider sense of all his relatives, but over foreign peoples as well. This blessing envisions the concept of universal dominion, which was indeed God’s original plan for Israel (see Deut. 4:6; 28:10; 2 Chron. 9:22, 23; Ps. 126:3; Zech. 2:11; 8:22, 23; 14:16; COL 289, 290).

31.zh:
也做了美味，拿來給他父親，說：請父親起來，吃你兒子的野味，好給我祝福。

**懷愛倫註釋（31–34節）**。《先祖與先知》181。

32.zh:
他父親以撒對他說：你是誰？他說：我是你的長子以掃。

以掃回來的時候，雅各剛領受完祝福離開他的父親。以撒所受到的打擊一定是令人心碎的。但他顯然看出了上帝在此事中的干預，並得知任何再與上帝的旨意相違背的努力都將是徒勞無益的。他自知無奈，因此他既不收回對雅各的祝福，也不咒詛他。以撒一定意識到他對這個不幸的局面所負的責任。他何必埋怨雅各呢？正如以掃不顧父母的意見擅自地選擇妻子一樣，以撒也不顧上帝的旨意擅自選擇繼承人。象巴蘭一樣，以撒發現自己無法轉移上帝所預定領受之人的福氣（見民22:35；23:8,11,12）。
32.en: **Who art thou?** Jacob had scarcely received the blessing and left his father when Esau returned. The shock must have been crushing to Isaac. But, he apparently saw in the incident the intervention of Providence and concluded that any further attempt on his part to act contrary to God’s will would be futile. He knew he could not; therefore he would neither withdraw the blessing from Jacob nor seek to inflict a curse upon him. Isaac must have realized his own responsibility for the sad situation; why should he blame Jacob? As Esau had acted independently of his parents in the selection of a wife, so Isaac had acted independently of God in attempting to select his heir. Like Balaam, Isaac found himself powerless to turn away the blessing of God from one destined to receive it (see Num. 22:35; 23:8, 11, 12).

34.zh:
以掃聽了他父親的話，就放聲痛哭，說：我父啊，求你也為我祝福！

**懷愛倫註釋（34–41節）**。《健康勉言》110。

36.zh:
以掃說：他名雅各，豈不是正對嗎？因為他欺騙了我兩次：他從前奪了我長子的名分，你看，他現在又奪了我的福分。以掃又說：你沒有留下為我可祝的福嗎？

雅各這個名字的含義見創25:26註釋。以掃深深地抱怨雅各兩次欺騙了他。以掃確已將長子的名分賣給了雅各。但他這時才意識到自己的愚蠢，已為時太晚了。他現在看出雅各對他的愚弄實質上就是搶奪。
36.en: **Is not he rightly named Jacob?** As to the meaning of Jacob’s name see on ch. 25:26. Esau complained bitterly that Jacob had now deceived him twice. True, he, Esau, had sold his birthright to Jacob; but now, too late, he recognized his folly. Jacob’s taking advantage of him he now saw to be what it truly was—robbery.

38.zh:
以掃對他父親說：父啊，你只有一樣可祝的福嗎？我父啊，求你也為我祝福！以掃就放聲而哭。

上帝當然願意將無限的福氣連肥沃的土地一同賜下。只要以掃認識到是自己有缺陷的品格使他無法領受祝福，只有通過態度的轉變才有可能獲得福氣，那麼上帝對亞伯拉罕和以撒的祝福也同樣能賜給他（見耶18:7-12）。但在以掃說話時沒有想到這些。他只想得到福氣，卻沒有想到接受隨之而來的義務。就像浪子的比喻中的大兒子一樣，他心懷嫉妒，不願意讓弟弟得到福惠（路15:29）。
**以掃就放聲而哭。**以撒在答覆以掃進一步的懇求，“你沒有留下為我可祝的福嗎？”時，實際上重申了對雅各祝福，並告訴以掃他已無能為力了。當他最親愛的父親都不站在他的一邊時，以掃才如夢初醒，意識到他被上帝完全撇棄的可怕現實。他的眼淚表達了他對其損失的哀惜，而不是因為導致此損失的行為。他的眼淚是無用的，因為他不再能真正悔改了（見來12:17）。他那不完全的品格就像一道無法逾越的鴻溝，使他與他那時所認定的無價之寶相隔（見耶8:20；路16:26；《天路》271頁）。
38.en:
**But one blessing, my father?** To be sure, God has unlimited blessings that He is ready to bestow with a lavish hand. Had Esau realized that his defective character disqualified him from receiving the blessing, and that it could be his only through a reversal of attitude, the blessings of God to Abraham and Isaac might have been his also (see Jer. 18:7–12). But it was not with this in mind that Esau spoke. He coveted the blessing without any intention of accepting the obligations that went with it. Like the elder son in the parable of the prodigal, he was jealously unwilling that favor should be shown his younger brother (Luke 15:29).
**Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.** In response to Esau’s further entreaty, “Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?” Isaac repeated in substance the blessing pronounced upon Jacob, and told Esau that he could do nothing further for him. When even his father, his best friend, seemed to turn against him, Esau awoke, finally, to the awful realization of his utter rejection by God. His tears expressed sorrow for his loss, but not for the conduct which had made that loss inevitable. His tears were ineffectual because he was no longer capable of true repentance (see Heb. 12:17). Like an impassable chasm, his imperfect character stood between him and the realization of that which now seemed to him of incomparable value (see Jer. 8:20; Luke 16:26; COL 271).

39.zh:
他父親以撒說：地上的肥土必為你所住；天上的甘露必為你所得。

有感於他愛子以掃的哀傷，以撒順應了他的懇請。但他一開口，就似乎被聖靈感動，說出了以掃未來的命運。但他所說的話，與其說是“祝福”，倒不如說是一個化裝的咒詛。
給以掃的“祝福”表面上是重述了授予雅各的屬世福分。但有一些重要的變動，如省去了“五穀新酒”和上帝的名。
希伯來原文的介詞min（屬於）也有“遠離”的意思。所以以撒的意思也可以理解為：“你的居所將遠離地上的肥土，遠離天上的甘露。”與迦南地相比，以東人的家鄉將是一片貧瘠的土地。這樣的理解不僅符合希伯來原文的結構，而且更符合上下文和歷史事實：一，這是對以掃後代的家鄉以東地淒涼而沙漠化特徵的真實寫照。二，這與所說的一切福氣都已授予雅各的話語吻合，不致矛盾（第33,37節）。三，解釋了“肥土”和“甘露”在這裡的含義與雅各的命運是相反的（第28節）。當然，這要對第39節和第28節中的介詞min採用不同的譯法。但這兩節經文不同的表達方式，說明以撒在第39節中巧妙地運用了文字遊戲。以撒在這裡沒有提到上帝，表明他憑自己的權柄說話，而不是出於靈感，象對待雅各那樣。
39.en:
**His father answered.** Moved by the pathetic lament of his beloved son Esau, Isaac complied with his impassioned appeal. Once more Isaac spoke, perhaps by inspiration, this time of the future lot of Esau. This pronouncement, however, is not called a “blessing.” Actually it was a modified curse.
**Thy dwelling.** Literally, “Thy dwelling shall be [from, min] the fatness of the earth, and of [from] the dew of heaven.” According to the KJV, Esau’s “blessing” appears to be, substantially, a repetition of the temporal blessing given to Jacob. There are, to be sure, certain important variations, such as the omission of “plenty of corn and wine,” and of the name of God.
The KJV translation is grammatically possible. However, the preposition “of,” min, also means “way from.” Isaac’s meaning would then be, “Thy dwelling shall be away from the fatness of the earth, and away from the dew of heaven,” meaning that in contrast to the land of Canaan, the home of the Edomites would be an infertile region. Such a rendering is not only in accord with the Hebrew construction but is decidedly more appropriate to the context and to the facts of history: (1) It is an apt description of the dreariness and desertlike character of Idumaea, the home of Esau’s descendants. (2) It agrees with Isaac’s statement that every blessing had already been bestowed upon Jacob and avoids having him reverse himself (vs. 33, 37). (3) It explains the play upon the words “fatness” and “dew,” here descriptive of a state of affairs precisely the opposite to that declared to be the lot of Jacob (v. 28). This interpretation, it is true, treats the preposition min of v. 39 differently from that of v. 28. The different phraseology of the two verses, however, suggests that in v. 39 Isaac is making a clever play on words. The fact that Isaac here does not mention the name of God may indicate that this pronouncement was made on his own authority and not by inspiration—as was that addressed to Jacob.

40.zh:
你必倚靠刀劍度日，又必事奉你的兄弟；到你強盛的時候，必從你頸項上掙開他的軛。

以東人的生活方式和職業完全適應他們的國土。這個預言應驗在以東人兇猛好鬥的性情上。他們靠打獵和控制貿易通道為生。
**事奉你的兄弟。**對以掃的應許預言了以東人要長期從事一場擺脫雅各轄制的鬥爭。這場鬥爭有時還會取得勝利。這裡重申了上帝在他們出生之前所發的預言（創25:23）。以東不斷重演受以色列所奴役、反叛以色列人和再次被以色列征服的歷史。經過開頭一段較長時期的獨立之後，以東人被掃羅打敗（撒上14:47），後來被大衛所征服（撒下8:14）。儘管他們在所羅門統治時期曾試圖反叛（王上11:14-22），但仍然受制於猶大國直到約蘭的時代才背叛（王下8:20-22）。他們後來又被亞瑪謝所征服（王下14:7-10；代下25:11-14），並且一直受制於烏西雅和約坦的權下（王下14:22；代下26:2）。（以東控制的最大範圍，是到位於亞喀巴灣頂端的以拉他。）直到亞哈斯在位的時候，以東人才永久地掙脫猶大國王的軛（王下16:6；代下28:16,17）。但最後他們被約翰·許爾堪徹底征服了。約在公元前126年，他們被迫接受了割禮，融入猶太人的國家（約瑟夫，《上古史》第十三卷第9章第1節；第十五卷第7章第9節）。又過了一段時期之後，在羅馬的允准之下，一個以安提帕特和希律為首的以東人王朝統治了猶大。
以撒關於他的兩個兒子的預言就這樣準確地應驗了（來11:20）。對於每個兒子的祝福都是一個預言。以撒雖然是被矇騙的，但他說談到雅各的一切話卻都是聖靈所默示的，雅各仍然受到了祝福（創27:33）。這並不意味著上帝認可欺騙的行為，上帝不需要人的辦法來實現祂的旨意。上帝並沒有認可欺騙的行為，但祂掌管了一切。祝福臨到雅各不是因為欺騙，與欺騙無關。
父母和兒子們都犯了錯誤，每個人都按各自的方式受到了應有的報應。欺騙的始作俑者永遠被分開了。利百加被迫打發她的愛子離開父家到異國他鄉去，再也見不到他了。雅各因他對兄弟和父親所犯的罪而經受了二十年的流亡生活，在此期間他自己一次又一次地遭遇欺騙與失望。他是身無分文離開故土的。以撒因不顧耶和華明示的旨意堅持偏愛以掃，而遭遇雅各詭計的得逞。他將與他所忽視的兒子分開，而他所盲目喜愛之子的不敬畏神的樣子將時常在他眼前。以掃因輕看上帝和屬靈的事，永遠失去了作為長子所應得的、擔任家庭領袖的權利。上帝的旨意在人的計劃與情感的衝突中得到了實現。
40.en:
**By thy sword.** The mode of life and occupation of the Edomites were well adapted to their country. This prediction found its fulfillment in the fierce and warlike disposition of the Edomites, who gained their sustenance by hunting and controlling forcefully the trade routes.
**Serve thy brother.** The promise to Esau envisioned a perpetual, and not altogether unsuccessful, struggle for freedom from Jacob. This was a repetition of the divine prediction made prior to their birth (ch. 25:23). The history of Edom is largely a reiteration of servitude to Israel, revolt from Israel, and reconquest by Israel. After a long period of independence to start with, the Edomites were defeated by Saul (1 Sam. 14:47) and later subjugated by David (2 Sam. 8:14). In spite of an attempted revolt under Solomon (1 Kings 11:14–22), they remained subject to the kingdom of Judah until the time of Joram, when they rebelled (2 Kings 8:20–22). They were subdued again by Amaziah (2 Kings 14:7–10; 2 Chron. 25:11–14), and remained in subjection under Uzziah and Jotham (2 Kings 14:22; 2 Chron. 26:2). (The control of Elath, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba, was tantamount to the control of all Edom.) It was not till the reign of Ahaz that the Edomites permanently shook off the yoke of the kings of Judah (2 Kings 16:6; 2 Chron. 28:16, 17). At length, however, they were completely conquered by John Hyrcanus, about 126 .., compelled to accept circumcision, and merged into the Jewish state (Josephus Antiquities xiii. 9. 1; xv. 7. 9). At a still later period, through Antipater and Herod, an Idumaean dynasty ruled Judea, with the blessing of Rome.
The predictions of Isaac concerning his two sons were thus accurately fulfilled (Heb. 11:20). The blessing upon each son constituted a prophecy. Though Isaac was deceived when he spoke concerning Jacob, what he said was nevertheless inspired, and Jacob remained blessed (Gen. 27:33). That this was so does not indicate divine approval upon the act of deception, for God is not dependent upon artifice to accomplish His will. God did not ordain the act of deception, He overruled it. The blessing came to Jacob, not because of deception, but in spite of it.
Parents and sons were all in the wrong, and each in his own way suffered as a result. The perpetrators of deception were forthwith and forever separated. Rebekah was obliged to send her beloved son forth from his father’s house to a foreign land, never to see him again. Jacob suffered for his sin against brother and father by 20 years of exile, during which he was himself repeatedly deceived and disappointed. Furthermore, he went forth from home utterly destitute. Isaac, by the success of Jacob’s stratagem, was chastened for persisting in his preference for Esau in spite of the revealed will of Jehovah. He was to be separated from the son he had passed by, and to have ever before him the ungodly example of the son he had cherished so blindly. For his contempt of God and religious things, Esau forfeited forever the privileges of family leadership due the first-born. And through all the counterplay of human plans and passions the purpose of God was accomplished.

41.zh:
以掃因他父親給雅各祝的福，就怨恨雅各，心裡說：為我父親居喪的日子近了，到那時候，我要殺我的兄弟雅各。

以掃的絕望很快變成了對兄弟的刻骨仇恨，但出於對父親的尊重，他不想讓父親因其謀殺害兄弟的行為而感到悲傷和恥辱。他以為他父親的病會導致他早死，就推遲了謀殺的計劃。他當然不知道他的父親竟會恢復健康又活了四十三年。
**懷愛倫註釋（41–43節）**。《教育論》147；《先祖與先知》183.237；《救贖的故事》89。
41.en: **The days of mourning.** Esau’s despair soon changed into mortal hatred for his brother, but out of respect for his father he decided to spare him the sorrow and shame of the intended act of fratricide. Thinking that his father’s illness would end in early death, he postponed his planned act of murder. He could not know, of course, that his father would recover and live 43 years longer.

43.zh:
現在，我兒，你要聽我的話：起來，逃往哈蘭、我哥哥拉班那裡去，

以掃可能在以撒的家人中威信很高。有別人知道了他的陰謀。其中有一個人告訴利百加以掃的企圖時，她就勸雅各逃到外面躲“一些日子”，以為以掃那遊移不定的性情會使他改變主意。另外雅各借著逃跑默認了自己的錯誤，好讓以掃在以撒去世後得到父親的財產。
43.en: **Flee thou to Laban.** Perhaps Esau was generally popular among the retainers of Isaac. There were others who shared a knowledge of his plot. When Rebekah was informed by one of these of Esau’s intention, she advised Jacob to go into voluntary exile for “some days,” thinking that the vacillating disposition of Esau would bring a change of heart. Furthermore, by flight Jacob would be tacitly admitting his mistake and would leave Esau, apparently, in possession of his father’s property at the time of Isaac’s supposed imminent decease.

45.zh:
你哥哥向你消了怒氣，忘了你向他所做的事，我便打發人去把你從那裡帶回來。為什麼一日喪你們二人呢？

如果以掃殺死雅各，那麼按照習俗，與後者關係最密切的親屬就有義務殺死以掃。或許以掃想象自己在家中的威信能保護他避免這一結局，特別是在他父親去世之後。
45.en: **Why should I be deprived?** If Esau should kill Jacob, then the latter’s nearest relative was obliged by custom to kill Esau. Perhaps Esau reasoned that his own personal popularity in camp would protect him from such an eventuality, particularly after the death of his father.

46.zh:
利百加對以撒說：我因這赫人的女子連性命都厭煩了；倘若雅各也娶赫人的女子為妻，像這些一樣，我活著還有什麼益處呢？

為了徵得以撒的同意，而又不讓他知道以掃的殺機使他傷心，利百加提出了一個完全不同而又合理的理由。以撒立刻同意了。因為他和利百加一樣因以掃的妻子而愁惱（創26:35）。
46.en: **I am weary.** In order to obtain Isaac’s consent to her plan without wounding his heart by telling him of Esau’s murderous intentions, she based her proposal upon an entirely different and legitimate reason. Isaac readily consented, for he, like Rebekah, was grieved by Esau’s wives (ch. 26:35).

27.12: **A curse upon me.** Rebekah silenced Jacob’s fear of the curse his father might pronounce on him should his deception be discovered; she would accept the curse herself. She was as set in her way as Isaac was in his. Bent upon securing that which seemed of supreme value, and which was about to elude her grasp, she would count the cost later— not now. For the present, only one thing mattered. She was so certain of the success of her stratagem as to have no fear whatever of the possibility of a curse.

1.zh:
拉結見自己不給雅各生子，就嫉妒他姊姊，對雅各說：你給我孩子，不然我就死了。

利亞成為一個母親使拉結的嫉妒無法忍受。 “嫉妒是骨中的朽爛”（箴14:30），“嫉恨如陰間之殘忍”（歌8:6）。雖然拉結享有她丈夫大部分的愛，但她只要在母道方面不如姐姐就無法得到滿足。因為對於東方人來說，這是妻子最重要的職責。撒拉生以撒時至少已經結婚25年了。利百加為了生孩子空等了20年後，才和以撒轉向上帝祈禱。但在競爭下等待，使拉結在婚後不久就嫉妒焦躁起來，並懷著怨恨的精神指責雅各。
1.en: **Give me children.** Leah’s success as a mother aroused Rachel’s jealousy beyond the point of endurance. Now, envy is “rottenness of the bones” Prov. 14:30), and “jealousy is cruel as the grave” (S. of Sol. 8:6). Though Rachel enjoyed the greater share of her husband’s affection, she could not be content so long as her sister surpassed her in what was, to an Oriental, most important of all the duties of a wife—motherhood. Sarah had been married at least 25 years when Isaac was born. Rebekah had vainly waited 20 years for a child, when she and Isaac turned to God in prayer. But waiting in the face of competition made Rachel jealously impatient relatively soon after her marriage, and in bitterness of spirit she censured Jacob.

2.zh:
雅各向拉結生氣，說：叫你不生育的是神，我豈能代替他作主呢？

雅各生氣是因他寵愛的妻子所說無端的話。對於一種只有上帝才能改變的局面，他拒絕接受責備。拉結很清楚只有上帝才能使她懷孕（第6節），但她對利亞的嫉妒使她一時氣昏了頭。雅各的回答也顯示了他靈性的軟弱。他為什麼沒有向失望而怨恨的妻子提議，說他們可以像他的父母在他出生以前那樣，一起在禱告中尋求幫助呢？相反他卻同意了一種錯誤的下策。
2.en: **Am I in God’s stead?** Jacob’s passionate displeasure was naturally aroused by his favorite wife’s unseemly words. He refused to take the blame for a situation only God could change. Rachel well knew that God alone could remove sterility (v. 6), but to this fact her jealousy of Leah appears for the moment to have blinded her. Jacob’s reply also manifests a certain lack of spirituality. Why did he not suggest to his disappointed and embittered wife that they seek help in prayer, as his parents had done before he himself was born? Instead of doing this he assented to a proposal that was nothing more than a sinful expedient.

3.zh:
拉結說：有我的使女闢拉在這裡，你可以與他同房，使他生子在我膝下，我便因他也得孩子【原文作被建立】。

雅各接受並實施了拉結的提議。這與撒拉所提出的建議同樣是錯誤的（創16:2），但理由比撒拉更不充足，因為現在不存在為雅各存留後裔的問題。即或真存在這樣的理由，也不能使這種做法合理化。就是亞伯拉罕這樣做也顯然沒有得到認可。
**使她生子在我膝下。**許多聖經註釋家認為這是表示領養的希伯來習語（見創50:23），可能起源於一種古代東方的習俗。即在一個將被領養的嬰孩出生時，領養的人要視其為已出。拉結可能想到這些習俗，打算在嬰孩出生時將其認養。
3.en:
**Behold my maid Bilhah.** Rachel’s proposal, which Jacob accepted and carried out, was as sinful as that of Sarah (ch. 16:2), but without Sarah’s excuse, since there was now no question as to an heir for Jacob. If such a reason had, indeed, existed, it would not have justified the act, which even in the case of Abraham had been so clearly condemned.
**She shall bear upon my knees.** This statement has been considered by many commentators as a Hebrew idiom expressing adoption (see ch. 50:23). It is possible that the expression originated in an ancient Oriental custom, whereby, at the birth of a child that was to be adopted, the one adopting the child would receive it as his own. Rachel probably had one of these customs in mind and planned to receive the baby from birth as her own.

4.zh:
拉結就把他的使女闢拉給丈夫為妾；雅各便與他同房，

雅各在婚姻上的不檢點以多妻開始，以納妾告終。上帝雖然為了以色列後裔的繁衍而掌管了這一切，但祂並沒有因此認可了這種習俗。
4.en: **Jacob went in unto her.** Jacob’s laxity in marriage began with polygamy and ended in concubinage. Though God overruled this for the development of the seed of Israel, He did not thereby place His approval on such a custom.

6.zh:
拉結說：神伸了我的冤，也聽了我的聲音，賜我一個兒子，因此給他起名叫但【就是伸冤的意思】。

看到利亞多產，拉結認為自己的不孕乃是一種不公。她視但的出生為上帝對自己的維護。當她說：“上帝審判了我”或“上帝伸了我的冤”時，表達了這一信念，所以她稱他為但（“審判”）。她所說“也聽了我的聲音”既可以指她曾為此事禱告，也可以指她將但的出生視為上帝對她苦求的答覆（第1節）。
6.en: **Dan.** Rachel, who had considered her sterility an injustice in view of Leah’s fecundity, looked upon the birth of Dan as divine vindication of her conduct. She clearly stated, this conviction when she said, “God has judged me” or “has procured for me justice,” for which reason she called him Dan, “judge.” Her statement, “and hath also heard my voice,” means either that she had prayed about the matter or that she considered Dan’s birth as God’s reply to her bitter complaints (v. 1).

8.zh:
拉結說：我與我姊姊大大相爭，並且得勝，於是給他起名叫拿弗他利【就是相爭的意思】。

但出生後，雅各可能視闢拉為其合法的妻子，也可能是聽從了拉結的新建議，就是藉著她的使女為她再生一個兒子。當闢拉的第二個兒子出生被她收養時，她說她與她姐姐“大大相爭”（直譯為“上帝[`Elohim]的摔跤”），並且得勝。因此她稱他為拿弗他利（“我的摔跤”）。
8.en: **Naphtali.** After Dan’s birth Jacob either considered Bilhah as one of his legitimate wives or followed a renewed suggestion of Rachel to procure another son for her by her maid. At the birth of Bilhah’s second son, whom Rachel considered hers by proxy, she stated that she had “wrestled with Great wrestlings,” literally, with “wrestlings of ’Elohim [God],” with her sister and had been successful. Hence she called him Naphtali, “my wrestling.”

9.zh:
利亞見自己停了生育，就把使女悉帕給雅各為妾。

原來每年生一個兒子的利亞，見自己似乎不能再生育時，就變得急噪起來。只要利亞還有生子的希望，她就不會計較被拉結藉著使女得子的事。但她現在也嫉妒起來了，像她妹妹原先那樣。拉結用來獲得雅各喜愛的手段使利亞產生嫉妒。結果她採用了與拉結相同的手法。但利亞似乎意識到這是她自行其是，故在悉帕的兩個兒子出生時沒有提到上帝。
令人驚奇的是，雅各竟如此輕易地接受了兩個妻子為增加後代而提出來的餿主意。如果他感到娶闢拉為妾有一定的理由，即為了滿足他所愛的但沒有自己孩子的拉結的話，那麼對於已有四個兒子的利亞的提議，他又能以何種藉口來安慰他的良知呢？他踏上歧途以後，似乎既看不到自己行為的錯處，也不考慮可能的後果。另一方面，也得承認他這樣做是依從當時的慣例。從漢穆拉比法典和其他的楔形文字的文獻中，我們得知這樣的慣例在法律上和社會上都是可以接受的，特別是當不孕症妨礙人生育時。這種習俗的存在可能是亞伯拉罕和雅各都不覺得娶女奴為妾有什麼不妥的主要原因。
9.en:
**When Leah saw.** Leah, accustomed to bearing a son each year, became impatient when it seemed she was to bear no more. That Rachel had obtained sons by her maid did not disturb Leah so long as there was prospect of her having sons of her own, but now she became the victim of envy, as her sister had been before. The means employed by Rachel to retain Jacob’s favor made Leah jealous, and jealousy drove her to the employment of the same means Rachel had used. However, Leah seems to have been conscious that she was pursuing a device of her own heart, since she made no reference to God in her statements at the birth of Zilpah’s two sons.
As for Jacob, it is surprising how easily he consented to the devious suggestions of his wives in order to increase their offspring. If he had felt some excuse for taking Bilhah in order to satisfy his beloved Rachel, who had no children of her own, by what excuse could he have quieted his conscience in regard to the proposal of Leah, who already had four sons? Having entered the path of wrongdoing, he seems neither to have seen the wrong of his conduct nor to have thought of its possible consequences. On the other hand, it must be admitted that in so doing he followed a common custom of his day. From the law code of Hammurabi and other cuneiform documents we know that such a practice was legally and socially acceptable, particularly when sterility prevented childbearing. The existence of this custom is probably the main reason that neither Abraham nor Jacob saw any great mistake in taking their servants as concubines.

11.zh:
利亞說：萬幸！於是給他起名叫迦得【就是萬幸的意思】。

英文KJV版將利亞在悉帕的兒子出生時所說的話譯為“一支軍隊來了”是根據後聖經時代的猶太教遺傳。事實上她說的意思是 “萬幸”。
11.en: **Gad.** The KJV translation of Leah’s exclamation at the birth of Zilpah’s son, “A troop cometh,” is based on Jewish tradition of the post-Biblical era. Actually, the expression means, “in good fortune,” as the LXX and Vulgate have it. Thus Leah called Zilpah’s son, God, “good fortune.”

13.zh:
利亞說：我有福啊，眾女子都要稱我是有福的，於是給他起名叫亞設【就是有福的意思】。

悉帕的第二個兒子名叫亞設（“喜樂者”或“帶來幸福的人”）。她成為許多孩子的母親。利亞在她四個兒子中的三個出生時所說的話中，都承認了耶和華（創29:32,33,35）。現在看到使女所生的兒子，她似乎沒有想到上帝。他們是她自己巧計的成果。
13.en: **Asher.** Zilpah’s second son was named Asher, “the happy one,” or “bringer of happiness.” She said literally, “to my happiness, for daughters call me happy,” that is, as a mother of many children. In statements she made upon the birth of three of her own first four sons, Leah had recognized Jehovah (ch. 29:32, 33, 35). Now, with those born to her maid, she seems not to think of God. They were the successful and welcome result of her own clever devising.

14.zh:
割麥子的時候，流便往田裡去，尋見風茄，拿來給他母親利亞。拉結對利亞說：請你把你兒子的風茄給我些。

在美索不達米亞北部，麥子的收成是在五、六月份。風茄是一種顛茄科的草本植物，花為白色略帶紅色。其淡黃色有異味的果實與小蘋果的形狀和大小相仿。現今和古時一樣，這種果實在近東被視為一種春藥。東方女子仍將風茄當作一種靈丹妙藥，認為它可以刺激性慾，幫助受孕。
14.en: **Mandrakes.** In Upper Mesopotamia the wheat harvest comes in May and June. The mandrake is an herb of the belladonna family with white and reddish blossoms. Its yellowish, odoriferous fruit is about the size and shape of a small apple. Today, as in ancient times, the fruit has been considered by people of the Near East as promoting fertility. Women of the Orient still make a philter of mandrakes, which was thought to stimulate sensual desire and to aid conception.

15.zh:
利亞說：你奪了我的丈夫還算小事嗎？你又要奪我兒子的風茄嗎？拉結說：為你兒子的風茄，今夜他可以與你同寢。

拉結顯然想用風茄來消除不孕。利亞一想到要與妹妹她分享能使她更得雅各寵愛的東西就感到憤慨。與利亞相比，拉結似乎更相信心風茄而不是上帝的大能。但她最終學會了信靠上帝，而不是風茄（見創30:22；詩127:3）。
15.en: **Is it a small matter?** Rachel, apparently, desired the mandrakes as a means of removing her sterility. Leah was indignant at the very thought of parting with something that might increase her sister’s prospects of securing more of Jacob’s love than she already had. Rachel it seems, perhaps in contrast to Leah, had more faith in mandrakes than in God’s power. Eventually, however, she learned to trust in God rather than in mandrakes (see Gen. 30:22; Ps. 127:3).

18.zh:
利亞說：神給了我價值，因為我把使女給了我丈夫，於是給他起名叫以薩迦【就是價值的意思】。

“上帝應允了利亞”（第17節），要證明生命不是來源於象風茄這樣的天然手段，而是來自生命的創始者上帝。利亞以為她第五個兒子的出生是上帝對她把使女給丈夫的獎賞。她顯然把出於嫉妒的行為當作克己的表現。這個名字有“獎賞”的含義，但我們無法確定是指“有一個獎賞”，還是按拉比的遺傳理解為“他有一個獎賞”。必須注意是利亞而不是摩西把以薩迦的出生中看作其錯行的“獎賞”。
18.en: **Issachar.** “God hearkened unto Leah” (v. 17), to show that it was not from such natural means as mandrakes, but from God, the Author of life, that life comes. Leah thought she saw in the birth of her fifth son a divine reward for having given her maid to her husband, apparently considering the action that had sprung from jealousy an evidence of self-denial. The name Issachar contains the idea of “reward,” but whether it means “there is a reward” or, according to a rabbinical tradition, “he bears a reward,” is not certain. Note that it was Leah, not Moses, who saw in Issachar’s birth a “reward” for sinful action.

20.zh:
利亞說：神賜我厚賞；我丈夫必與我同住，因我給他生了六個兒子，於是給他起名西布倫【就是同住的意思】。

利亞稱第六個兒子為西布倫（“同住”），表達了她的願望，就是希望雅各現在會喜歡她超過其不生育的妹妹。她爭取在他的感情中居首位，給予她作為長房應有的尊敬，與她“同住”。
20.en: **Zebulun.** In naming her sixth son Zebulun, “dwelling,” Leah expressed her hope that now Jacob would prefer her to her barren sister. She was bidding for the first place in his affections, bidding for him to “dwell” with her in the honored relationship of first wife.

21.zh:
後來又生了一個女兒，給他起名叫底拿。

這個名字的意思是“伸冤”。她不是雅各唯一的女兒（創37:35；46:7）。這裡提到她可能是為了創34章中有關她的不幸遭遇埋下伏筆。“後來”指西布倫出生以後又過了一段時期。底拿是雅各返回迦南時的唯一女兒（見創34:1註釋）。
21.en: **Dinah.** The name means “vindication.” She was not the only daughter of Jacob (chs. 37:35; 46:7) and is probably mentioned here in anticipation of the account of her misfortune in ch. 34. The word “afterwards” indicates that some time had passed since the birth of Zebulun. Dinah was Jacob’s only daughter when he returned to Canaan (see on ch. 34:1).

22.zh:
神顧念拉結，應允了他，使他能生育。

拉結似乎最終將她的問題在禱告中交給了耶和華。她的祈求被垂聽。信心使她得到了從前因急躁和不信所得不到的東西。
22.en: **God remembered Rachel.** It seems that Rachel eventually took her problem to the Lord in prayer. Her petition was heard, and faith obtained what impatience and unbelief had heretofore prevented.

23.zh:
拉結懷孕生子，說：神除去了我的羞恥，

在古代東方，一個不生育的婦女不是被憐憫而是被藐視。無兒女被視為一種羞恥和咒詛。所以象利百加、拉結和哈拿這樣的婦女，當發現自己沒有孩子時會有如此強烈的反應。在猶太人當中，不生育被視為離婚、多妻或納妾的正當理由。
23.en: **My reproach.** In the Ancient Orient a barren woman was not pitied but despised, and childlessness was considered a shame and a curse. This explains why women like Rebekah, Rachel, and Hannah felt it so keenly when they found themselves without children. Among the Jews, barrenness was considered as justifying divorce, polygamy, or concubinage.

24.zh:
就給他起名叫約瑟【就是增添的意思】，意思說：願耶和華再增添我一個兒子。

**約瑟。**意思是“他去除”，喻指除去恥辱，或是“願他加添”，期待上帝會再加給她一個兒子。恥辱的去除暗示了這一可能性。
24.en: **Joseph.** Meaning either “he takes away,” in allusion to the removal of her reproach, or “he shall add,” in anticipation of another son whom she hoped God would add to this first one. The removal of the reproach implied this possibility.

25.zh:
拉結生約瑟之後，雅各對拉班說：請打發我走，叫我回到我本鄉本土去。

在約瑟出生後，雅各請求拉班允許他返回迦南。根據第25-28節的記載，約瑟似乎是在雅各為拉班服務的第十四年結束時出生的，也就是他結婚七年之後（見創29:21-28）。至於雅各的十一個兒子是在從他結婚後，到他為拉班服務的第十四年結束之間的七年中出生的，還是他們當中有一些是在二十年裡剩餘的六年中出生的（創31:38），我們無從得知。
這裡所排列的雅各眾子不一定按照他們出生的先後，而似乎是依據他們的母親。摩西將他們分為五組，首先列舉了利亞的四個兒子，然後是闢拉和悉帕各自的兩個兒子，利亞的另外兩個兒子，以及拉結的一個兒子。舊約中對雅各眾子的排列順序，沒有一次是完全一樣的（見創46:8-25；49:3-27；出1:1-4；民1:5-15；代上2:1,2等）。因此，人們弄不清楚他們出生的準確順序。
十一個兒子和一個女兒（創29:32至30:24）不大可能都在雅各婚後頭七年中出生，而在他為拉班服務的剩下六年中一個也沒有生。若是這樣，利亞在頭七年中必生了七個孩子，包括一段明顯的不育期（創29:35；30:9），依次有闢拉和悉帕的四個孩子出生。這樣看來，七年時間顯然是太短了。除了利亞的六個兒子被分為固定的兩組以外，我們可能認為摩西這裡所採取的順序是嚴格地依據母親。由於事實顯然並非如此，因此這五組似乎是按照每組的第一兒子出生的順序排列的，而且任何相臨各組之間都可能出現一些重疊。這種解釋似乎最符合上下文和已知的事實。所以但的出生應在所有列在他後面的兒子之先，但不一定在猶大之後。原則上說，迦得、以薩迦和約瑟也是如此。這樣的重疊可以使十一個兒子在七年時間裡出生。但即或我們接受重疊的原則，也沒有理由要求十一個兒子都在七年中出生。其中的一些兒子可能是在雅各在拉班處寄居的最後六年中出生的。事實上，後一種可能性似乎更大，因為即或我們承認在七年間重疊的可能性，如此迅速的連續出生即使從東方人的標準來看也是太密了。
25.en:
**It came to pass.** Upon the birth of Joseph, Jacob sought Laban’s permission to return to Canaan. According to vs. 25–28, it seems that Joseph was born at the end of Jacob’s 14th year of service for Laban, 7 years after his marriage (see ch. 29:21–28). Whether the 11 sons Jacob now had were all born during the 7 years intervening between his marriage and the close of this 14 years of service with Laban, or whether some of them were born during the 6 remaining years of the 20 he spent there (ch. 31:38), is not entirely clear.
The order in which Jacob’s sons are here listed does not necessarily represent the precise chronological order of their birth, but it seems to be based on their maternal parentage. Moses lists four for Leah, then two each for Bilhah, Zilpah, and again Leah, and one for Rachel—in these five groups. No two lists of Jacob’s sons recorded in the OT give them in precisely the same order (see Gen. 46:8–25; 49:3–27; Ex. 1:1–4; Num. 1:5–15; 1 Chron. 2:1, 2; etc.), and therefore it is impossible to discover any consistent pattern of birth sequence.
It would seem more than passing strange for 11 sons and 1 daughter (Gen. 29:32 to 30:24) to have been during Jacob’s first 7 years of married life, and none during the remaining 6 years he served with Laban. If, however, that be the case, then Leah bore seven children in seven years, with a distinct interval of time during which she bore no children (chs. 29:35; 30:9). If, during this interval, the four children of Bilhah and Zilpah were born in sequence, seven years would obviously be far too short. Except for the fact that Leah’s six sons are separated into two groups, it might be thought that Moses’ order here was based strictly on maternal parentage. Since this is obviously not the case, it would seem that the five groups are arranged in the order of the birth of the first son of each group, and that there is probably some overlapping between any two consecutive groups. This suggestion seems to accord best with the context and with known facts. Accordingly, the birth of Dan would be found to precede that of all the sons listed subsequent to him, but not necessarily to follow that of Judah. The same, in principle, would be true for Gad, Issachar, and Joseph. Close overlapping such as this would make possible the birth of the 11 sons within a 7-year period. But even if the principle of overlapping be accepted, there is no reason for requiring that all 11 be born during that 7 years; some may have come during the final 6 years of Jacob’s sojourn with Laban. The latter possibility, in fact, seems more likely, for, even granting the possibility of overlapping during the seven years, the rapid succession in which the births must then have come would be extremely close even according to Oriental standards.

28.zh:
又說：請你定你的工價，我就給你。

第二個七年大約是在約瑟出生時結束的，因此雅各請求拉班允許他返回迦南（第25節）。但拉班不願失去如此有用的人，又沒有留住他的理由。他讓雅各定自己的工價，但他在六年裡十次改變工價（創31:7）。在拉班的背後是那惡者，為阻撓上帝的計劃儘量阻止雅各返回應許之地。
28.en: **Appoint me thy wages.** Inasmuch as the second period of seven years terminated about the time of Joseph’s birth, Jacob requested Laban’s permission to return to Canaan (v. 25). Laban, however, was ill-disposed to lose so valuable a man, and yet was at a loss for a stratagem by which to keep him longer. The fact that he invited Jacob to state his wages did not prevent him from changing them ten times during the six years (ch. 31:7). Back of Laban was the evil one, intent upon thwarting God’s plan by preventing, if possible, Jacob’s return to the Land of Promise.

31.zh:
拉班說：我當給你什麼呢？雅各說：什麼你也不必給我，只有一件事，你若應承，我便仍舊牧放你的羊群。

當拉班再次提到工價，表明他是當真的時，雅各提出了他留下來的條件。他這樣提議是因為近東地區的山羊一般都是黑色或深棕色的，極少有白色或帶白斑的；而綿羊則大都是白色的，很少有黑色或帶斑點的。由於雅各的提議只涉及到了拉班的羊群中的一小部分，拉班馬上就同意了（第34節）。雅各還提出當日就將它們區分開來，好讓拉班看到其結果。
故事後來的經過表明雅各和拉班之間的協議還包括其他一些內容。摩西可能只提到和約的基本原則，而省略了定期區分離羊群的事；也可能這一點起初就沒有提，而是雙方所默認了的。不論如何，雅各都按約行事。拉班雖然屢次更改協議的條款（創31:7,8,41），但也沒有表示異議。
31.en:
**If thou wilt do this thing.** When Laban repeated his offer, evincing his seriousness in making it, Jacob proposed terms on which he would be willing to stay. His proposal was based on the fact that in the Near East goats, as a rule, are black or dark brown, rarely white or spotted with white, and that sheep are for the most part white, seldom black or speckled. Inasmuch as Jacob’s proposal involved but a small part of Laban’s flocks and herds, Laban hastened to approve of the plan (v. 34). Jacob offered, furthermore, to begin separating them “that day,” so that Laban might be able to see just what the results were likely to be.
The further course of the narrative shows that more was involved in the agreement between Jacob and Laban. Either Moses chose to mention only the basic principle of the agreement, and so omitted the fact that the separation was to be repeated at regular intervals, or this point was not mentioned at first, but rather taken for granted by both parties. Either way, Jacob proceeded accordingly, to which even Laban, notwithstanding his frequent alterations in the contract, does not appear to have taken exception (ch. 31:7, 8, 41).

34.zh:
拉班說：好啊！我情願照著你的話行。

拉班欣然接受了這一提議，卻沒有讓雅各進行挑選（第34-36節）。而是自己動手，可能為了確保一切都按他對合同的理解來執行的。他將雜色的綿羊和山羊交給自己的兒子們（在這裡首次提到）牧養，而只讓雅各牧養純色的羊群。最後，拉班“使自己和雅各相離三天的路程”，讓他兒子們牧養的羊群和雅各所牧養的羊群之間保持距離，防止兩個羊群之間的交配。
34.en: **According to thy word.** Laban cheerfully accepted the proposal, but did not leave Jacob to make the selection (vs. 34–36). He undertook that himself, probably to make certain that it was done according to his interpretation of the agreement. He then gave the off-color sheep and goats to his own sons (here mentioned for the first time) to tend, and left Jacob in charge of only the pure-color animals of the flock. Finally, Laban “set three days’ journey betwixt himself and Jacob,” namely, between the flock to be tended by himself through his sons and that to be tended by Jacob, in order to prevent breeding between the two flocks.

40.zh:
雅各把羊羔分出來，使拉班的羊與這有紋和黑色的羊相對，把自己的羊另放一處，不叫他和拉班的羊混雜。

第37-40節的記載表面上似乎與已知的遺傳法則相違背，有人們據此證明聖經是不科學的。但仔細研究上下文，把這段記載與已知的遺傳法則相互對照，就能使我們瞭解事實的真相，並且令人吃驚地證明聖經是上帝所默示的。關於這個課題的科研，詳見F·L·馬什，《創造論研究》367-374頁。
拉班一心要維護他在雅各所提交易條件中的利益，就立即將羊群隔離開了（第36節）。這證明拉班知道一些遺傳的法則。他將所有的雜色綿羊、山羊等都交給了自己的兒子們牧養，希望不讓它們受雅各的控制，避免將這些雜色的特徵交配回（至少看起來是）純色羊群的可能性。拉班所不知道的是這些看似純色的牲口中，有些可能還攜帶著隱性的顏色特徵，可以遺傳給它們的後代。拉班以為自己已藉著隔離羊群的聰明做法智勝了雅各。
雅各無疑是想依靠選擇性的交配手段，他對這一點的瞭解至少和拉班是一樣多的。根據對協議的嚴格解釋，這一做法是完全合理的。雅各把肥壯的與瘦弱的牲口分開（第41節），證明他通過觀察懂得了遺傳學的一些規律。拉班已將所有雜色的牲畜都分出去了，雅各此時可能不知所措，因為他顯然和拉班一樣，對隱性特徵的遺傳不太瞭解。憑著自以為的聰明和從古至今一直流行的迷信，就是母親在孕期所見的東西和所受的驚嚇會給後代留下記號，他採取了上述經文中的做法。F·L·馬什寫道：
“雅各想在拉班羊群的後代身上留下標記完全是不可能的。……在唯一聯繫母親與胎兒的胎盤與臍帶中沒有任何神經。……因此絕對不存在象雅各所以為母親能給後代留下記號的機理”（《創造論研究》368,369頁）。
另一個明顯的難解之處是雅各的方法似乎極為成功的（第43；創31:7-9）。上帝惟恐雅各將成功歸於他自己的巧計和迷信，就在一個夢中向他顯明隱性的雜色特徵是如何通過看似純色的父母傳給後代的（創31:10-12）。天使在夢中所告訴雅各的話，只能用在雅各所牧養的羊群中，因為所有雜色的牲口都已被拉班分走了（創30:35,36）。對這一遺傳法則的運用，上帝給予特別的祝福，因為隱性特徵通常不會象第43節中所描述的那樣，明顯地表現出來。祂可能運用了現今尚未完全被人瞭解的遺傳學原則。
科學家一直沒有發現和理解遺傳學法則的這一啟示，直到幾十年前才證實了聖經的科學準確性和神聖啟示性。馬什教授在結束這個問題的探討時總結說：
“聖經教訓說家畜中的這種標誌是父母雙方的遺傳因素，按照孟德爾遺傳學說的原則運作的結果，而不是由於母親懷孕時的印象。客觀地研究經文，能證明那些常被用來說聖經是一本神話書的事件，實際上正是它出於默示的重要理由之一。”（同上，第374頁。）

41.zh:
到羊群肥壯配合的時候，雅各就把枝子插在水溝裡，使羊對著枝子配合。

古猶太拉比將這節經文理解為雅各只在春天的交配季節才實施他的計謀，因為古人認為牲畜在春季受孕秋季出生，要比在秋季受孕春季出生的健壯。但現代的註釋家傾向於這是指同一季節早出生的和晚出生的羔羊，因為早春的羔羊要比晚春的羔羊值錢。根據這種觀點，雅各沒有對第二批牲口進行實驗，因為他知道它們比較瘦弱。他所實驗的是早生的較肥壯的那批牲口。不論雅各採用了何種方式，他確實壯大並增添了自己的羊群。這顯然是以削弱並減少拉班的羊群為代價的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》237。
41.en: **The stronger cattle.** The ancient Jewish rabbis understood this passage as meaning that Jacob practiced his trick during the spring breeding season only, since the ancients considered animals conceived in the spring and born in the autumn stronger than those conceived in the autumn and born in the spring. Modern commentators are inclined, however, to apply it to the early- and late-born lambs of the same season, since early-spring lambs are more valuable than those born later in the season. According to this opinion, Jacob did not conduct his experiments with the second litter of cattle, because he knew they would be weaker, but with the early, stronger litter. Whatever method Jacob used, he did so to strengthen and increase his own flocks, obviously at the expense of weakening and diminishing Laban’s.

43.zh:
於是雅各極其發大，得了許多的羊群、僕婢、駱駝，和驢。

雅各與拉班的故事是狡計和技巧與貪心和違規的較量。狡計，即運用更高明的知識，往往是弱者對付強者的武器。貪婪、狡猾，但缺乏智慧的人常常被同樣狡猾但更為聰明的人所勝。正理在雅各一邊。他只是利用了他的新地位來彌補十四年勞動所受的虧負。但他卻缺乏嚴格的誠實和正直。在他的身上沒有人們在一個義人身上所期望看到坦誠單純的品格。的確，雅各的計劃非常成功，但這並不意味著耶和華的僕人應該效法他。雅各的錯在於過多地依賴他自己的聰明，來謀求上帝向他所應許的福氣，而不是依靠上帝的大能和眷佑。但雅各將他的成功歸之於上帝的大能（創31:9）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》192。
43.en: **The man increased exceedingly.** The story of Jacob’s relations with Laban is one in which cunning and skill are matched against avarice and foul play. Cunning, which applies superior knowledge, is often the weapon of the weak against the strong. Men who are grasping and treacherous but lacking in wisdom are often outwitted by men of equally devious but more clever ways. Justice was on Jacob’s side. He was simply taking advantage of his new position to offset the disadvantage under which he had labored for 14 years. However, he was lacking in strict honesty and integrity. That openness and simplicity of character people expect to find in a righteous man were lacking. Jacob’s plan was most successful, to be sure, but does not commend itself as one that a servant of Jehovah would be expected to follow. Jacob erred, furthermore, in relying more upon his own craft to secure the divine blessing promised him than upon the power and providence of God. For his part, Jacob, however, attributed his success to the power of God (ch. 31:9).

30.37:
**Jacob took him rods.** The narrative of vs. 37–40 appears on the surface to contradict known laws of genetics, and is sometimes cited as proof that the Bible is unscientific. However, a careful study of the context and a comparison of the narrative with known facts relating to the laws of genetics reveals what took place and vindicates in a truly remarkable way the inspiration of the Scriptures. For a detailed, scientific discussion of the subject, see F. L. Marsh, Studies in Creationism, pp. 367-374.
Thinking to safeguard his own interests in the bargain proposed by Jacob, Laban immediately separated flocks and herds (v. 36), a fact which indicates that Laban also knew something of the laws of heredity. He placed all the off-color sheep, goats, and cattle under the care of his own sons, intending thereby to remove them from Jacob’s charge and thus avoid the possibility of breeding these off-color characteristics back into what, visibly at least, was pure stock. What Laban did not know was that some of the apparently purebred animals might still carry recessive color characteristics that could be transmitted to their offspring. Laban thought he had outwitted Jacob by the shrewd device of separating the flocks.
Jacob, for his part, had no doubt been counting on selective breeding, concerning which he must have known at least as much as Laban did. This procedure would have been entirely legitimate according to a strict interpretation of the contract. The distinction Jacob made between strong and weak cattle (v. 41) is evidence that observation had taught him something of the laws of heredity. Now that Laban had separated all the off-color animals Jacob was probably at a loss to know what to do, for it is apparent that he know no more about the transmission of recessive characteristics than did Laban. Trusting to his own supposed cleverness and to the application of the ancient and still popular superstition that offspring may be marked in a way corresponding to sights or fears experienced by the mother during the prenatal period, he set up the procedure explained in these verses. Says F. L. Marsh:
“All marking of the offspring such as that which Jacob thought he was accomplishing in Laban’s flocks, is completely impossible. … In the placenta and umbilical cord, which constitute the only connection between the mother and the fetus, there are no nerves. … Thus absolutely no mechanism exists whereby the mother can mark her offspring in the way that Jacob thought he was accomplishing the marking” (Studies in Creationism, pp. 368, 369. Italics in the original).
A further apparent difficulty lies in the fact that Jacob’s method seems to have proved method eminently successful (v. 43; ch. 31:7–9). Lest Jacob, however, credit his own ingenuity and superstition, God revealed to him in a dream how the recessive, off-color characteristics were transmitted through apparently pure-color parents to their offspring (ch. 31:10–12). What the angel told Jacob in a dream could only apply to the flocks and herds under Jacob’s care, for all off-color animals had previously been removed by Laban (ch. 30:35, 36). To the operation of this law of genetics God added His special blessing, for recessive characteristics would not normally show up in so marked a manner as is indicated in v. 43. In so doing, He may perhaps have utilized principles of genetics at present only imperfectly understood.
This revelation of a law of genetics not discovered and understood by scientists until a few decades ago attests the scientific accuracy and divine inspiration of the Scriptures. Professor Marsh closes his discussion of the subject by saying:
“The Scriptures teach that such markings among domestic stock are the result of hereditary factors in both parents working according to Mendelian principles and are not due to maternal impressions. A fair reading of the text thus shows that that incident in the Scriptures, which is so often cited as proof that the Bible is a book of fables, is in actuality one of the important reasons for believing that it is indeed an inspired volume” (ibid., p. 374. Italics in the original).
In passing, it may be observed that the Hebrew word translated “hazel” in the KJV should be rendered “almond,” and the “chestnut tree” as “plane tree.” The Oriental plane tree belongs to the maple family.

1.zh:
雅各聽見拉班的兒子們有話說：雅各把我們父親所有的都奪了去，並藉著我們父親的，得了這一切的榮耀【或作財】。

拉班兒子們的抱怨顯然言過其實，因為當雅各離開時拉班仍有羊群（第19節）。拉班的兒子們雖然沒有公開指責他，卻暗示說他靠欺騙的手段獲取財富。他們無法證實他有違約的行為，但他們確信他一定這樣做了。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–55節）**。《先祖與先知》190-194。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–3節）**。《救贖的故事》90。
1.en: **The words of Laban’s sons.** The claim of Laban’s sons was obviously exaggerated, since Laban still had flocks when Jacob left him (v. 19). Laban’s sons hinted that Jacob had secured his wealth by fraud, though they did not openly accuse him of that crime. They could not prove that he had in any way violated any provision of the agreement between him and their father, though they were sure he must have done so.

2.zh:
雅各見拉班的氣色向他不如從前了。

雅各無意中聽到的話語證實了他從拉班的態度中所觀察到的事實。拉班的一切手段，都絲毫不能阻止雅各財產的急劇加增。結果連他們過去虛假的友善關係現在都變成了公然的敵對，在上帝天意的安排下，拉班的態度成為了雅各回鄉的動因。雅各堅信現在他該返回父家了。直接來自上帝的信息堅定了這種信念。
2.en: **The countenance of Laban.** What Jacob overheard was confirmed by what he observed in Laban’s attitude. As a result of the fact that nothing Laban did seemed to hinder in the least Jacob’s rapid increase in wealth, even the pretense of friendliness that had marked their relations in the past had now changed to overt antagonism. In the providence of God, Laban’s attitude became the means of bringing about Jacob’s return to the land of his birth. Jacob’s conviction that the time had come to return to the land of his fathers was confirmed by a direct message from God.

3.zh:
耶和華對雅各說：你要回你祖、你父之地，到你親族那裡去，我必與你同在。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》193。

4.zh:
雅各就打發人，叫拉結和利亞到田野羊群那裡來，

雅各和羊群離家有一段距離。他叫妻子到田野來是為了更安全地策劃他們的逃離。如果在家裡商量，拉班的人可能會偷聽到他們的談話並報告拉班，讓他來阻止他們離去。儘管他們十分謹慎，消息仍然在第三天傳到了拉班的耳中（第19,22節）。對羊群和牲畜的管理似乎發生了一些改變，因為雅各現在看管著自己的羊群（見創30:35,36），或至少可以接近它們。拉班很可能是因給自己的羊剪羊毛而不在，使雅各能帶著他所有的財產逃跑（第1,29節），否則是不可能逃跑的。雅各可能是在給自己的羊剪羊毛的同時，打發他的妻子帶來一切所有的，在那裡支搭帳棚假裝擺設筵席，因為人們在這種場合經常這樣做。這樣，他為逃跑做了準備，以免提前被人察覺。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–7節）**。《救贖的故事》90。
4.en: **Called Rachel and Leah.** At some distance from home with the flocks, Jacob called his wives to the field for greater secrecy in planning their departure. Had this been done at home, members of Laban’s household might have overheard their conversion and reported to Laban in time for him to return and prevent their leaving. Despite all their precautions, word reached Laban the third day (vs. 19, 22). It seems that some change had taken place in the supervision of the flocks and herds, for Jacob was now in charge of his own (see ch. 30:35, 36), or at least had access to them. Likely, it was Laban’s absence, shearing his own sheep, that made possible Jacob’s escape with all his property, an event that would obviously have been impossible otherwise (vs. 1, 29). Perhaps Jacob was simultaneously shearing his own sheep, and sent for his wives and all their belongings, to erect tents on the spot under the pretext of festivities usually held upon such occasions. Thus he prepared the way for a departure that would not arouse suspicion in advance.

7.zh:
你們的父親欺哄我，十次改了我的工價；然而神不容他害我。

“十次”可能不按字面理解。它也許只是表示一個大概的數目，說明變動的經常性，就像我們所說的“十倍”（參但1:20）。拉班顯然想借著不斷更改條款限制其最初的協議。雅各隻字不提他自己的策略，而將他憑巧計獲得的一切都歸功於上帝的賜福。這說明他意識到自己採取了不完全誠實的手段。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》190。
7.en: **Changed my wages.** “Ten” may not have been meant literally. It was used, perhaps, simply as a round number to indicate very frequent change, much as we would say “a dozen times” (cf. Dan. 1:20). Laban apparently made repeated attempts to limit the original agreement by changing its provisions. That Jacob passed over in silence his own stratagem and attributed to God’s blessing all that he secured by craft implies consciousness that the means employed were not completely honest.

9.zh:
這樣，神把你們父親的牲畜奪來賜給我了。

雅各或許感到若不是上帝定意要祝福他，他自己的努力將是徒然的。因此，他當然要將其財富的加增歸功於上帝慈善的眷佑。他肯定感到他自己的計謀和上帝的賜福是不矛盾的。
9.en: **God hath taken away.** Jacob felt, perhaps, that had it not been God’s will to bless him, his own efforts would not have succeeded. Therefore, and not without reason, he deemed it right to attribute his increased wealth to God’s benevolent care. It is certain that he felt his own devices and the blessing of God not to be mutually exclusive.

11.zh:
神的使者在那夢中呼叫我說：雅各。我說：我在這裡。

我們無法確知這個夢是與第3節中的簡短啟示分別賜下的，還是對那個神聖啟示更為詳細的講述。有些註釋家認為那夢是在雅各最後六年的服務開始時臨到他的。還有人認為這只是一個普通的夢，雅各將它與伯特利所做的夢結合在一起，現在告訴妻子是為了加深她們的印象。這種觀點是站不住腳的，因為所啟示的信息在生物學方面十分準確，與雅各自己的迷信正好相反（見創30:37-42註釋）。
11.en: **Spake … in a dream.** It is uncertain whether this dream came separately from the brief revelation of v. 3, or whether it is a more complete account of that divine communication. Some commentators suggest that it came at the very beginning of Jacob’s last six-year term of service. Some think that it was only an ordinary dream Jacob connected with the one he had received at Bethel, and now related in order to impress his wives. This view is untenable because of the biological accuracy of the information revealed in it, information which was contrary to Jacob’s own superstitious beliefs (see on ch. 30:37–42).

14.zh:
拉結和利亞回答雅各說：在我們父親的家裡還有我們可得的分嗎？還有我們的產業嗎？

兩姊妹雖然相互嫉妒，但對她父親的行為卻表現出了一致的態度。這說明她們的抱怨是真實的。拉班的冷酷和貪得無厭是十分露骨的，甚至連他的女兒也起來反對他。她們抱怨說她們雖然是生而自由，是合法的兒女，但卻沒有得到任何的產業，而且她們還曾象奴隸一樣被出賣。顯然，拉班把所有財產都給了兒子們，女兒們什麼也沒有得到。
14.en: **Rachel and Leah answered.** The fact that the two sisters were in perfect agreement in regard to their father’s conduct, in spite of their own mutual jealousies, is clear evidence of the validity of their complaints. Laban’s heartless cruelty and insatiable greed were obviously so pronounced that even his own daughters eventually rose in protest. They complained that in spite of being freeborn, legitimate children, no inheritance had been given them, and they had been sold like slaves. Apparently, all of Laban’s property had been transferred to his sons, for his daughters received none of it.

15.zh:
我們不是被他當作外人嗎？因為他賣了我們，吞了我們的價值。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》189。

16.zh:
神從我們父親所奪出來的一切財物，那就是我們和我們孩子們的。現今凡神所吩咐你的，你只管去行吧！

拉結和利亞從丈夫驚人的成功中意識到上帝的作為。她們與父親的疏遠雖然是令人遺憾的，但他的吝嗇與卑鄙使這樣的反應即使不是無法避免，也是可以理解的。另一方面，她們感到自己和她們的丈夫，就是她們孩子的父親，已經緊密而溫柔地結合在了一起了。她們與他同命運，共呼吸。兩姊妹第一次表現出一致的意見。拉結剛剛成為一個兒子的母親。這可能緩解了二人在婚姻生活頭幾年所存在的緊張和嫉妒。
16.en: **All the riches.** Rachel and Leah recognized the hand of God in their husband’s remarkable prosperity. Regrettable as their alienation from their father may be, his severity and meanness made such a reaction understandable if not inevitable. On the other hand, they felt bound to their husband, the father of their children, in a close and tender union. Their lives and fortunes were now completely identified with his. For the first time the two sisters are presented as united in opinion. That Rachel had but recently become the mother of a son herself may have eased the tension and jealousy that had existed between them during the first years of their married life.

19.zh:
當時拉班剪羊毛去了，拉結偷了他父親家中的神像。

拉班離家出去可能在雅各叫他妻子到田野去之前，而不是在他們決定離開哈蘭之後。拉結得以偷取她父親的神像說明拉班在她離去時並不在家。雅各知道他的岳父將參加剪羊毛和通常與此相關的歡宴要化好幾天時間（見撒上25:4,11；撒下13:23），朋友們經常被邀請參加筵席。我們無法確知到底是雅各沒有受到邀請，還是由於他們之間的矛盾，他謝絕了拉班的邀請。但這確實為他的順利逃跑提供了一個絕好的機會。
“神像”（teraphim，見士17:5；18:14等），通常是一些小（第34節）的偶像，偶爾也有較大的，一般是用木頭製成的（撒上19:13-16）。近東的考古發掘發現了大量用木頭、泥土和貴重金屬製成的神像。有些為男性神祗，但大多數都是5至8釐米長的女神小雕像。它們被用作家庭神像或隨身攜帶的護身符。由於它們大都為性徵突出的裸體女神，很可能被認為是促進生育能力的神，所以拉結特別喜歡它們。從美索不達米亞的努斯發掘出來的楔形文字文獻顯示，家庭神像只有當父親去世時家中確實沒有親生兒子時才能由養子繼承。如果一個人有兒子，他的神像就不能傳給女兒。因此，拉結沒有權利佔有她父親的家神，正如雅各承認的那樣（創31:32）。在美索不達米亞的努斯發現的文獻表明，在先祖時代，擁有拉班這樣的家庭神像意味著擁有家產的繼承權（ANET，第219,220頁）。所以拉班急於要把它們拿回來（見第30,33-35節）。
19.en:
**Laban went to shear his sheep.** The RSV translation, “had gone,” is preferable to that of the KJV, “went,” for Laban had probably left home before Jacob called his wives to the field, and not after their decision to leave Haran. The fact that Rachel was able to steal her father’s images suggests Laban’s absence from home at the time of her own departure. Jacob knew that his father-in-law would be detained several days by the task of shearing his sheep and the festivities commonly connected with it (see 1 Sam. 25:4, 11; 2 Sam. 13:23), to which friends were often invited. Whether Jacob had not been invited, or had declined Laban’s invitation, owing to the dissension existing between them, is uncertain. But it did afford him an excellent opportunity to escape unhindered.
**Rachel had stolen the images.** These “images,” teraphim (see Judges 17:5; 18:14; etc.), were usually small (v. 34) human figurines, occasionally larger, often made of wood (1 Sam. 19:13-16). Near Eastern excavations have brought them to light in profuse numbers, made of wood, clay, and precious metals. Some represent male gods, but the majority are figurines of female deities 2 to 3 in. in length. They were used as household gods or were carried on the body as protective charms. Since most of them represent nude goddesses whose sexual features are accentuated, they were probably thought to promote fertility. This may be the reason Rachel especially cherished them. Cuneiform texts from Nuzi in Mesopotamia reveal that the household gods were inherited by adopted sons only when no actual sons were present at the father’s death. If a man had sons, his gods could not go to his daughters. Rachel therefore had no right to her father’s household gods, as Jacob frankly admitted (Gen. 31:32). Documents found at Nuzi, in Mesopotamia, indicate that in the patriarchal age the possession of the family’s household gods, such as Laban had, guaranteed to their holder the title to his father’s properties (ANET 219, 220). This was probably the chief reason why Laban was so eager to retrieve them (see vs. 30, 33–35).

20.zh:
雅各背著亞蘭人拉班偷走了，並不告訴他，

直譯為他“欺騙了亞蘭人拉班的心”或他“瞞騙了拉班”（英文RSV版）。
20.en: **Jacob stole away.** Literally, he “deceived the heart of Laban the Aramaean,” or he “outwitted Laban” (RSV). For the expression “the Syrian,” meaning the Aramaean, see on ch. 25:20.

21.zh:
就帶著所有的逃跑。他起身過大河，面向基列山行去。

**大河。**即幼發拉底河（王上4:21；拉4:10,16）。我們不知道雅各是如何帶著他的羊群渡過幼發拉底河的，特別是在春季（創31:19）。當然這裡沿河兩岸有許多地方淺灘。雅各的第一個目的地基列，是雅姆克河谷南部的多山地帶。拉班就是在基列趕上了他的。雅各在此場合下起了基列（迦累得）（第47節）這個名字。其原來的名稱不為人知。
雅各逃亡和與以掃和好的行程
1. 雅各從別是巴出發經過了伯特利，可能渡過了約旦河沿著大路來到大馬士革。
2. 他繼續向北經過了哈馬（哈瑪特）、阿勒坡，最終到達哈蘭。
3. 二十年後，在回家的路上，他被拉班在靠近瑪哈唸的地方追上。
4. 雅各在瑪哈念附近見了一個異象，為他與以掃見面的前夕在毗努伊勒所經歷的嚴峻考驗做好思想準備。
5. 雅各從毗努伊勒遷移到了示劍，以掃返回希伯侖。
21.en: **Passed over the river.** The Euphrates, pre-eminently the river of Bible times (1 Kings 4:21; Ezra 4:10, 16). How Jacob succeeded in crossing the Euphrates with his flocks, particularly in the springtime (Gen. 31:19), is not known. There are, of course, fords at various places along the river in this vicinity. Jacob’s immediate destination, Gilead, was the mountainous region south of the Yarmuk River. Gilead is mentioned here in view of the fact that Laban overtook him there. The name Gilead (Galeed) was given it by Jacob upon that occasion (v. 47). Its former name is unknown.

23.zh:
拉班帶領他的眾弟兄去追趕，追了七日，在基列山就追上了。

由於拉班在雅各逃跑兩三天後才得到消息（第22節），所以花了七天的時間追趕。二人似乎是在雅各離開哈蘭九或十天後才相遇的。基列的山地離哈蘭有440多公里，大約是駱駝快行七天的路程。這正是拉班所花費的時間。但這樣短的時間絕對不可能趕著羊群和牲畜行走如此長的一段距離，因為它們每天行走的路程超不過15或16公里。拉班在聽到他們逃跑的消息後顯然沒有立即追趕。他知道雅各行進的速度一定很慢（創33:13,14），因此不需要著急。由於拉結偷取了她父親的家庭神像，她一定是從哈蘭動身的，因她父親的家在那裡（創29:4,5）。拉班知道他的偶像被偷，說明他在追趕雅各之前回過家。他可能完成了剪羊毛的工作，結束了相關的歡宴，安排好照料雅各在離開哈蘭時所留下的羊群。從他得知雅各逃跑的消息到他自己出發，也可能有三十多天時間。
23.en: **Pursued after him.** Since Laban received word two or three days after Jacob’s flight (v. 22), and overtook him after a pursuit of seven days, it appears that the two met nine or ten days after Jacob’s departure from the vicinity of Haran. The mountains of Gilead lie more than 275 mi. from Haran, a distance that can be covered by fast camels in 7 days, the time required by Laban. But it would be impossible to drive the flocks and herds such a distance in that length of time, since they could cover no more than 9 or 10 mi. a day. Apparently Laban did not pursue the fugitives immediately upon receiving word of their flight. He knew that Jacob could make but slow progress (ch. 33:13, 14), and that he himself need therefore be in no haste. Since Rachel had taken her father’s household gods, her departure must have been from Haran, where her father’s home was situated (ch. 29:4, 5). The fact that Laban knew his idols had been stolen suggests that he must have returned home before pursuing Jacob. He may have finished the shearing of his sheep, concluded the accompanying festivities, and arranged for the care of the flocks Jacob had forsaken before leaving Haran. The time that elapsed between his receiving word of Jacob’s flight and his own departure may easily have been 30 days or more.

24.zh:
夜間，神到亞蘭人拉班那裡，在夢中對他說：你要小心，不可與雅各說好說歹。

上帝以出乎意料的方式實現了二十年前對雅各的應許（創28:15,20,21）。上帝在夢中向一個拜偶像的人親自顯現是很不尋常的。拉班曾通過他的祖父拿鶴以及亞伯拉罕的僕人以利以謝瞭解到了亞伯拉罕的宗教（創24:31,50），後來又與自己的外甥長期相處，所以他認出在他趕上雅各的前夕與他夢中說話的乃是真神（第29節）。
**說好說歹。**直譯為“從好到歹”，是一句諺語（創24:50；撒下13:22）。不論是用武力還是用利誘，拉班都不得勉強雅各回去。
24.en:
**God came to Laban.** In a most unexpected way God fulfilled the promise given to Jacob 20 years earlier (ch. 28:15, 20, 21). It is unusual that God should have revealed Himself to an idolater thus in a dream. Laban, who had become acquainted with Abraham’s religion through his grandfather Nahor, through Abraham’s servant Eliezer (ch. 24:31, brGE 24:50>50), and more recently through his long association with his own nephew, recognized the true God as the speaker in his dream the night previous to his overtaking Jacob (v. 29).
**Good or bad.** This expression, literally “from good to bad,” is proverbial (Gen. 24:50; 2 Sam. 13:22). Laban was not to compel Jacob to return, either by force or by making further attractive inducements.

27.zh:
你為什麼暗暗地逃跑，偷著走，並不告訴我，叫我可以歡樂、唱歌、擊鼓、彈琴的送你回去？

拉班趕上了雅各。他擺出一幅深受委屈和傷害的父親的樣子。難道雅各不知道拉班是多麼容易強迫他回哈蘭嗎？拉班之所以能夠與雅各說話而沒有報復他，完全是他列祖的上帝昨夜干涉的結果。但雅各渴望回家，為什麼要偷岳父的神象呢？這是拉班唯一正當的理由，是一支鋒利的矛。雅各可能勸過岳父放棄異教的神，指出偶像的虛妄，要他接受真宗教。而現在他自己似乎很在意拉班的家庭神像，不願舍下它們離開哈蘭。拉班是否擔心雅各想借此得到他其餘的財產呢（見19節註釋）？
27.en: **Wherefore didst thou flee.** Overtaking Jacob, Laban assumed the role of a good-natured but grievously wronged and deeply hurt father.
