A character more excellent than that of his older brothers qualified him for the leadership of the family, and his posterity for leadership in Israel (see ch. 49:3, 4, 8–10).

29.zh:
隨後這孩子把手收回去，他哥哥生出來了；收生婆說：你為什麼搶著來呢？因此給他起名叫法勒斯。

他瑪兒子的名字都是依據他們出生時的趣事。孿生兄弟出生的順序與起先相反。收生婆批評第二個兒子：“你為什麼搶著來呢？”，即“你知道怎麼搶先”。這孩子便依據收生婆話取名為法勒斯（“搶出來”）。儘管收生婆不看他為長子，但他在家譜中總排列謝拉之前（創46:12；民26:20等）。他成了大衛王的先祖（得4:18-22），彌賽亞也是從他而出的（太1:3-16）。
29.en: **Pharez.** The names of Tamar’s children were based on the interesting episode which occurred at their birth. When the twins were born in the reverse order from that in which they first appeared, the midwife addressed the second one reprovingly, saying as it were, “What a breach you have made for yourself,” meaning perhaps, “You really knew how to push yourself to the front.” From this saying of the midwife the boy received the name Pharez, “break.” Although the midwife did not consider him the first-born, he is henceforth always placed before Zarah in the genealogical lists (Gen. 46:12; Num. 26:20; etc.). He became the ancestor of King David Ruth 4:18–22), and through him, of the Messiah (Matt. 1:3–16).

30.zh:
後來，他兄弟那手上有紅線的也生出來，就給他起名叫謝拉。

**謝拉。**帶有紅線的孿生兄弟起名為謝拉，意思是“興起”。
30.en: **Zarah.** The twin with the scarlet thread was named Zarah, “rising.”

1.zh:
雅各見埃及有糧，就對兒子們說：你們為什麼彼此觀望呢？

**懷愛倫註釋（1–8節）**。《先祖與先知》224。

2.zh:
我聽見埃及有糧，你們可以下去，從那裡為我們糴些來，使我們可以存活，不至於死。

旱情越來越嚴重，人畜都受到煎熬，雅各決定從埃及購糧，免得家人捱餓。他之所以沒有象亞伯拉罕（創12:10）和以撒（創26:2）那樣舉家遷往埃及，可能是由於埃及也象迦南一樣在鬧饑荒。
2.en: **Get you down thither.** As the drought became more and more severe, and man and beast were both suffering, Jacob made the decision to fetch grain from Egypt to preserve his family from starvation. That he did not, like Abraham (ch. 12:10) and Isaac (ch. 26:2), plan to move his family to Egypt may have been due to the fact that the famine prevailed in Egypt as well as Canaan.

3.zh:
於是，約瑟的十個哥哥都下埃及糴糧去了。

十個人一起去埃及既可能為了安全，也可能是因為糧食要分配給各家的家長。他們人多可能會使他們分到多一些，以便帶回更多的糧食。另外，饑荒也很有可能導致有人搶劫他們商隊的糧食。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》234；《證言》卷三67。
3.en: **Ten brethren went down.** That all ten went to Egypt was either for safety or because the grain was distributed to heads of families. Their number would possibly enable them to secure more grain, and would certainly enable them to return with more of it. Also, the famine conditions would render plundering of their caravan for its supplies of food a very real possibility.

4.zh:
但約瑟的兄弟便雅憫，雅各沒有打發他和哥哥們同去，因為雅各說：恐怕他遭害。

便雅憫不是因為年紀小而留在家中，他現在已經二十多歲了，而是因為他是拉結唯一剩下的孩子，取代約瑟成為雅各最關愛的對象。
4.en: **Benjamin.** Benjamin was not kept back because of his youth, since he was now more than 20 years of age, but because, as the only remaining child of Rachel, he had taken Joseph’s place as the object of Jacob’s most tender affections.

5.zh:
來糴糧的人中有以色列的兒子們，因為迦南地也有饑荒。

約瑟的哥哥們可能加入某個迦南的商隊，也可能和其他人一起來埃及購糧。
5.en: **Among those that came.** Joseph’s brothers either formed part of a caravan of Canaanites or simply arrived with others who had come for the same reason.

6.zh:
當時治理埃及地的是約瑟；糶糧給那地眾民的就是他。約瑟的哥哥們來了，臉伏於地，向他下拜。

治理（shallit）一詞源自詞根shalat，表示被授予無限權柄的人。該詞在亞蘭語和阿拉伯語中，隱含在蘇丹（sultan）這個頭銜，或撒拉提斯（Salatis）這個人名之內。按照馬尼託的說法，撒拉提斯是希克索斯第一位國王的名字。馬尼託可能將這個表示“統治者”的詞誤認為人名。該詞表明約瑟不是一位普通的糧食部長。作為全國位居第二者，他是埃及實際的統治者和宰相。
6.en: **The governor.** From shalliṭ in turn derived from the root shalaṭ, “to rule.” It is used to designate one invested with unlimited authority. This word, known also in Aramaic and Arabic, lies behind the title sultan, and perhaps behind the personal name Salatis, which, according to Manetho, belonged to the first Hyksos king. Manetho, however, may have mistaken the word meaning “ruler” for a personal name. This word shows clearly that Joseph was more than an ordinary minister of food. As the second man in the country he was the actual ruler, or prime minister, of Egypt.

7.zh:
約瑟看見他哥哥們，就認得他們，卻裝作生人，向他們說些嚴厲話，問他們說：你們從哪裡來？他們說：我們從迦南地來糴糧。

約瑟立刻認出了他的哥哥，他們卻沒有認出他來（第8節），因為他們已有二十多年沒有見他了。他現在不僅長大了，而且也埃及化了。他穿著埃及人的衣裳，臉也刮淨了，沒有留著閃族人的大鬍子。另外，他說著一種陌生的語言，顯然是一位大官。他們不可能把這樣一位權貴與約瑟聯繫在一起（見創45:3）。
約瑟之所以“向他們說些嚴厲話”不是出於報復心，而是為了瞭解他們現在的心思，特別是對他和便雅憫的態度，因為便雅憫不在一定引起了他的注意並且使他產生懷疑。
7.en:
**He knew them.** Joseph recognized his brothers at once, but they, not having seen him for more than 20 years, did not recognize him (v. 8). Not only was he older now, but he was Egyptianized as well, wore Egyptian dress and had a clean-shaven face instead of a Semite beard. Furthermore, he spoke a strange language and was, apparently, a great lord. The mere thought of connecting Joseph with this mighty man would have seemed highly absurd (see ch. 45:3).
**Spake roughly unto them.** That Joseph spoke “hard things to them,” as the text reads literally, was not due to a feeling of revenge, but rather to ascertain their present state of mind, particularly with regard to himself and to Benjamin, whose absence had certainly arrested his attention and perhaps aroused his suspicion.

9.zh:
約瑟想起從前所做的那兩個夢，就對他們說：你們是奸細，來窺探這地的虛實。

這就是約瑟向他哥哥們所說的“嚴厲話”。埃及一直對東部鄰國存有戒心，因為他們不但曾襲擊埃及然後退回沙漠，而且還曾侵入埃及並實際控制了部分地區。在第十二王朝之前的第一過渡期中，這樣的入侵曾使國王阿蒙尼姆赫特一世在地中海與紅海之間修築邊境防禦工事，稱為“統治者之牆”，防範迦南人入侵埃及。此後，同樣來自東方的希克索斯人獲得了埃及的統治權。他們謹防其他民族也步他們的後塵。因此，約瑟對東方人的嚴加盤查並設法查出不受歡迎的人或真正的奸細，這是很自然的。鄰國流行的饑荒使大量的外國人來到埃及購糧，所以政府需要更為謹慎地將那些可能危及國家安全的人清除出去。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–17節）**。《先祖與先知》225。
9.en: **Ye are spies.** The “hard things” Joseph spoke to his brothers are now revealed. Egypt had always been suspicious of its eastern neighbors, who had not only raided Egypt and then vanished back into their desert abodes, but had in the past infiltrated Egypt and actually taken over the government of parts of the country. Such incursions during the First Intermediate Period, prior to the Twelfth Dynasty, had led King Amenemhet I to build border fortifications between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, called “Wall of the Ruler,” to keep the Canaanites out of Egypt. The Hyksos, coming afterward and also from the east, had now gained the supremacy of the country and were watchful that others might not do to them what they had done to the Egyptians. It was therefore natural for Joseph to examine all easterners carefully, and make an effort to detect any undesirables or actual spies. Since the famine raging in the neighboring countries brought great numbers of foreigners to Egypt as grain purchasers, greater care had to be taken to weed out those whose presence in the country might endanger its security.

10.zh:
他們對他說：我主啊，不是的。僕人們是糴糧來的。

約瑟的哥哥們雖然對這個指控不滿，但懼怕之心使他們不得不吞聲忍氣，他們堅稱自己是無辜的。當他們見自稱為誠實人，仍未能說服埃及首長時，就告訴他家中更具體的情況，想借此證明自己的無辜。他們都屬於一個不可能對埃及發動侵襲的家族，所以沒有任何理由懷疑他們是奸細。約瑟接受了他們的說法，並堅持要他們帶來不在場的最小兄弟，以證實他們的故事。
10.en: **Nay, my lord.** If Joseph’s brothers were offended by the accusation hurled against them, fear led them to swallow their pride, and they asserted their complete innocence. When their claim to being honest men failed to impress the Egyptian lord, they told him more particularly about their family. By this they sought to prove their innocence. Inasmuch as they all belonged to one family, which could hardly make a hostile attack upon a whole kingdom, there was no real reason for suspecting them of being spies. Joseph took up the challenge and insisted that they prove the accuracy of their story by producing their missing youngest brother.

17.zh:
於是約瑟把他們都下在監裡三天。

約瑟嚴肅地命令他的哥哥們（第15節）打發他們當中的一個回迦南去將便雅憫帶來。他們不肯，因為他們知道雅各絕不會同意的。於是約瑟將他們全都下在監裡三天。這表面上是因為他們不接受他的提議，實際上是要進一步考驗他們。由於他們的殘忍，他曾在監裡受了近三年的苦，而他只讓他們關了三天。
17.en: **Into ward three days.** Joseph had solemnly charged his brothers (v. 15) to send one of their number back to Canaan to fetch Benjamin. Their apparent unwillingness to do this, in the knowledge that Jacob would not consent, led Joseph to send them all to jail for three days. This was ostensibly done in consequence of their unwillingness to agree to his proposal, but in reality to test them further. He had languished in prison for approximately three years, as the result of their inhuman treatment; he inflicted on them a confinement of only three days.

18.zh:
到了第三天，約瑟對他們說：我是敬畏神的；你們照我的話行就可以存活。

到了第三天，約瑟改變了嚴厲的態度。他所說“我是敬畏上帝的”是泛指的，以一位埃及統治者口氣說話，不是指耶和華。他並沒有將九個人留在監裡，而只扣留一個，允許其他的人回去將便雅憫帶回來，並帶糧食給他們受苦的家人。他們若帶著便雅憫回來，就能確保那被監禁之人的獲釋。如果他們用謊言欺騙約瑟的話，就將死於飢餓，而那留在埃及的人將被當作奸細處死。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–29節）**。《先祖與先知》226。
18.en: **This do, and live.** On the third day Joseph modified his severe attitude. His explanation, “I fear God,” was intended to be understood in a general way, without reference to Jehovah, as supposedly coming from an Egyptian ruler. Instead of imprisoning nine of them he would keep only one in prison, and allow the others to return to fetch Benjamin and to carry food to their suffering families. Their return with Benjamin would procure the release of the one to be held in prison. If, on the other hand, they had deceived Joseph with their story, they would die of hunger, and the one remaining behind in Egypt would be executed as a spy.

21.zh:
他們彼此說：我們在兄弟身上實在有罪。他哀求我們的時候，我們見他心裡的愁苦，卻不肯聽，所以這場苦難臨到我們身上。

當他們意識到這位埃及的首長不會單因懷疑就處罰或殺死他們，而是公正地審判他們時，他們的開始良心發現了。他們對約瑟的做法的是何等的不同啊！全埃及的統治者尚且同情他們在迦南捱餓的家人，而他們卻曾想讓他們的兄弟在坑中餓死。當這些想法從他們的腦海中浮現時，他們就承認了自己的罪行。他們自己的遭遇使他們想起他們兄弟的痛苦。流便提醒他們，當初他曾如何警告他們不要傷害那孩子，卻是徒然。而他們現在得到這種冷酷的公正報應。他們如此在約瑟的面前自責，卻不知道他明白他們的每句話。
21.en: **We are verily guilty.** As they realized that this lord of Egypt would not punish or slay them upon mere suspicion, but judge them justly, their consciences began to speak. How differently they had acted toward Joseph! The ruler of all Egypt had compassion on their families, who suffered hunger in Canaan, whereas they had intended to leave their brother in the pit to starve. As these and similar thoughts passed through their minds, they were led to an acknowledgment of their guilt. Their own misfortune brought back to them the anguish of their brother. Reuben reminded them of how he had warned them, unsuccessfully, not to sin against the boy, and now they were receiving a just reward for their coldness toward him. Thus they accused themselves in Joseph’s presence, without realizing that he understood every word.

24.zh:
約瑟轉身退去，哭了一場，又回來對他們說話，就從他們中間挑出西緬來，在他們眼前把他捆綁。

約瑟放過了相對無辜的流便，選擇使他遭受殘酷待遇的主謀西緬（《祖》226頁）。西緬的殘酷也表現在其他的場合之中，例如在他和利未屠殺示劍人的時候。當西緬在他兄弟的眼前被綁起來的時候，他們想起了他們曾對約瑟所做的事。約瑟則希望他們對西緬的憐憫會促使他們儘快帶來便雅憫。
24.en: **Took from them Simeon.** Passing by Reuben, who had been comparatively guiltless, Joseph selected Simeon, the chief instigator of the cruel treatment he received (PP 226). Simeon’s heartlessness had been manifested on other occasions also, as when he and Levi had massacred the Shechemites. As Simeon was bound before the eyes of his brothers they were forcefully reminded of what they had done to Joseph, who may have hoped that pity for Simeon would encourage their more speedy return with Benjamin.

25.zh:
約瑟吩咐人把糧食裝滿他們的器具，把各人的銀子歸還在各人的口袋裡，又給他們路上用的食物，人就照他的話辦了。

器具（keli），可能指籃子或其他容器。放錢的“口袋”希伯來文是saq，通過希臘語sakos和拉丁語saccus進入歐洲語言。除了這兩個名詞以外，這個故事還用了一個表示“口袋”的古老詞彙（`amtachath），是saq的同義詞，因為它們是可以互換的（第27,28節；創43:12等）。
約瑟把錢退給他們不是出於惡意，而是他覺得不能接受父親和兄弟買糧的錢。即或他可能想到哥哥們會因發現銀錢而驚恐，他也看不出有理由使他們免受這樣的憂慮。經過了前幾天苦澀的經歷，這會有助於進一步軟化他們剛硬的心。
25.en:
**Their sacks.** The first word translated “sacks,” keli, means “vessels” or “receptacles,” and may have signified a basket or other container. The second word “sack,” into which the money was placed, is a transliteration of the Hebrew śaq, which has found entrance into the European languages through the Greek sakos and the Latin saccus. Besides these terms another old word for “sack” is used, the Hebrew ‘amtachath. It is employed in the Bible only in connection with this story, and must have been a synonym of śaq, because it is used interchangeably with it (vs. 27, 28; ch. 43:12; etc.).
Joseph did not return their money maliciously, but could not bring himself to accept money from his father and brothers for bread. Even if he may have thought it possible that his brothers would be alarmed upon finding the money, he saw no reason for sparing them this anxiety. It would help to soften their hard hearts still more, after the bitter experiences of the preceding days.

27.zh:
到了住宿的地方，他們中間有一個人打開口袋，要拿料餵驢，才看見自己的銀子仍在口袋裡，

他們當中的一人發現了銀錢，給眾人都帶來了驚恐。這難道是要降在他們身上更多不幸的預兆？他們在埃及已經被當作奸細；難道現在還要被指控為盜賊嗎？兄弟們把這個使他們困惑的事情，看作一種來自上帝的懲罰。這證明了這事對他們的有益。他們在驚恐之餘，忘了查看其餘的口袋。
27.en: **Opened his sack.** The word “inn” would be more accurately rendered “lodging place,” as in the RSV. The discovery of his money by one of them brought consternation to all. Was it a harbinger of further misfortunes yet to befall them? In Egypt they had already been taken for spies; would they now also be accused as thieves? That the brothers looked upon this, for which they were at a loss to account, as a punishment from God, is evidence of its salutary effect upon them. In their consternation and alarm they forgot to examine the rest of the sacks.

29.zh:
他們來到迦南地、他們的父親雅各那裡，將所遭遇的事都告訴他，說：

回家之後，他們彙報了自己的遭遇，包括西緬的被囚。當他們打開袋子發現銀錢全在時，就比以前更加感到害怕了。只有一個人在路上發現了銀錢，而其他人到家後才發現，可能因為只有那份銀錢藏在口袋的開口處，其他的都藏在口袋的底部或底部附近。也可能是因為一份放在飼料袋中，而其他的放在糧袋中。
29.en: **They came unto Jacob.** Reaching home, they reported their sad experiences, including the detention of Simeon. Upon opening their containers and finding all their money, they were more alarmed than ever. The reason that only one had discovered his money while on the road, and the others after their return home, may have been that it was hidden in the opening of one sack only, but at or near the bottom of the others. Or, it may have been placed in the fodder sack of one and in the food sacks of the others.

36.zh:
他們的父親雅各對他們說：你們使我喪失我的兒子：約瑟沒有了，西緬也沒有了，你們又要將便雅憫帶去；這些事都歸到我身上了。

雅各聽了他們的遭遇，看到了銀錢歸還的不祥之兆，並意識到他又失去了一個兒子，不禁放聲痛苦，指責他的兒子們要為失去約瑟和西緬的負責。現在，他們又打算將便雅憫帶走。雅各對待他的兒子並不公平，因為他不知道他們在約瑟失蹤的事上有過錯，他們當然也不應直接為西緬的被囚而受到責難。儘管如此，他們還得把雅各的哀怨接受為一種應得的責備。他們知道他所說的一切比他自己所知道的還要真實。他們確實使他們的父親失去了約瑟，他們也感到西緬的被囚乃是對那殘酷之舉的公正報應。現在，他們既然無法擔保便雅憫會安全回來，他們怎能承擔帶便雅憫去埃及的責任呢？他們處在兩難之境，但他們唯一其他的選擇就是捱餓。如果他們想要使西緬獲釋並救他免死，如果他們和他們的家人想要倖免於飢餓，就必須回埃及購糧。
**懷愛倫註釋（36–38節）**。《先祖與先知》227。
36.en: **Me have ye bereaved.** Upon hearing their sad story and seeing the evil omen of the returned money, and realizing that he had lost a second son, Jacob broke out in a bitter lament, accusing his sons of responsibility for the loss of Joseph and Simeon. Now, they were bent on taking Benjamin away also. Jacob was hardly fair toward his sons, since he did not know that they were guilty in the matter of Joseph’s disappearance, and since, of course, were not directly to blame for Simeon’s imprisonment. Nevertheless, they must have accepted Jacob’s lament as a well-deserved rebuke. They knew that he spoke more truly than even he himself knew. They had certainly bereaved their father of Joseph, and felt also that Simeon’s imprisonment was a just reward for that cruel act. How could they now shoulder the responsibility of taking Benjamin to Egypt, when there was no certainty that he would return safely? They were in a predicament, but their only other choice was starvation. If they were to secure Simeon’s release and save him from certain death, and if they and their families were to survive the famine, they must return to Egypt for grain.

37.zh:
流便對他父親說：我若不帶他回來交給你，你可以殺我的兩個兒子。只管把他交在我手裡，我必帶他回來交給你。

流便的建議表現出極大的犧牲精神。這是一個真誠而魯莽的建議。流便雖然肯定不是雅各眾子中最聰明的，但卻是年紀最大的。他再次表現出是一個軟心腸的人。但雅各拒絕了；他不大相信他們保證會讓便雅憫安全回來。他們的手不乾淨，過去曾給他帶來許多憂慮的時光。流便曾犯過嚴重的罪行，西緬和利未曾屠殺一城的人。猶大的家十分罪惡，他的兩個兒子都因犯罪而早年夭折。上帝怎能用這樣的人來擔保便雅憫呢？他們所參與的每件事都以失望或災難告終。
37.en: **Reuben spake.** Reuben’s offer represented supreme sacrifice on his part. It was a sincere but rash offer. Reuben was the eldest, though certainly not the wisest, of Jacob’s sons, and once more he turns up as the tenderhearted one. But Jacob refused; he had little confidence in their ability to guarantee Benjamin’s safe return. Their hands were not clean. They had caused him many anxious hours in the past. Reuben had committed a grievous sin, Simeon and Levi had murdered the population of a city, and the family of Judah was so evil that two of his sons had died in their youth for their wickedness. How could God prosper Benjamin with such men? Everything in which they were involved ended in disappointment or disaster.

1.zh:
那地的饑荒甚大。

**懷愛倫註釋（1–34節）**。《先祖與先知》227-228。

2.zh:
他們從埃及帶來的糧食吃盡了，他們的父親就對他們說：你們再去給我糴些糧來。

從埃及帶回來的糧食都吃完了，持續的旱災使饑荒得不到緩解。雅各就打發他的兒子們回去埃及“糴些糧來”。兒子們自己沒有采取主動；他們知道不帶著便雅憫回埃及是沒有用的，也知道不可能改變他們父親的主意。於是猶大代表大家提出，堅持要帶便雅憫同去，因為埃及的首長曾經鄭重地宣佈，沒有他們最小的兄弟，他們就不得見他的面。雅各的第四個兒子猶大之所以成了這次的代言人，是因為雅各的長子流便已經被拒絕了，西緬被囚在埃及，而利未可能因他對示劍人所用的詭詐而失去了父親的信任（創34）。
2.en: **Go again.** When the grain brought from Egypt had all been consumed, and the continued drought brought no relief from famine, Jacob called upon his sons to return to Egypt for “a little food.” The sons themselves were not taking the initiative; they knew the uselessness of returning without Benjamin, and the apparent impossibility of changing their father’s mind. Judah, becoming spokesman for the others, firmly maintained that they would not go unless Benjamin should accompany them, since the Egyptian lord had solemnly declared that they should not see his face without their youngest brother. Judah, Jacob’s fourth son, was spokesman upon this occasion because Reuben, Jacob’s eldest son, had already been refused, Simeon was in an Egyptian prison, and Levi had probably forfeited his father’s confidence as a result of his treachery against the Shechemites (ch. 34).

6.zh:
以色列說：你們為什麼這樣害我，告訴那人你們還有兄弟呢？

對於父親追問他們為什麼要告訴埃及的首長有關便雅憫的事，他們辯護說他們並沒有說漏嘴。他們怎麼知道這會成為一個禍根呢？雖然前面沒有提到約瑟問起他們的家況（創42:13,22），但他們這樣說顯然是回答一個直接的提問。猶大後來在替便雅憫向約瑟求情的時候，曾提到約瑟問過這樣的一個問題（創44:19）。
6.en: **Wherefore dealt ye so ill?** To the father’s reproachful question, why they had informed the Egyptian viceroy about Benjamin, they replied in self-defense that they had been guilty of no slip of the tongue. How could they have known that such a question would become a source of trouble later on? Though Joseph’s questions concerning their family do not appear in the preceding narrative (ch. 42:13, 22), it is apparent that that information had been supplied in answer to a direct inquiry. In pleading before Joseph in behalf of Benjamin, Judah later reminded him of having asked just such a question (ch. 44:19).

9.zh:
我為他作保；你可以從我手中追討，我若不帶他回來交在你面前，我情願永遠擔罪。

猶大接著重申了不得不重返埃及的局面，暗示否則的話大家都會餓死。他親自承擔保證便雅憫安全回來的責任。他或者他們當中的其他人還能做什麼呢？猶大的話語所體現的高尚品格，後來在他向約瑟的懇求中也表現了出來（創44:18-34）。自從發生了創37,38章所記載的事件以後，他的品格一定發生了很大的變化。
9.en: **I will be surety.** Judah repeated then the unavoidable condition for returning to Egypt, hinting at death by famine as the only alternative. He would personally accept responsibility for Benjamin’s safe return. What more could he, or any of them, do? The nobility of character so conspicuous in Judah’s language is illustrated later in his pathetic pleading before Joseph (ch. 44:18–34). A great change must have taken place in his character since the incidents recorded in chs. 37, 38.

11.zh:
他們的父親以色列說：若必須如此，你們就當這樣行：可以將這地土產中最好的乳香、蜂蜜、香料、沒藥、榧子、杏仁都取一點，收在器具裡，帶下去送給那人作禮物，

猶大的邏輯是駁不倒的，經過他這一番感人的懇求，雅各只好尊重現實。他既已同意讓便雅憫去，就盡其所能地為這次出行的成功做準備。他所提出的禮物都是本地最好的產品，是埃及人所特別看重的（見創37:25註釋）。
**蜂蜜。**可能不是“蜂蜜”，因為埃及盛產蜂蜜。從巴勒斯坦帶來的少量蜂蜜就連送禮者也不會視為貴重的禮品。所以更有可能是是葡萄蜜，就是將葡萄汁或新酒熬至原來的一半或三分之一而製成的。希臘人稱之為hepsema（“煮沸之物”），至今仍從巴勒斯坦的希伯侖地區出口到埃及。
**榧子。**在聖經中只提到過這一次。這是阿月渾子樹（Pistacia vera）的長橢圓形果仁（即開心果），具有一個多脂的核子，被東方人視為上等的美食。
**杏仁。**杏樹在希伯來語中為shaqed（“守望者”），源自動詞shaqad（“不眠”、“醒著”、“警醒”）。這是春季第一個開花的樹，在敘利亞和巴勒斯坦生長茂盛，在古埃及卻不為人知。
11.en:
**If it must be.** After the eloquent plea of Judah, whose logic was irrefutable, Jacob submitted to the inevitable. Now that he was reconciled to Benjamin’s going, Jacob set about doing everything within his power that might contribute to the success of the journey. The present he suggested was to be of the choice products of the country, ones that were highly valued in Egypt (see on ch. 37:25).
**A little honey.** That this was probably not bee “honey” appears from the fact that honey was abundant in Egypt. A small quantity of bee honey from Palestine would not have been considered a respectable gift, even by the giver. More likely, it was grape honey, prepared by boiling grape juice or new wine down to a half or a third of its original volume. The Greeks called it hepsema, “the boiled matter.” It is still imported into Egypt from the Hebron region of Palestine.
**Nuts.** This fruit, the oblong nut of the Pistacia vera, is mentioned in the Bible only this once. It has an oily kernel and is considered a choice delicacy by Orientals.
**Almonds.** The almond tree is called shaqed, “the watcher,” from the verb shaqad, “to be sleepless,” “to be awake,” “to watch.” It is the first of all the trees to blossom in the spring. Though it flourished in Syria and Palestine, this tree seems not to have been known in ancient Egypt.

12.zh:
又要手裡加倍地帶銀子，並將歸還在你們口袋內的銀子仍帶在手裡；那或者是錯了。

由於第一次購糧的銀錢被退了回來，雅各建議他的兒子們帶雙份的銀錢返回埃及，用以支付上次和這次的糧款。儘管雅各擔心退還銀錢在埃及可能會引起誤會（創42:35），但他希望這是弄錯了。
12.en: **Double money.** Since the amount paid for the first lot of grain had been returned, Jacob advised his sons to take a double amount of money back to Egypt, to pay for the grain procured previously and for food to be bought on this trip. Although Jacob had feared that the return of the money might be interpreted falsely in Egypt (ch. 42:35), he expressed hope that it might have been done by mistake.

14.zh:
但願全能的神使你們在那人面前蒙憐憫，釋放你們的那弟兄和便雅憫回來。我若喪了兒子，就喪了吧！

在他們離開之前，年邁的先祖為十個兒子祝福，相信上帝會使他們在埃及統治者面前蒙憐憫。“憐憫”原文指“腹部”，古人視之為情感的所在。雅各雖然表達了對上帝保護的信心，但下一句話卻表現他對於上帝是否會賜福給那些不良的兒子們沒有把握。他們是一群無法預測的人，什麼事都有可能幹得出來。他只好聽天由命，接受上帝的旨意。
14.en: **If I be bereaved.** Before their departure, the aged patriarch blessed his ten sons and expressed confidence that God would give them mercy before the ruler of Egypt. The word translated “mercy” means, literally, “bowels,” and refers to the abdomen, considered anciently the seat of the affections and emotions. Though Jacob expressed faith in God’s protection, his very next statement reveals uncertainty as to whether God could bless his reprobate sons. They were an unpredictable lot, and might be counted on to get into trouble even where none might otherwise exist. In a spirit of resignation he acquiesced to the divine will, whatever it might be.

16.zh:
約瑟見便雅憫和他們同來，就對家宰說：將這些人領到屋裡。要宰殺牲畜，預備筵席，因為晌午這些人同我吃飯。

約瑟曾經指控他們是奸細，所以他們不可能越過他，而從一個較小的官員那裡得到所需要的糧食。約瑟可能曾經下令，只要他們一回埃及，就將他們帶到他的面前來。外國人，特別是雅各的眾子，不論需要履行的是什麼手續，反正這十個兄弟很快就被再次帶到那位可怕的首長面前。約瑟一見到他們，就下令將他們帶到他的私人住宅，併為他們預備了筵席（直譯為“宰殺了要宰殺之物”）。埃及的浮雕表明，埃及富人的家常便飯是由牛肉和鵝肉，而且在款待賓客時會用相當數量的肉食。
16.en: **When Joseph saw Benjamin.** Inasmuch as Joseph had charged them with being spies, there was no way of by-passing him and getting the desired corn from a lesser official. Joseph had probably issued an order to have them brought to him personally as soon as they should return to Egypt. Whatever may have been the procedure required of foreigners, especially of Jacob’s sons, the ten brothers soon found themselves once more in the presence of the dreaded lord of the land. Seeing the men, Joseph gave orders for them to be taken to his private residence and a meal prepared for them, literally, “to slaughter a slaughtering.” Egyptian reliefs reveal that beef and geese constituted the rich man’s usual fare in Egypt, and that considerable quantities of meat were served at meals when visitors were entertained.

18.zh:
他們因為被領到約瑟的屋裡，就害怕，說：領我們到這裡來，必是因為頭次歸還在我們口袋裡的銀子，找我們的錯縫，下手害我們，強取我們為奴僕，搶奪我們的驢。

當約瑟的兄弟們得知要被帶到約瑟的屋裡時，就比先前更害怕了。他們可能聽不懂約瑟的話，因為是用埃及話說的，當他們到了他的官邸並被吩咐進去時，以為是因被控偷竊而要淪為奴隸。為了避免所擔心的事的發生，他們就接近門口的家宰，向他解釋如何在口袋裡發現了銀錢，並且準備歸還。創42:27,28的記載和這裡的重述並沒有矛盾。他們可能在旅店裡都打開過他們的口袋，但只有一個人在當時發現了他的銀錢。我們無法想象整隊人馬只帶回了十袋糧食來供養他們的牲畜和家人好幾個月之久。
18.en: **The men were afraid.** Joseph’s brothers were more deeply alarmed than ever upon discovering that they were to be taken to Joseph’s house. They may not have understood Joseph’s order, which had been given in Egyptian, and when they arrived at his official residence and were bidden to enter, they expected to be put into slavery, under indictment for theft. In an effort to avert what they feared, they approached the steward at the door, explaining how they had found the money in their sacks and that they were prepared to repay it. There is no need to assume a discrepancy between the record of the occurrence as given in ch. 42:27, 28 and as repeated here. It is possible that all had opened their sacks at the “inn,” but that only one had discovered his money at that time. It is inconceivable that the entire group had taken back only ten sacks of grain to feed their animals and their families for a period of several months.

23.zh:
家宰說：你們可以放心，不要害怕，是你們的神和你們父親的神賜給你們財寶在你們的口袋裡；你們的銀子，我早已收了。他就把西緬帶出來，交給他們。

家宰顯然知道約瑟的計劃。他的安慰使他們放了心。他對他們說，他已經收下了他們的銀錢。銀錢的再次出現應理解為上帝所為。彷彿是為了消除他們所有的恐懼，他將西緬領來，以正式的東方禮節將他們當作客人款待，給他們水洗腳，並給他們運輸用的牲口草料。
23.en: **I had your money.** The steward, who apparently knew of Joseph’s plans, calmed them with the reassurance that their money had reached him, and that the reappearance of their money was to be explained as an act of God. As if to banish all their fears, he brought Simeon to them, and with true Oriental courtesy treated them as guests, giving them water for washing their feet and feeding their beasts of burden.

26.zh:
約瑟來到家裡，他們就把手中的禮物拿進屋去給他，又俯伏在地，向他下拜。

兄弟們來到時，約瑟可能正忙於要務而不能立即接見。更有可能的是，他已經安排妥當，不想在預定的時刻以前見到他們。約瑟一回來，他們就畢恭畢敬地將禮物獻上，不知不覺地應驗了約瑟那曾引起他們恨他的異夢。
26.en: **When Joseph came home.** Joseph may have been busy on some important matter when his brothers arrived, and could not give them his attention just then. Or, more likely, his plans were already well laid, and he did not wish to see them until the time designated. Upon Joseph’s return, they handed him their present with the most reverential obeisance, unwittingly fulfilling the dreams of Joseph that had incited their intense hatred for him.

29.zh:
約瑟舉目看見他同母的兄弟便雅憫，就說：你們向我所說那頂小的兄弟就是這位嗎？又說：小兒啊，願神賜恩給你！

當約瑟舉目看見他同母的兄弟便雅憫時，就以詢問其身份的方式，確認這些人是否實際履行了所要求的條件。
29.en: **Saw his brother.** When his eyes fell upon Benjamin, his brother by his own mother, Joseph went through the form of inquiring as to his identity—had the men actually fulfilled the required conditions?

30.zh:
約瑟愛弟之情發動，就急忙尋找可哭之地，進入自己的屋裡，哭了一場。

這是約瑟第二次被情感所勝，第一次是當他的哥哥們談到他們對他的殘忍之時（創42:21）。見到了他二十二年沒見面的親兄弟，使他激動不已。“發動”一詞原文的意思就是“腸發熱”，是由於愛的強烈所引發的（見14節註釋）。為了考驗他的哥哥們對便雅憫的態度，他還不準備向他們暴露自己的身份，於是他急忙隱退，免得無法繼續他的計劃，得出合乎邏輯的結論來。在筵席上，他們必定會自由交談；這樣他就有了一個極好的機會了解他們的態度。在鎮靜下來以後，他洗了臉，又回到其兄弟當中，並吩咐人擺設筵席。
30.en: **His bowels did yearn.** This was the second occasion on which Joseph was overcome with emotion, the first having been when his brothers spoke of their cruelty toward himself (ch. 42:21). Now it was the sight of his own brother, whom he had not seen for 22 long years, that stirred his emotions. The expression “did yearn” reads literally, “were becoming warm,” that is, due to the intensity of his love (see on v. 14). Since he desired to test the attitude of his brothers toward Benjamin, he was not yet ready to make himself known to them, and withdrew hastily lest he be unable to carry his plan through to its logical conclusion. At the meal, where they might be expected to converse freely, he would have an excellent opportunity to discern their attitude. Regaining his poise, he washed his face, rejoined his brothers, and ordered dinner served.

32.zh:
他們就為約瑟單擺了一席，為那些人又擺了一席，也為和約瑟同吃飯的埃及人另擺了一席，因為埃及人不可和希伯來人一同吃飯；那原是埃及人所厭惡的。

他獨自就餐可能是因為他的地位，也可能是因為其埃及的隨從不願意和約瑟的兄弟一同吃飯，也不願意與他這個亞細亞人一同吃飯。古埃及人在與外國人交往上總是很挑剔的。他們認為自己是最高級的人種。他們自稱為“人”，而所有其他的人差不多都是介乎他們與動物之間的野蠻人。對外國人的厭惡在吃飯的問題上清楚地表現出來。例如，希伯來人宰殺和食用動物，是被埃及人當作聖物的。根據希羅多德的記載（第二章第41節），沒有一個埃及人願意用希臘人的刀、叉、或燉鍋，也沒有一個埃及人願意吃用希臘式的刀具所切的潔淨動物的肉。
32.en: **For him by himself.** A separate table was prepared for him, for his brothers, and for the Egyptians who dined with him. He ate separately either because of his high position or because his Egyptian entourage would not eat with him, an Asiatic, for the same reason they would not eat with Joseph’s brothers. The ancient Egyptians were always particular in the matter of association with foreigners. They considered themselves to be the highest class of human beings. They called themselves “people,” whereas all others were more or less barbarians, creatures standing between them and the animal world. The aversion to foreigners revealed itself strikingly in the matter of eating. The Hebrews, for example, slaughtered and ate animals that were regarded by the Egyptians as sacred. According to the account of Herodotus (ii. 41), no Egyptian would use the knife, or fork, or saucepan of a Greek, nor would he eat of the flesh of a clean animal that had been cut up with a Grecian knife.

33.zh:
約瑟使眾弟兄在他面前排列坐席，都按著長幼的次序，眾弟兄就彼此詫異。

他們發現他們在餐桌上的排列次序是按照年齡的，就以詫異的眼神彼此相望，認為這個令人敬畏的首長知道他們的年齡一定是出於超自然的啟示。
33.en: **The men marvelled.** Discovering their arrangement at the table according to age, the men looked at one another with amazement, convinced that this august official had been supernaturally advised as to their ages.

34.zh:
約瑟把他面前的食物分出來，送給他們；但便雅憫所得的比別人多五倍。他們就飲酒，和約瑟一同宴樂。

一份份特殊的食物從約瑟的餐桌上送到了他們的面前，表示對他們的重視。約瑟分給便雅憫的上等肉塊比其他人多五倍，以表示對他特別的重視。便雅憫是貴賓。其他古代文獻也記載把最大的和最好的部分送給貴賓以表示尊重（見撒上9:23,24；荷馬史詩《伊利亞德》第七章第321節；第八章第162節；希羅多德，第六章第57節）。約瑟想考驗他的哥哥們，以便發現他們對便雅憫，從而對他自己的真實情感。他希望看出他們是否因其母系出身而嫉恨他們最小的弟弟，就像他們從前嫉妒他自己一樣。
34.en: **Five times.** To honor the men, special servings were brought them from Joseph’s table. To show Benjamin special honor, Joseph sent him choice cuts five times larger than those sent the others. Benjamin was the guest of honor. The custom of showing respect to distinguished guests by giving them the largest and best pieces appears in other ancient records (see 1 Sam. 9:23, 24; Homer Iliad vii. 321; viii. 162; Herodotus vi. 57). Joseph sought to test his brothers that he might discover their real feelings toward Benjamin, and thus toward himself. He desired to see whether they envied and hated their youngest brother on account of his maternity, as they had formerly envied Joseph.

1.zh:
約瑟吩咐家宰說：把糧食裝滿這些人的口袋，儘著他們的驢所能馱的，又把各人的銀子放在各人的口袋裡，

**懷愛倫註釋（1–34節）**。《先祖與先知》229-230。

2.zh:
並將我的銀杯和那少年人糴糧的銀子一同裝在他的口袋裡。家宰就照約瑟所說的話行了；

這是約瑟向其兄弟表明身份之前最後的和決定性的考驗，目的在於造成一種局面，使他能依法將便雅憫扣留在埃及。這樣，他的哥哥們就有理由不帶他們父親最喜愛的兒子返回迦南了。他也就藉此瞭解他們現在是怎樣的人了。他們或者服從約瑟將便雅憫扣留在埃及的決定，而將令人心碎的信息帶給他們的父親，讓他接受失去他所愛之拉結唯一倖存之子的事實，或者他們將盡全力來阻止這一不幸的發生。
2.en: **Put my cup.** This was Joseph’s final and decisive test prior to revealing himself to his brothers. His purpose was to create a situation by which he could legitimately claim the right to retain Benjamin in Egypt, so that his brothers might have an excuse for returning to Canaan without the favorite of their father. By this he would learn beyond a doubt what kind of men they now were. Either they would abide by the decision of Joseph to keep Benjamin in Egypt and return to their father with the heartbreaking message that he must reconcile himself to the loss of the remaining son of his beloved Rachel, or they would do everything in their power to prevent such a misfortune.

5.zh:
這不是我主人飲酒的杯嗎？豈不是他占卜用的嗎？你們這樣行是作惡了。

這個酒杯是個貴重的物品。它不僅用來飲酒，而且據認為可以查出任何有毒物質。這種杯子還可用來行法術。“占卜”的意思是“耳語”、“喃喃而語”、“說預言”。古典作家說到東方人將水倒入酒杯，然後通過觀察預測未來的事（任布利庫，《魔法》第三章第14節）。古人所描述的另一種習俗是將水倒入酒杯中，將一塊塊的金銀或寶石投進去，然後觀察並解釋水中的形像（普林尼《自然歷史》第三十七章第73節；斯特拉波，《地理學》第十六卷第2章第39節）。約瑟吩咐家宰向兄弟們提及行法術的事，並不意味著約瑟真的接受了這種迷信的做法。就像先前一樣（創43:33），他願意讓他們相信他能讀懂他們的思想，從而使他們放棄偽裝吐露真情。
埃及人很可能因為約瑟的大智大慧而認定他能行法術。他難道沒有準確地預言了豐年和荒年，並關照埃及為災荒做準備嗎？他確實比他們最佳的“術士”還要出色（創41:8），因此一定擁有更高明的法術（見出8:19）。他作為一個智士的聲譽可能已經廣為流傳，甚至傳到了外國，以至約瑟後來質問涉嫌盜竊酒杯的人是否瞭解這一事實（創44:15）。
5.en:
**Whereby indeed he divineth.** The goblet was a valuable possession. It was not an ordinary drinking cup, but one, supposedly, capable of detecting any poisonous substance placed in it. Such cups were also used for the practice of magic. The word translated “divineth” means “to whisper,” “to mumble,” “to prophesy.” Classical writers speak of the Oriental practice of pouring water into a goblet and looking into it for representations of future events (Jamblichus De mysteriis iii. 14). Another custom described by the ancients consisted of pouring water into a goblet, dropping in pieces of gold and silver or precious stones, and then observing and interpreting the appearance in the water (Pliny Natural History xxxvii. 73; Strabo Geography xvi. 2. 39). That the steward was ordered to mention the practice of magic to the brothers does not imply that Joseph had actually adopted this superstitious practice himself. As previously (ch. 43:33), he was willing that they should believe he could read their thoughts. This would tend to unnerve them and lead them to abandon pretense.
On account of his great wisdom, the Egyptians probably attributed to Joseph the practice of magic. Had he not accurately predicted the years of plenty and of famine, and taken care that Egypt be prepared for the emergency? He certainly excelled their best “magicians” (ch. 41:8), and must therefore possess superior magic (see Ex. 8:19). Perhaps his fame as a wise man had spread far and wide, even to foreign lands, so that the supposed thieves of the goblet might appropriately be asked whether they were unaware of this fact (Gen. 44:15).

9.zh:
你僕人中無論在誰那裡搜出來，就叫他死，我們也作我主的奴僕。

兄弟們認為自己完全無辜，就毫不遲疑地聲明：如果所丟失的物品在他們當中找到，他們甘願受最嚴厲的處罰。他們鹵莽的話語似乎有欠考慮，特別是經歷過口袋裡神秘地出現銀錢之後。他們本來容易受人懷疑，所以應該更為謹慎。但他們在第二次前往埃及時，受到首長本人及其下屬這麼真誠友善的款待，以致打消了對約瑟動機之誠意的一切懷疑。
9.en: **Let him die.** Conscious of their complete innocence, the brothers did not hesitate to pronounce upon themselves the most severe penalty should the missing object be found with them. Their rash words seem a little foolhardy, particularly after the experience of finding their money mysteriously placed in their sacks. They might have been expected to be suspicious, and consequently somewhat more cautious. However, the unfeigned friendliness with which they had been received and entertained upon their second visit to Egypt, both by the viceroy himself and by his subordinates, had dissipated all doubts concerning the sincerity of Joseph’s intentions.

10.zh:
家宰說：現在就照你們的話行吧！在誰那裡搜出來，誰就作我的奴僕；其餘的都沒有罪。

家宰以冠冕堂皇的語氣，拒絕了將無辜者與罪犯一同受罰的想法，或像他們所建議的那樣嚴厲地處罰罪犯。別人如果信口開河，我們絕不要乘人之危。我們自己可能有時也會作一些的欠考慮的承諾，要不是他人的寛容，可能會給我們帶來傷害。
10.en: **Let it be.** Professing an exalted sense of fairness and justice, the steward declined to think of punishing the innocent with the guilty, or even the guilty as rigorously as they proposed. When others speak rashly we should not take advantage of their rashness. We ourselves may at times make commitments without due deliberation which might bring injury to us, except for the leniency of others.

12.zh:
家宰就搜查，從年長的起到年幼的為止，那杯竟在便雅憫的口袋裡搜出來。

家宰有條不紊的搜查，一定使他們想起一天前發現他們自己按照年齡就座時所產生的詫異。他們一定感到非常緊張，因為丟失的物品直到最後一刻才被找到。他們一個接一個得到洗刷。隨著他們無辜的證據越來越明顯，他們可能以面部的表情，甚至口中的話來表達自己的清白。但最後丟失的物品卻在便雅憫的口袋裡發現了。面對這場新的災難，他們悲痛驚恐地撕裂了他們的衣服（見創37:34註釋），重新讓驢馱上貨物，返回城中。
12.en: **He searched.** The steward’s systematic search must have reminded them of their surprise the day before at finding themselves seated according to age. Also it must have kept them tense, for the lost object was not found until the very last moment of the search. One after another the men found themselves cleared. By facial expression, and perhaps even in words, they may have expressed triumph at the growing evidence of their declared innocence. But then the lost object was found in Benjamin’s sack. With anguish and alarm at this new calamity they rent their clothes (see on ch. 37:34), reloaded their asses, and returned to the city.

13.zh:
他們就撕裂衣服，各人把馱子抬在驢上，回城去了。

現在可以看出在他們的內心深處，是如何看待他們父親最疼愛的兒子的了，就是那位受埃及的首長如此看重的便雅憫。他們會不會像他們當初對待約瑟那樣地放棄他，使他們年邁的父親滿懷悲傷地死去呢，還是願意捨棄自己的自由和生命，以使他能夠平安地回到父親身邊？
13.en: **Returned to the city.** Now it would be seen how they felt in their inmost hearts toward their father’s favorite, who had been so honored by the great man of Egypt. Would they give him up as they had Joseph, and bring their aged father with sorrow to the grave, or would they be ready to surrender their own liberty and lives that he might return in safety to his father?

14.zh:
猶大和他弟兄們來到約瑟的屋中，約瑟還在那裡，他們就在他面前俯伏於地。

這些人在猶大的帶領下回到了約瑟的屋。他們都在他面前俯伏於地請求憐憫。古埃及的浮雕保存了許多類似情景的畫面。其中有一幅展示公元前十四世紀迦南的請願人在哈仁姆哈伯將軍面前的景象。他們中有的平伏在地上，伸出手臂抬起頭向高官懇求。其他的人在他面前跪下或鞠躬。所有的人都舉起胳膊，讓將軍知道他們要求的迫切性。那些伏在哈仁姆哈伯面前的人，請求准許在埃及定居，因為他們被趕出了自己的家園。
14.en: **They fell before him.** With Judah leading the way, the men came to Joseph’s house, where they all fell down before him, pleading for mercy. Several ancient Egyptian reliefs depicting similar situations have been preserved. One shows Canaanite petitioners before the general Haremhab in the 14th century .. Some of them lie flat on the ground, with arms outstretched and heads lifted pleadingly to the high official. Others kneel or bow low before him, all of them with arms raised, to impress the general with the urgency of their request. In the case of those who fell down before Haremhab the request was to be permitted to settle in Egypt, since they had been expelled from their homeland.

15.zh:
約瑟對他們說：你們做的是什麼事呢？你們豈不知像我這樣的人必能占卜嗎？

約瑟嚴厲的話語一定使他們想起第一次來埃及時所受到的待遇。關於約瑟沒有行法術，見第5節註釋。
15.en: **Wot ye not?** Joseph spoke harshly, which must have been reminiscent of the reception accorded them on their first visit to Egypt. On Joseph as not being a practitioner of magic, see on v. 5.

16.zh:
猶大說：我們對我主說什麼呢？還有什麼話可說呢？我們怎能自己表白出來呢？神已經查出僕人的罪孽了。我們與那在他手中搜出杯來的都是我主的奴僕。

第二次來埃及的領隊猶大（創43:8）作為代表走上前來。他並未試圖替自己和他的兄弟們辯護，洗刷他們的嫌疑，而是坦然承認自己有罪。他無疑是指對他們的兄弟約瑟所犯的罪行，這個一直在折磨他們良心的罪（創42:21,22）。對於在旁的埃及人，特別是家宰，猶大這番認罪的話無疑使他們感到詫異，因為他們知道這些人實際上是無辜的。約瑟一定感受到他們心靈的痛苦，覺得那即將宣佈的處罰是他們罪有應得的。猶大提出，他們都留在他們曾一度出賣他們兄弟為奴之地埃及為奴隸，約瑟答覆說，他的裁決將是公正合理的。只留下有罪的人作他的奴隸；其他的人都可以平平安安地回到他們父親那裡去。
16.en: **Judah said.** Judah, the leader of this second mission to Egypt (ch. 43:8), stepped forward as spokesman. He made no attempt to justify himself and his brothers or to clear himself and them from suspicion, but acknowledged freely their guilt. He referred, without doubt, to the crime committed against their brother Joseph, a crime that had been haunting their consciences ever since its perpetration (ch. 42:21, 22). To the Egyptian bystanders, particularly the steward, the words of Judah meant the acknowledgment of their guilt, and this no doubt astonished the Egyptians, since they knew the men were really innocent. Joseph must have felt the anguish of their souls, realizing that they felt the punishment soon to be meted out was deserved. In reply to Judah’s offer that all should remain as slaves in Egypt, where they had once sold their brother into slavery, Joseph declared that his sentence would be mild and just. The guilty one alone should be his slave; the others might go back to their father unharmed and unmolested.

18.zh:
猶大挨近他，說：我主啊，求你容僕人說一句話給我主聽，不要向僕人發烈怒，因為你如同法老一樣。

本章剩下的17節經文記錄了猶大替他兄弟便雅憫求情的話。這段話堪稱希伯來文學的傑作之一，也是世界上最具本色的優秀演講之一。
猶大首先懇請約瑟開恩傾聽。他是在和一位與法老同等的，具有定罪和赦罪大權的人說話。在埃及，國王被視為神，是一切完美之物的典範、擁有人間的最高尊榮。
18.en:
**Judah came near.** The remaining 17 verses of the chapter repeat the speech of Judah on behalf of his brother Benjamin. This speech has appropriately been called one of the masterpieces of Hebrew literary composition, one of the finest specimens of natural eloquence in the world.
**Thou art even as Pharaoh.** Judah’s speech began with a request for a gracious hearing. He was speaking to one who was equal to Pharaoh, with authority to condemn or to pardon. Inasmuch as the monarch of Egypt was considered a god, the paragon of all perfection, the highest honor that might be conferred upon a person was comparison with the monarch.

19.zh:
我主曾問僕人們說：你們有父親有兄弟沒有？

首先，猶大講述了便雅憫被捲入困境的緣由。約瑟曾詢問他們的家事，他們則以實相告，說他們最小的兄弟還在家中。約瑟堅持說他們若不帶他們的兄弟來，藉以證明他的存在，以及他們話語的真實性，就不該貿然返回埃及。猶大的話要比創42章的簡短記錄詳細些，但猶大一定是在準確地複述當初的對話，避免虛構或誇張。
19.en: **My lord asked his servants.** First of all, Judah related how Benjamin happened to become involved in the trouble. Joseph had inquired into their family affairs, and they had truthfully informed him concerning their youngest brother, who was still at home. Joseph had insisted that they should not venture to return to Egypt without their brother, by way of proving his existence and thus the accuracy of their statements. Although some phases of this report relate more than the shorter account of the conversation in ch. 42, Judah must have reported the original conversation accurately, in order to avoid making any untrue or exaggerated statements.

25.zh:
我們的父親說：你們再去給我糴些糧來。

猶大以有禮貌而又確切的話語提醒約瑟：是他的要求導致了便雅憫來埃及。他接著以既感人又形象的語言描述了他們年邁之父對其晚年所生之子的疼愛，以及當他們告訴他沒有便雅憫他們就不能返回埃及時，他心中的悲傷。他說他們的父親在經過一番劇烈的掙扎之後最終允許他同去時所懷有的強烈憂慮。他強調他們若不帶回這年輕人的話，就會使他們的父親白髮蒼蒼、悲悲慘慘的下到陰間去了（見創37:35）。
25.en: **Our father said.** After having reminded Joseph in courteous but definite terms that his demands were the cause of Benjamin’s presence in Egypt, he proceeded to depict in affectionate and effective words the love of their aged father for the son of his old age, and his grief when they informed him that they might not return to Egypt without Benjamin. He related the intense anxiety with which, after a severe struggle, their father had finally permitted him to come. He emphasized the sober fact that they would bring down the gray hairs of their father with sorrow to the grave (see ch. 37:35), should they return without the youth.

27.zh:
你僕人─我父親對我們說：你們知道我的妻子給我生了兩個兒子。

第一次用這樣的說法，表明雅各對拉結的感情，超過利亞、闢拉、和悉帕（見創46:19）。她一直是他心中所愛。
27.en: **Ye know that my wife.** This remark, made here for the first time, implies that Jacob regarded Rachel more as his actual wife than Leah, Bilhah, or Zilpah (see ch. 46:19). She was ever the wife of his affections.

28.zh:
一個離開我出去了；我說他必是被撕碎了，直到如今我也沒有見他。

雅各的意思是如果約瑟還活著，肯定會回來或捎信回來。自從約瑟離開希伯侖的那個不幸的日子起，雅各就再也沒見過他。他只能得出結論：他的擔心被完全證實了。
28.en: **Surely he is torn.** Jacob meant here that Joseph, had he been alive, would certainly have been able to return himself or to send word. Never having seen him since that fateful day of his departure from Hebron, Jacob could only conclude that his fears were fully justified.

33.zh:
現在求你容僕人住下，替這童子作我主的奴僕，叫童子和他哥哥們一同上去。

猶大的捨己確實是值得稱讚的。為了不使年邁的父親悲傷和痛苦，他甘願代替更受父親眷愛的兄弟為奴，這種精神是極為可貴的。猶大的忘我境界，很少有人達到，從未有人超過。猶大在這裡表顯為一個真心悔改了的人，配得上擔任所應許之後裔的祖先，把他的名字賦予上帝的選民。
約瑟再也不懷疑他哥哥們的徹底悔改了，特別是當初慫恿把約瑟賣掉的猶大。約瑟的策略取得了完全的成功。他現在已經知道了兄弟的態度，並且滿意他們的真心悔改。沒有必要進一步考驗他們了。他打算亮明自己的身份。
33.en:
**Instead of the lad.** Judah’s self-sacrifice is certainly deserving of praise. Voluntary submission to servitude on behalf of a brother who enjoyed a higher degree of parental affection, in order to save his aged father fresh sorrow and anguish, cannot be overestimated. Judah’s self-forgetful magnanimity has never been surpassed, and but seldom equaled. Judah emerges here as a truly converted man, a worthy ancestor of the promised seed, and worthy to give his name to the chosen people of God.
Joseph could no longer doubt that a complete change had come over his brothers, and over Judah in particular, since the day when he had so eloquently urged the sale of Joseph into slavery. Joseph’s tactics had proved eminently successful. He was now convinced regarding the attitude of his brothers, and satisfied that their conversion was genuine. There was no further need to test them, and he was therefore ready to reveal his identity.

1.zh:
約瑟進去告訴法老說：我的父親和我的弟兄帶著羊群牛群，並一切所有的，從迦南地來了，如今在歌珊地。

**懷愛倫註釋（1–31節）**。《先祖與先知》233-234。

2.zh:
約瑟從他弟兄中挑出五個人來，引他們去見法老。

約瑟原已通知法老其家人來到歌珊的消息。他帶了五個兄弟來見國王。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–4節）**。《先祖與先知》233。
2.en: **Took some of his brethren.** Having previously informed Pharaoh of the arrival of his relatives in Goshen, Joseph presented five of his brothers to the king. The Hebrew expression correctly translated “some of his brethren” in the KJV was misunderstood by earlier commentators, who gave unwarranted interpretations of it. It is simply a Hebrew idiom meaning “out of the whole number of his brothers.”

6.zh:
埃及地都在你面前，只管叫你父親和你弟兄住在國中最好的地；他們可以住在歌珊地。你若知道他們中間有什麼能人，就派他們看管我的牲畜。

他們來到這裡寄居（沒有定居），因為旱災使他們在迦南地失去了牧養羊群的草場。於是國王批准約瑟將全國最好的地區，即歌珊地給他父親和兄弟居住。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》233，241，《救贖的故事》104；《證言》卷五189。
6.en: **The land of Egypt is before thee.** They had come to sojourn in the land (not to settle there) because there was no pasture for their flocks in the land of Canaan, owing to the drought. The king then authorized Joseph to give his father and brothers a dwelling in the best part of the country, the land of Goshen.

7.zh:
約瑟領他父親雅各進到法老面前，雅各就給法老祝福。

約瑟得到國王定居歌珊地區的許可之後就領他父親到法老那裡。有人認為約瑟兄弟的參見是公務性的，而雅各與君主的會晤則屬私人性質。可能是國王提出要會見首相的父親。
**雅各就給法老祝福。**雅各沒有按照常規向法老致敬，如稱“願王萬歲！”（撒下16:16；王上1:25；但2:4等）。他意識到自己作為耶和華之先知的尊嚴，向國王宣告了屬天的祝福。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》233。
7.en:
**Joseph brought in Jacob.** Joseph then presented his father to Pharaoh, once royal permission had already been given for settling in the region of Goshen. It has been suggested that the interview granted Joseph’s brothers was of an official nature, whereas Jacob’s audience with the monarch was of a purely private character. The king may have requested the opportunity of meeting the father of his first minister.
**Jacob blessed Pharaoh.** Jacob did not extend to Pharaoh the customary salutation accorded kings, such as, “May the king live forever!” (2 Sam. 16:16; 1 Kings 1:25; Dan. 2:4; etc.). Conscious of his own dignity as a prophet of Jehovah, Jacob pronounced upon him a heavenly benediction.

9.zh:
雅各對法老說：我寄居在世的年日是一百三十歲，我平生的年日又少又苦，不及我列祖在世寄居的年日。

雅各稱自己和父親的一生為“寄居在世”。他們沒有實際佔有迦南，而是在應許之地漂泊，無固定居所，也無家可歸。這象徵著屬世生活的多變和辛勞。人們從中得不到上帝造他時要他得到的、他的心靈所不斷渴求的真安息（見來4:8,9）。保羅將雅各的這番話正確理解為先祖渴望屬天迦南的永恆安息（來11:13-16）。
**一百三十歲。**約瑟任職時是三十歲（創41:46）。經過去了七個豐年（創41:47-49）和兩個荒年（創45:6），現在他已經三十九歲了，而他的父親是一百三十歲。據此我們得知約瑟是在他父親九十一歲時出生的。那是在雅各寄居巴旦亞蘭的第十四年末（創30:25），所以雅各剛到那裡時一定是七十七歲。
**又少又苦。**與其先輩相比，雅各對自己一生的評價是十分準確的。亞伯拉罕活到一百七十五歲，以撒活到一百八十歲。他們都沒有經歷過像他那樣漂泊不定，飽經風霜，充滿痛苦危險、患難煎熬的人生。從逃往哈蘭到遷居埃及，他的一生不過是一連串的苦難（創42:36）。
9.en:
**The years of my pilgrimage.** Jacob referred to his own life and that of his father as a “pilgrimage.” They had not come into actual possession of Canaan, but had been obliged to wander about, unsettled and homeless, in the land promised them as an inheritance. This “pilgrimage” was at the same time a figurative representation of the inconsistency and weariness of the earthly life, in which man does not attain to that true rest for which he was created and for which his soul continually longs (see Heb. 4:8, 9). Paul could therefore appropriately regard these words of Jacob as a declaration of the yearning of the patriarchs for the eternal rest of the heavenly Canaan (Heb. 11:13–16).
**An hundred and thirty years.** Joseph had been 30 years old at the time of his appointment to office (Gen. 41:46), and since that time the 7 plentiful years (ch. 41:47–49) and 2 years of famine had passed (ch. 45:6). Now he had reached the age of 39, and his father was 130 years of age. It is evident from these figures that Joseph was born when his father was 91 years old. Since his birth occurred at the close of Jacob’s 14 years of residence in Padan-aram (ch. 30:25), the patriarch’s age upon arrival there must have been 77.
**Few and evil.** Jacob’s evaluation of his life was only too true when compared with that of his fathers. Abraham had lived to be 175 years old, and Isaac 180. Neither had led so uncertain a life, so full of distress and danger, of tribulation and anguish, as had Jacob. From his flight to Haran to the time of his removal to Egypt, his life had been nothing but one long succession of troubles (ch. 42:36).

11.zh:
約瑟遵著法老的命，把埃及國最好的地，就是蘭塞境內的地，給他父親和弟兄居住，作為產業。

對此批評聖經的學者有兩種觀點。有人認為這充分證明關於以色列人在埃及定居的地點還存在不同的說法，因為此前一直都說是歌珊（第1,6節）。其他學者認為這說明以色列人在埃及的年代是拉美西斯王朝。拉美西斯王朝是於公元前1320年開始掌權的。第一種觀點是不可接受的，因為摩西是《創世記》的唯一作者。這是一部歷史而不是一部傳說集。第二種觀點也不能接受，因為會給舊約故事中這一部分年代造成混亂。因此“蘭塞境內的地”應理解為“歌珊地”後來的新名。這種說法也體現了某個抄寫者為了讓讀者確認“歌珊”所做的努力。同樣，我們都知道紐約是荷蘭人所建造的，當時叫新阿姆斯特丹。但現在我們只能稱之為紐約，因為新阿姆斯特丹這個名稱對於大多數的現代讀者來說已不具有任何意義了。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《救贖的故事》 104。
11.en: **The land of Rameses.** Two views concerning this statement are held by critical scholars. According to some, it constitutes strong evidence for a variant tradition regarding the settlement of the Israelites in Egypt, inasmuch as the land has thus far been called Goshen (vs. 1, 6). Others have drawn the conclusion that it indicates the time when the children of Israel were in Egypt as that of the Ramessides. The first Ramses began to reign in 1320 .. The first argument is unacceptable because Moses was sole author of Genesis, and the book is a historical narrative and not a collection of traditions. Neither can the second argument be accepted, for it would bring chronological confusion to this section of the OT narrative. It must therefore be assumed that the term “land of Rameses” was a later name for the older term “and of Goshen,” and accordingly represents the effort of a copyist to identify “Goshen” for his readers. By the same procedure we might say today that New York was founded by the Dutch, although the city they founded was known as New Amsterdam. Our statement would nevertheless be considered not only correct but even desirable, for the name New Amsterdam would have no meaning for many modern readers.

12.zh:
約瑟用糧食奉養他父親和他弟兄，並他父親全家的眷屬，都是照各家的人口奉養他們。

**照各家的人口。**直譯為“照孩子們的口”。有些註釋家認為這是指約瑟象父親對孩子一樣供養他的親人。還有的註釋家認為這指的是所有的人從最老的到最小的都得到了供養。鑑於以後五年的饑荒給埃及和迦南的居民帶來的痛苦，約瑟對於其家人的好處就越發明顯了。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–24節）**。《先祖與先知》241。
12.en: **According to their families.** Literally, “according to the mouth of the little ones.” It probably means “in proportion to the size of their families.” Some commentators, however, have thought that it refers to Joseph as providing food for his relatives as a father would for his offspring, and others, that it means all were fed, from the greatest to the least. The benefits Joseph was in a position to confer upon his family become all the more apparent from the description of the distress into which the inhabitants of Egypt and Canaan were plunged by the continuation of the famine for five years more.

13.zh:
饑荒甚大，全地都絕了糧，甚至埃及地和迦南地的人因那饑荒的緣故都餓昏了。

本節開始描述埃及因嚴重的饑荒而面臨的社會大變革。饑荒已使整個國家處於赤貧狀態。
13.en: **Fainted.** This verse introduces a great social revolution forced upon Egypt by the stern necessity of famine, which had by now reduced the entire nation to a state of utter misery.

16.zh:
約瑟說：若是銀子用盡了，可以把你們的牲畜給我，我就為你們的牲畜給你們糧食。

歸於法老的牲畜可能由原來的主人照料。因此這些條件並不象表面看來那樣苛刻。捱餓的人不會指望從飢餓和垂死的畜群那裡獲得任何利益。他們現在需要為他們的牲畜領取飼料，並且可能從它們身上獲得部分收益，就像次年他們的土地和出產一樣（見第23,24節）。
16.en: **Give your cattle.** The animals that thus became Pharaoh’s property were probably left in the care of their owners. These terms, therefore, were not so severe as it would appear. A famishing people could expect no profit from starving cattle and dying herds. Now they were to receive fodder for their animals, and probably enjoy a partial profit on them, by analogy to what happened to their land and its produce the next year (see vs. 23, 24).

17.zh:
於是他們把牲畜趕到約瑟那裡，約瑟就拿糧食換了他們的牛、羊、驢、馬；那一年因換他們一切的牲畜，就用糧食養活他們。

馬在埃及的存在證明約瑟的故事不可能發生在希克索斯時代以前，因為直到希克索斯人把馬引進埃及，人們才知道什麼是馬（見創41:43註釋）。
**那一年。**我們不知道這是指七個荒年中的哪一年。有些註釋家認為向農民發放種子（第23節）是饑荒的第七年，以牲畜換食物則是在第六年。但可能有些農作物在整個荒年期間一直在尼羅河岸邊的田地裡種植，所以第23,24節中所提到的種子，不能作為這是最後一年的證據。儘管如此，第17節所指的很可能是饑荒的後期。
17.en:
**For horses.** The existence of horses in Egypt proves that the Joseph narrative may not be dated earlier than the Hyksos period, since the horse was unknown there until the Hyksos introduced it (see on ch. 41:43).
**For that year.** It is not certain which of the seven years of famine is here meant. Some commentators think that the distribution of seed to farmers the following year (v. 23) shows that that was the seventh year of the famine, and the year in which the cattle were exchanged for food consequently the sixth year. However, it is probable that some planting had been carried on during all the years of famine in fields bordering on the Nile, which would render the reference to seed in vs. 23, 24 of no value as evidence that the last year is here meant. Nevertheless, the year referred to in v. 17 probably fell in the latter part of the period of famine.

18.zh:
那一年過去，第二年他們又來見約瑟，說：我們不瞞我主，我們的銀子都花盡了，牲畜也都歸了我主。我們在我主眼前，除了我們的身體和田地之外，一無所剩。

就是在他們的錢都用完後的第二年，而不是饑荒的第二年。
18.en: **The second year.** That is, the second year after their money was gone, not the second year of famine.

19.zh:
你何忍見我們人死地荒呢？求你用糧食買我們和我們的地，我們和我們的地就要給法老效力。又求你給我們種子，使我們得以存活，不致死亡，地土也不致荒涼。

他們覺得做法老的農奴要比自由但捱餓要好得多，他們認為這樣做對他們自己和國王都是有利的。填飽的肚子要比捱餓幸福得多。
雖然我們沒有任何聖經以外的同時代文獻來證實聖經有關此饑荒的記載，但事實是：在希克索斯人被趕出埃及以後，埃及的國王擁有一切非宗教的財產。這在希克索斯人來到埃及之前是不可能的。在希克索斯入侵埃及之前，大部分國土都是由臣民擁有的，控制在大小地主的手中。關於希克索斯人統治時期的狀況，沒有任何記錄保留至今。但該時期結束後，又出現紀念碑揭示當時的景況時，人們發現所有的土地以及幾乎埃及所有其他的財產都為國王和祭司所獨佔。對於埃及社會結構的這一鉅變，最佳的解釋就是聖經有關約瑟在七個荒年中所採取之措施的記載。
19.en:
**Buy us and our land.** Realizing that their lot as Pharaoh’s serfs would be preferable to that of free but starving citizens, they considered this solution advantageous to themselves as well as to the king. A full stomach was a far happier prospect than starvation.
Although no contemporary non-Biblical records have survived to corroborate the Bible account of the famine, the fact remains that the kings of Egypt enjoyed sole possession of all nonecclesiastical properties after the expulsion of the Hyksos, a situation that did not exist before their arrival. Prior to the Hyksos invasion of Egypt a great proportion of the land was owned by the people, being in the hands of large and small landowners. Concerning conditions during the Hyksos period no records exist, but when that period ended and the monuments began to shed light on the existing situation once more, it is found that all lands and practically all the other property of Egypt had become the monopoly of the crown and the priesthood. The best explanation for this radical change in the social structure of the nation is the Biblical record of Joseph’s administrative measures during the seven years of famine.

21.zh:
至於百姓，約瑟叫他們，從埃及這邊直到埃及那邊，都各歸各城。

這句話似乎是說約瑟按照糧食儲藏的城市來分佈或安排國家的人口，將他們安置在城中或在這些城市的附近。但希臘文七十士譯本和拉丁文通行本可能更準確地反映了原文的意思：“他使百姓被奴役成為他的奴僕”。
21.en: **He removed them to cities.** This statement is an accurate translation of the Hebrew text as we know it today. It seems to mean that Joseph distributed, or organized, the population of the land according to the cities in which grain was stored, placing them either in the cities or in their immediate vicinity. However, the LXX and the Vulgate may reflect the original more accurately: “He brought the people into bondage to him for servants.” Since the Hebrew text presumably underlying these early translations would represent the exchange of but two very similar Hebrew letters, the equivalents of d and r, and the addition of another letter, b, it is possible that the LXX and the Vulgate are closer to the original text. Their rendition certainly seems more appropriate to the context. Until the recovery of an ancient Hebrew text of this passage may decide the problem one way or the other, however, it is best to withhold judgment.

22.zh:
惟有祭司的地，約瑟沒有買，因為祭司有從法老所得的常俸。他們吃法老所給的常俸，所以他們不賣自己的地。

祭司是埃及社會中最有影響力和最強大的階層。沒有一個法老曾永久打破他們的勢力，只有少數的幾位法老敢於得罪或觸怒他們。埃及的全部財富一半以上都在祭司的手中。他們在埃及的整個古代歷史中都是免稅的。甚至連希克索斯的國王也不敢公開與祭司對抗，儘管他們大都不敬拜埃及的神。約瑟個人並不認同埃及的祭司，但他很聰明，不去觸動長期確立的祭司特權，從而保證了他們對公共開支的支持。
22.en: **The land of the priests.** The priests formed a most influential and powerful segment of Egyptian society. No Pharaoh ever succeeded in permanently breaking their power, and very few dared to arouse their hatred or even lose their good will. More than half of all the wealth of Egypt was in the hands of the priests. They were tax-exempt throughout Egypt’s ancient history. Even the Hyksos kings did not openly fight the priesthood, though in general they did not worship the national gods. Joseph, who personally did not sympathize with the Egyptian priests, was wise enough not to interfere with the long-established priestly privileges, which guaranteed their support at public expense.

24.zh:
後來打糧食的時候，你們要把五分之一納給法老，四分可以歸你們做地裡的種子，也做你們和你們家口孩童的食物。

在七個豐年中徵收百分之二十作為特殊的措施，因為出產的豐富並沒有成為過重的負擔。此後，這將成為永久的稅率，因為全國的土地都已成了國王的財產。
24.en: **Ye shall give the fifth part.** The levy of 20 per cent collected during the 7 plentiful years, as an exceptional measure, had not seemed an excessive burden because of the tremendous amount of produce. Henceforth it was to be perpetuated as the regular tax rate, inasmuch as all lands had become the property of the crown.

25.zh:
他們說：你救了我們的性命。但願我們在我主眼前蒙恩，我們就作法老的僕人。

百姓的感謝說明新政策並未被視為苛刻或不公正的。這是充分證明指控約瑟剝奪了埃及人的自由，並將自由人變為奴隸的說法是錯誤的。奴隸主通常不會滿足於徵收財產總收入的百分之二十。除了稅收以外，國王對土地的佔有多半是名義上的而不是實際上的。百姓自己並不覺得稅收過高。他們因能活生命並保留對其牲畜、房屋和土地的使用而感激不盡，儘管這一切在名義上都歸屬於法老。
25.en: **Saved our lives.** This acknowledgment by the people shows clearly that the new regulation was not considered harsh or unjust. It is an adequate refutation of the oft-repeated charge that Joseph despoiled the Egyptians of their liberties and reduced a free people to slavery. Slave-owners are usually not content with a tax of 20 per cent on the gross income of their estates. Except for the tax, royal ownership of the lands was more nominal than real. At all events, the tax was not considered exorbitant by the people themselves. They were grateful to be able to remain alive and to retain the use of their animals, houses, and lands, even though it be under the nominal lordship of Pharaoh.

27.zh:
以色列人住在埃及的歌珊地。他們在那裡置了產業，並且生育甚多。

雅各的家族住在肥沃的地區，得到約瑟的充足供養（第12節），難怪他們享受到一段前所未有的繁榮時期。結果不僅財富積累了，而且人口也急劇增長。上帝在別是巴對雅各的應許這時開始應驗了（創46:3）。
27.en: **Multiplied exceedingly.** Since Jacob’s family lived in a fertile region and were amply supplied by Joseph (v. 12), it is not astonishing that they enjoyed an unprecedented period of prosperity. The result was not only an accumulation of wealth but also a rapid increase in population. Thus began the fulfillment of the promise made by God to Jacob at Beersheba (ch. 46:3).

28.zh:
雅各住在埃及地十七年，雅各平生的年日是一百四十七歲。

這幾節經文和以後的幾章講述了先祖雅各臨終前的景況。他在迦南生活了七十七年，在巴旦亞蘭生活了二十年，回到迦南又生活了三十三年，最後在埃及生活了十七年，共活了一百四十七歲。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》233。
28.en: **Seventeen years.** In these verses and in the following chapters the patriarch Jacob’s last days are described. He had lived 77 years in Canaan, 20 in Padan-aram, 33 more in Canaan, and finally 17 in Egypt, in all 147 years.

29.zh:
以色列的死期臨近了，他就叫了他兒子約瑟來，說：我若在你眼前蒙恩，請你把手放在我大腿底下，用慈愛和誠實待我，請你不要將我葬在埃及。

關於這一古老習俗，見創24:2註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（29–30節）**。《先祖與先知》234。
29.en: **Thy hand under my thigh.** Concerning this ancient custom, see on ch. 24:2.

30.zh:
我與我祖我父同睡的時候，你要將我帶出埃及，葬在他們所葬的地方。約瑟說：我必遵著你的命而行。

雖然雅各的要求部分是由於對祖先安葬之地深深的眷戀，但主要還是因為他堅信迦南是以色列真正的產業。他知道他的後代終將返回應許之地，作為他們永久的家鄉，他也知道埃及只是他們在危難之時一個臨時的避難所。
30.en: **Bury me.** Though Jacob’s request was due in part to a deep-seated attachment to the ground where his ancestors lay buried, it was chiefly inspired by clear faith that Canaan was the true inheritance of Israel. He knew that his descendants would eventually return to the Land of Promise as their permanent home, and that Egypt offered them but a temporary refuge for the time of their necessity.

31.zh:
雅各說：你要向我起誓。約瑟就向他起了誓，於是以色列在床頭上【或作扶著杖頭】敬拜神。

公元前三世紀希臘文七十士譯本的猶太翻譯家因為拼寫的關係將mth（“床”）理解為mattah（“杖”），故譯為：“以色列扶著杖頭敬拜”。由於在向上帝敬拜時扶著杖頭要比轉身在床頭上更符合雅各的年齡和病體，而且來11:21也採用了希臘文七十士譯本的譯法，故後一種譯法可能更接近原意，也是更為準確。不論先祖採用了何種姿勢，都是懷著感恩崇敬向上帝傾心吐意。
31.en: **Upon the bed’s head.** This is an accurate translation of the Hebrew text as vocalized by the Jewish scholars, the Masoretes, in the 7th century of our era. The Jewish translators of the LXX of the 3d century .., however, whose Hebrew text contained no vowels, took the word mṭh, vocalized by the Masoretes as miṭṭah, “bed,” to be maṭṭah, “staff.” Accordingly, they translated the passage, “Israel bowed himself on the top of his staff.” Since the action of leaning on his staff while doing obeisance to God would be quite as suitable to Jacob’s age and infirmity as turning over and bowing on the head of his bed, and inasmuch as Heb. 11:21 reflects the LXX reading of Gen. 47:31, the latter is probably closer to the meaning of the original than the extant vocalized Hebrew text, and therefore preferable. Whatever the exact position of the patriarch, it was a posture of devotion in which he poured out his soul in grateful adoration to God.

1.zh:
約瑟伏在他父親的面上哀哭，與他親嘴。

約瑟無疑合上了他親愛父親的眼睛，正如上帝所應許的（創46:4）。本段只描述約瑟的悲傷，並不意味著其他兒子沒有為父親的去世而傷心。他們的悲傷可能表現得不象約瑟那樣明顯。因為約瑟的心特別容易受親情的影響。約瑟的悲傷代表了所有人的悲傷，而且我們可以想像他們的悲傷同樣也是十分真切的。
1.en: **Joseph fell upon his father’s face.** Joseph had no doubt closed the eyes of his beloved father, as God had promised (ch. 46:4). That only Joseph’s grief is described in this passage does not imply that the other sons did not sorrow for their father. Perhaps their grief was less demonstrative than that of Joseph, since the heart of Joseph appears to have been peculiarly susceptible to tender emotions. The grief of Joseph is representative of the grief of all, and we may assume that their sorrow was just as real.

2.zh:
約瑟吩咐伺候他的醫生用香料薰他父親，醫生就用香料薰了以色列。

希羅多德（第二卷第86章）和狄奧多羅（第一卷第91章）描述了古埃及人用香料薰屍的方法。他們描述的準確性基本上被古埃及的文獻和對木乃伊的檢驗所證實。這一工藝非常的昂貴，高達一千美金。首先彎曲的金屬管把腦汁從鼻孔中吸出，然後用藥水徹底清除顱腔內任何殘餘部分。用一把鋒利的刀切開腹腔，將內臟取出來分別放在各個罐子裡。這些罐子被稱為天篷罐。用棕櫚酒和一種由各種香料泡製的溶液洗淨腹腔，然後填滿各種香料。切開的口子縫合之後，填滿香料的屍體將在鹼液中浸泡多日（多達70天）。然後洗淨屍體，用麻布壽衣包裹，塗上樹膠，最後繪上已故者的相貌特徵。
2.en: **Embalmed Israel.** The ancient Egyptian method of embalming has been described, both by Herodotus (ii. 86) and by Diodorus (i. 91). The accuracy of their descriptions has been confirmed in the main by ancient Egyptian documents and by an examination of the mummies themselves. The process was expensive, costing as much as $1,000. The brain was first extracted through the nostrils by means of a crooked piece of metal, and the skull was then thoroughly cleansed of any remaining portions by rinsing it with drugs. Through an opening in the left side made with a sharp knife, the viscera were removed and placed in separate jars, the so-called canopic jars. The empty abdomen was purified with palm wine and an infusion of aromatics, and then filled with various spices. After the opening had been sewed up, the stuffed form was submerged for many days (up to 70) in a bath of natron solution. Then it was washed, wrapped in a linen shroud, smeared over with gum, and finally painted to resemble the natural features of the deceased.

3.zh:
薰屍的常例是四十天；那四十天滿了，埃及人為他哀哭了七十天。

根據埃及的文獻，從一個人的去世到安葬，時間各有不同。有時薰屍需要十六天，裹屍三十五天，安葬七十天，共一百二十一天；有時薰屍需要六十六天，準備安葬四天，安葬本身二十六天，一共九十六天。在另一處，我們得知薰屍需要長達七十或八十天，安葬十個月（見E·A·W·布治，《木乃伊》）。時間的長短在於已故者家族的貧富以及所處埃及的歷史時期。雅各作為宰相的父親，得到了當時最好的待遇。他的薰屍持續了四十天，為他的安葬所做的準備又花了七十天。這是所宣佈正式的哀悼時期。
3.en: **Forty days.** It is known from Egyptian documents that the length of the period from the death of a man to his burial varied. In one case the embalming occupied 16 days, the bandaging 35 days, and the burial 70 days, 121 days in all. In another case the embalming occupied 66 days, preparations for burial 4 days, and the burial itself 26 days, in all 96 days. Elsewhere we are told that the embalming lasted for 70 or 80 days, and the burial 10 months (see E. A. W. Budge, The Mummy). The time involved depended upon the wealth of the family of the deceased and the period of Egyptian history. Jacob, being the father of the prime minister, received the best care of the time. His embalming continued for 40 days, and the preparations for his burial another 70 days. This was proclaimed an official period of mourning.

4.zh:
為他哀哭的日子過了，約瑟對法老家中的人說：我若在你們眼前蒙恩，請你們報告法老說：

註釋家們一直在推測，約瑟為什麼在哀悼期結束後沒有親自向國王提出請求，而是通過他的侍臣。沒有人知道他這種看似奇怪之做法的原因，但這在當時可能是很正常的。有人說約瑟這樣做是尊重侍臣，為得到他們的好感。可能約瑟是通過祭司報告國王的，因為祭司與死者的埋葬直接有關。也有可能約瑟伴根據哀悼的習俗留起了鬍子和頭髮，因此在剃淨鬚髮之前不能來到國王面前。有些人說約瑟的權柄在饑荒結束之後受到了限制，或另一位對約瑟不太友善的法老作了王。這些說法都是沒有根據的。埃及人都哀悼雅各的去世。如果約瑟的名望降低了，就不會這樣。而且約瑟通過第三者接近國王的做法，很可能是遵照東方人通過中間人辦理重要個人事務的習慣。
4.en: **The house of Pharaoh.** It has been a matter of conjecture among commentators why Joseph, at the end of this period of mourning, did not place his request before the king personally, rather than through other courtiers. His reasons for this apparently strange procedure are unknown, but it may have been perfectly normal in his time. Some have suggested that Joseph did so in recognition of the courtiers and to earn their good will. Perhaps the men through whom Joseph addressed the king were priests, and as such directly concerned with the interment of the dead. It is possible that Joseph, having allowed his beard and hair to grow, incident to the customs of mourning, could not enter the king’s presence without first being shaved. The suggestion made by some, that Joseph’s authority had been restricted after the famine, or that another Pharaoh who was less friendly to Joseph had come to the throne, is without foundation. Jacob’s death was mourned by the Egyptians, and this would not have been the case had the popularity of Joseph waned. Again, Joseph’s procedure of approaching the king through mediaries may have been due to nothing more than the Oriental tendency to transact important personal business through a middleman.

5.zh:
我父親要死的時候叫我起誓說：你要將我葬在迦南地，在我為自己所掘的墳墓裡。現在求你讓我上去葬我父親，以後我必回來。

有人說，雅各稱自己挖掘了埋葬他祖父亞伯拉罕的墳墓，與創23章的記載相矛盾。然而我們沒有必要推定雅各說自己做了亞伯拉罕所做的事情。雅各既可能擴大了原先的麥比拉洞以安放更多的屍體，也有可能預備了他自己想用的墓穴。或者約瑟只是用這句話告訴法老，葬禮不會在埃及舉行，而是在迦南舉行，因此需要得到批准。
5.en: **In my grave.** Jacob’s claim to have dug the tomb in which his grandfather Abraham had been interred, has been criticized as a contradiction of facts presented in ch. 23. However, it is not necessary to assume that Jacob here attributed to himself what had really been done by Abraham. Jacob may either have enlarged the original cave at Machpelah to make room for additional bodies or prepared in it the special niche he intended to occupy. Or, the expression may simply be Joseph’s way of informing Pharaoh that the burial would not take place in Egypt, but in Canaan, and that therefore permission was requested to go thither.

7.zh:
於是約瑟上去葬他父親。與他一同上去的，有法老的臣僕和法老家中的長老，並埃及國的長老，

國王批准以後，一大群人將屍體送回迦南。與約瑟同去的有宮廷的主要官員和家族的全體成員。可能還有一大隊戰車和騎兵保護他們穿越沙漠進入迦南異鄉。埃及官員們的隆重護送部分是因為約瑟在埃及的顯赫地位，部分是因為埃及人喜歡參加這樣的葬禮。
7.en: **Joseph went up.** The king’s permission having been granted, the corpse was carried to Canaan, attended by a large company. With Joseph, there went up the leading officers of the court, together with all members of the family. As an escort through the desert and into the foreign land of Canaan, a large company of chariots and horsemen probably accompanied them. The splendid retinue of Egyptian officers may be explained, in part, from the esteem in which Joseph was held in Egypt and, in part, from the fondness of the Egyptians for such funeral processions.

10.zh:
他們到了約但河外、亞達的禾場，就在那裡大大地號咷痛哭。約瑟為他父親哀哭了七天。

**約但河外。**送葬的隊伍沒有選擇最短的路線，經迦薩穿過非利士地，也沒有經過別是巴，而是繞過死海。我們不知道他們為什麼選擇這條迂迴的較長路線，這可能是出於政治的原因。我們對希克索斯時代埃及與巴勒斯坦之間的關係所知甚少，南巴勒斯坦局勢的不穩定可能導致約瑟選擇了這一條到希伯侖的不尋常路線。
**亞達的禾場。**禾場是一大塊用牛來碾穀子的空地，能容納隨約瑟而來的大隊人馬。亞達可能是主人的名字，也可能指這裡長滿了王紫萁，因為希伯來文`atad就是王紫萁。
**他們就在那裡大大地號咷痛哭。**在古埃及陵墓中的浮雕和壁畫顯示埃及人為死者進行的公開哀悼非常激情和狂熱。他們撕裂衣袍、捶胸、在頭上揚灰和土，並隨著去掉響片的小手鼓發出的樂聲吟唱出殯曲。
10.en:
**The threshingfloor of Atad.** The threshing floor was a large open area for the trampling out of grain by oxen, and was most convenient for the accommodation of a large body of people such as accompanied Joseph. Atad was either the name of the owner or, since ’aṭad is the Hebrew name for buckthorn, it may have indicated that buckthorn grew abundantly.
**Beyond Jordan.** The funeral procession did not take the shortest route, by Gaza, through the country of the Philistines, nor through Beersheba, but around the Dead Sea. The reasons for this long detour are unknown, but may have been political. Very little is known of the general relations between Egypt and Palestine during the period of the Hyksos, and a state of insecurity in southern Palestine may have been responsible for the extraordinary route Joseph took to reach Hebron.
**There they mourned.** Sculptured reliefs and painted murals in ancient Egyptian tombs reveal that the Egyptians were very demonstrative and vehement in their public lamentations for the dead. They rent their garments, beat their breasts, threw dust and mud on their heads, and chanted funeral hymns to the music of a tambourine from which the tinkling plates had been removed.

11.zh:
迦南的居民見亞達禾場上的哀哭，就說：這是埃及人一場極大的哀哭。因此那地方名叫亞伯麥西，是在約但河東。

出殯的隊伍在亞達（第10節）的禾場停留了七天，作為哀悼的一個特別時期。在此期間，當地的居民對埃及人為他們的高官父親的哀哭留下了深刻的印象。這一不尋常的事件使迦南人稱那地方為亞伯麥西，即“埃及的草場”。該詞`abel（草場）與`ebel（哀哭）具有相同的輔音，故一語雙關。
11.en: **The name of it.** When the procession made a halt of seven days at the threshing floor of Atad (v. 10), for a special mourning, the inhabitants of the surrounding countryside were much impressed by the way the Egyptians mourned the father of one of their dignitaries. This unusual event was the reason the Canaanites of that region called the place Abel-mizraim, the “meadow of Egypt.” This name represents a play on the words “mourning,” ’ebel, and “meadow,” ’abel, both having the same consonants.

13.zh:
把他搬到迦南地，葬在幔利前、麥比拉田間的洞裡；那洞和田是亞伯拉罕向赫人以弗崙買來為業，作墳地的。

埃及人似乎留在了亞達的禾場，只有約瑟和他的兄弟們前往迦南，在希伯侖的麥比拉洞安葬了他們的父親。關於這個安葬地點的歷史，見創23章註釋。
13.en: **His sons carried him.** It seems that the Egyptians remained at the threshing floor of Atad, while Joseph and his brothers proceeded alone to Canaan for the burial of their father, in the cave of Machpelah at Hebron. For the history of this burial place, see on chapter 23.

14.zh:
約瑟葬了他父親以後，就和眾弟兄，並一切同他上去葬他父親的人，都回埃及去了。

雅各的後代在迦南永久定居的時候還沒有來到。他們必須先成為“一個大族”（創46:3）。
14.en: **Joseph returned.** The time had not yet arrived for the descendants of Jacob to settle permanently in Canaan. They were first to become “a great nation” (ch. 46:3).

15.zh:
約瑟的哥哥們見父親死了，就說：或者約瑟懷恨我們，照著我們從前待他一切的惡足足地報復我們。

**懷愛倫註釋（15–26節）**。《先祖與先知》239-240。

16.zh:
他們就打發人去見約瑟，說：你父親未死以先吩咐說：

約瑟的兄弟們現在十分害怕，擔心他會報復他們以前的殘酷。他們以為約瑟對父親的親情使他不在父親活著的時候報復他們。這句話的原意為他們打發他們當中的一位，很可能是便雅憫，去請求約瑟尊重他們父親在他臨終前的遺願並懇求饒恕。我們沒有理由把他們提到父親的遺願僅僅看作一種藉口。雅各在他的祝福中沒有提到他們的罪，證明他作為父親已經饒恕兒子們的罪了，因為上帝的恩典已使他們的罪行成為了其家族得救的途徑。
16.en: **Thy father did command.** Joseph’s brothers were now filled with alarm, fearing that he might avenge himself for their cruelty. They thought that Joseph’s tender love for his aged father might have restrained him from taking revenge so long as he lived. Literally, “they charged Joseph,” meaning they sent one of their number, possibly Benjamin, to appeal to Joseph to honor the desire expressed by their father before his death and to implore forgiveness. There is no reason for regarding the appeal to their father’s wish as a mere pretense. The fact that no reference was made to their sin by Jacob in his blessings proves that he, as their father, had forgiven the sin of his sons, in view of the fact that the grace of God had made their crime the means of his family’s salvation.

17.zh:
你們要對約瑟這樣說：從前你哥哥們惡待你，求你饒恕他們的過犯和罪惡。如今求你饒恕你父親神之僕人的過犯。他們對約瑟說這話，約瑟就哭了。

兄弟們沒有親自來到約瑟面前。他們對他的愛竟有這樣的誤解，令他感到非常傷心。
17.en: **Joseph wept.** Inasmuch as the brothers did not personally appear before Joseph, it would perhaps be better to translate, “Joseph wept at their address to him.” He was hurt that they should for a single moment have entertained such a misconception of his love.

18.zh:
他的哥哥們又來俯伏在他面前，說：我們是你的僕人。

得知約瑟沒有報復的意思後，他們才敢親自前來見他，表示願意作他的奴隸。其實約瑟心中從來就沒有想過要報復。他的心靈充滿了寬恕之心。他雖然親身體會到人類的奸詐，卻從未懷過任何怨恨的念頭。他急忙向兄弟們保證說，他們不必怕他，並且可以完全相信他。
18.en: **His brethren also went.** Assured that Joseph had no intention of taking revenge, they dared to meet him personally, offering themselves as his slaves. But any thought of revenge was far from Joseph’s thinking. The spirit of his inner life was permeated with forgiveness. Though acquainted by experience with human treachery, he had never entertained any thoughts of bitterness or hatred. He hastened to assure his brothers that they had nothing to fear of him, but could trust him completely.

22.zh:
約瑟和他父親的眷屬都住在埃及。約瑟活了一百一十歲。

約瑟是在他父親九十一歲時出生的（見創27:1；創47:9註釋），所以他在他父親去世時是五十六歲，他比他父親多活了五十四年。
22.en: **Joseph lived an hundred and ten years.** Since Joseph had been born when his father was 91 years of age (see on chs. 27:1; 47:9), he was 56 at his father’s death, and consequently outlived his father by 54 years.

23.zh:
約瑟得見以法蓮第三代的子孫。瑪拿西的孫子、瑪吉的兒子也養在約瑟的膝上。

我們不知道這裡指的是以法蓮的曾孫還是孫子。十誡第二條誡命中“三四代”的說法（出20:5；申5:9）顯然包括父親及孫子和曾孫。在民14:18中也有同樣的意義。但出34:7原文的順序是：父、子、子之子、第三和第四代，最後的兩代顯然是指曾孫和重孫。由於有時父親被包括在內，有時又排除在外，因此我們無法確定約瑟所見到的是哪一代。摩西顯然是想說明約瑟活著見到他父親之祝福的初步應驗。約瑟得見以法蓮的曾孫並不是不可能。由於他的兩個兒子是在他三十七歲前出生的（創41:50），所以他在五六十歲的時候可能就有孫子，二十年後當他八十歲的時候，他就可以有曾孫了。在他大約一百歲的時候，他就可能有重孫了。
**瑪吉的兒子。**對於瑪拿西的孩子，摩西講得更具體一些，特別提到約瑟得見他自己的曾孫。
**養在約瑟的膝上。**見創30:3註釋。
23.en:
**Joseph saw Ephraim’s children.** It is not certain whether Ephraim’s great-grandchildren or his grandchildren are meant. In the second commandment of the Decalogue the expression “third and fourth generation” (Ex. 20:5; Deut. 5:9) apparently includes the fathers, and means the grandchildren and great-grandchildren. It is used in the same sense in Num. 14:18. However, in Ex. 34:7, where the following sequence is given, fathers, children, children’s children, third and fourth generation, the latter two generations obviously refer to great-grandchildren and great-great-grandchildren. Since sometimes the father is included in the number of generations mentioned, and sometimes excluded, it is uncertain, in Joseph’s case, what was meant. At the same time it is perfectly clear that Moses desired to show that Joseph lived to see the beginning of the fulfillment of his father’s blessing. There is no practical difficulty in Joseph’s seeing the great-grandsons of Ephraim. Since his 2 sons were born before he himself was 37 years old (ch. 41:50), he may have had grandsons by the time he was 56 or 60, and great-grandsons 20 years later at the age of 80. Great—grandsons may thus have been born when he was approximately 100 years old.
**The children also of Machir.** In the case of Manasseh’s children Moses is more definite, stating specifically that Joseph saw his own great-grandchildren.
**Upon Joseph’s knees.** Literally, “were born upon Joseph’s knees” (see on ch. 30:3).
**I die.** As Joseph saw death approaching, he expressed to his brothers firm belief in the fulfillment of the divine promise (see chs. 46:4, 5; 15:16). He placed them under oath, that when God should lead them to the Promised Land they would bury his bones there. This desire was carried out. When he died he was embalmed, like his father (see on vs. 2, 3), and placed in a coffin. His body probably was accorded a temporary burial in a previously prepared tomb, according to Egyptian custom, and remained in Egypt until the time of the Exodus. At that time the Israelites, fulfilling his desire, carried his remains to Canaan and buried them at Shechem, in the piece of land that had been bought by Jacob and given to his son Joseph (Gen. 33:19; 48:22; Joshua 24:32).
In an act of faith on the part of the dying Joseph the history of the patriarchal period ends. His coffin, or tomb, became to the sojourners in Egypt a constant reminder of the promises of God, that their permanent abode was to be the land of Canaan and not Egypt. It remained a standing exhortation to them to turn their eyes from Egypt to Canaan, and to wait in patience and faith for the fulfillment of the promise God had made to their fathers.

24.zh:
約瑟對他弟兄們說：我要死了，但神必定看顧你們，領你們從這地上去，到他起誓所應許給亞伯拉罕、以撒、雅各之地。

當約瑟看到死亡臨近時，就向兄弟們表達了自己堅信上帝應許的應驗（見創46:4,5；15:16）。他叫他們起誓，當上帝領他們回應許之地時，他們要把他的埋葬在那裡。這一願望後來實現了。他去世以後，像他的父親一樣被薰屍（見第2,3節註釋），安放在一個棺材裡。他的遺體可能按照埃及人的習慣，臨時性安葬在事先預備好的陵墓中，一直保留到以色列人出埃及的時候。那時，以色列人實現了他的遺願，將他的遺體運到迦南埋葬在示劍，就是那塊雅各所購買賜給了他兒子約瑟的土地（創33:19；48:22；書24:32）。
先祖時代的歷史在約瑟臨終的一個信心之舉中結束了。他的棺材或陵墓不斷提醒在埃及寄居的人：他們永久的居所是在迦南而不是在埃及，同時也經常告戒他們要將目光從埃及轉向迦南；要憑著耐心和信心地等候上帝對他們祖先承諾的應驗。

0.zh:
**一、卷名**
猶太人給《創世記》定名是根據希伯來文本的第一個詞beres-hith，意思是“起始”,但猶大《塔木德》則稱之為“世界創造之書”。“創世記”一詞名意為“起源”，最早是七十士譯本用來指該卷書的內容。英語譯本採用了這個詞。副標題“摩西的第一卷書”希伯來原著中是沒有的，而是幾世紀以後加上去的。
**二、作者**
猶太人和基督徒都認為，出埃及時期希伯來人偉大的立法者和領袖摩西是《創世記》的作者。在基督教初期的一段時間裡，曾有異教學者對此提出異議，可是大約十八世紀中葉以前的所有基督徒和猶太人從來沒有真正地懷疑過這一點。從兩個多世紀以前開始，人們對人類思想各個領域的信念和見解提出疑問，從而在一些未知的領域中有了發現，種種的發明大大改變了這個世界的生活方式。然而，這同一種好問的精神也引導一些喜歡批評的人對於作為基督教信仰基礎的聖經的真實性提出了疑問。
《創世記》是現代第一部受到嚴格考察的書，從而開始了聖經高等考證的時代。1753年，法國的一位法醫讓·阿斯特魯克（Sean Astruc）出版了一本題為《推測》（Conjectures）的書，聲稱《創世記》裡上帝的不同名稱證明它是由不同來源的材料編集而成。阿斯特魯克承認摩西是這些材料的收集者和編篡者，可是他的追隨者不久就不承認摩西為《創世記》的編者。喜歡批評的神學家們在兩個多世紀時間裡一直試圖把《創世記》所謂的不同來源區分開來，說《創世記》出自不同作家的手，至少是在所謂若干個階段裡撰寫、整理、修改、編輯，最後合成一本書。學者們堅持這些批評的觀點，並在一項重大原則上達成一致意見，即《創世記》是由許多不同價值觀，不同作者，不同時間的不同文稿所組成，但是他們在哪些部分屬於某一時期，哪些部分屬於另一時期的問題上意見大不相同。各個批評學派大相徑庭的見解表明他們假設的基礎是何等不穩。過去一百年裡考古的發現已證明了許多批評意見的錯誤。批評家們不得不經常改變自己的理論和說法。然而他們當中仍有許人以種種理由不承認摩西為《創世記》的作者。現將他們的若干理由羅列如下:
１、《創世記》使用了三個不同的上帝名稱，在某一部分顯然愛用一個名稱，在另一部分則用另一名稱，這證明《創世記》不止一人所著。一些批評家認為多采用“耶和華”（希伯來語YHWH或JHWH“亞衛”）的部分為“亞衛底本”的作者所寫，簡寫為J，而主要採用“艾洛希姆”稱號的部分為所謂的“艾洛希姆底本”的作者所著，簡寫為E，參予《創世記》編著的其他作者據說還有一位祭司（即“祭司底本”，簡寫為P），一位編輯者(R),以及其他的人。
２、根據一些批評家的看法，《創世記》中故事多處出現的重複，表明是一位後來的作者採用了一些平行的記敘，並草草編集而成。這位作者無法隱瞞他採用了不同來源材料的事實。
３、《創世記》故事的環境與當時的時代不符，反而與遲得多的時代相符。
４、一些地名採用的是遲得多的名稱，而不是原來不同的名稱。
５、古巴比倫關於創造，洪水和先祖的傳說與聖經的記載十分相似，所以大部分現代神學家認為希伯來作者是在被擄期間吸收了巴比倫的傳說，按照一神論的觀點進行改編，以迎合希伯來的讀者。
保守的基督徒不同意上面的觀點，理由如下:
１、上帝，主，耶和華的聖名在整部希伯來文聖經都是多少有點隨意選用的，不能證明其出於不同的作者，象批評家們所說的那樣，七十士譯本和最古老的希伯來聖經抄本，包括最近發現的以賽亞古卷，表明在某一種抄本的某一段落採用“上帝”的地方，在另一抄本中則採用“主”或“耶和華”，相反的情況也有。
２、敘事中的重複並不一定證明某一文學作品來自不同的來源。維護摩西著作統一性的人發現聖經以外的許多文學作品，不論是古代的還是現代的，由同一位作者所寫的著作也有著類似的重複。
３、對於古代歷史和環境瞭解的增加，表明《創世記》的作者很熟悉他所描寫的時代。有關先祖的記載與當時的環境完全吻合。
４、抄錄聖經的人在某些地方採用較後的地名是為了便於讀者的理解。
５、巴比倫的傳說與希伯來文字記錄某些方面的相似性，不能證明一個民族的說法是從另一個民族那裡吸收來的，而只能從它們是有共同的來源這一點上得到解釋。《創世記》是靈感之作，以崇高純潔的形式敘述事件，而巴比倫的傳說則以低級異教的格調敘述同樣的事件。
本文的目的不是駁斥高等考證家用以支持他們學說的種種論點。更重要的是要注意摩西作為作者的證據。
《出埃及記》的作者一定是創世記的作者，因為五經的第二卷是第一卷的繼續，明顯地體現相同的精神和宗旨。既然基督曾親自證實《出埃及記》的作者，稱之為“摩西的書”（可12:26），前面一卷《創世記》也一定是摩西所寫的。《出埃及記》所用的詞語和表達方式，以及約瑟的歷史中所表顯出來對埃及生活和風俗的熟悉，與摩西所受的教育和經歷是一致的。雖然《創世記》由摩西所寫的證據沒有《出埃及記》那樣的明顯和直接，但摩西五經共有的語言特點證明它們是出於同一位作者。新約的證言也指出摩西是在聖靈的感動下寫作的。
耶穌基督曾數次引用《創世記》。祂的證言表明祂把《創世記》看作聖經的一部分。祂引用了創1:27和2:24後，講了祂引聖經時常用的一句話:“你們沒有念過嗎？”（太19:4,5）這表明引文中所含的真理仍然有效，具有約束力。當時耶穌是在與法利賽人辯論上帝有關離婚的法律。在這段記錄中（可10:2-9），很明顯地看出耶穌把《創世記》的引文視為摩西所作。當耶穌的對手們問祂有沒有權利休妻時，祂沒有直接回答，而反問說:“摩西吩咐你們的是什麼？”法利賽人在回答時引用了五經的第五卷《申命記》24:1-4中摩西的一項規定。對於這一點，基督說，摩西給他們定了這一條是因為他們心地剛硬，原來並不是這樣的。接著祂引用了摩西的另外兩段話來支持自己的說法（創1:27；2:24）。
在其他幾個場合，耶穌提到一些只記載在《創世記》的事件，表明祂把《創世記》看作是準確的歷史記錄（見路17:26-29；約8:37等）。
在使徒的著作中也多次引用了《創世記》，清楚地表明他們確信《創世記》為摩西在靈感之下所作（見羅4:17；加3:8；4:30；來4:4；雅2:23）。
根據上述的證據，基督徒可以確信摩西是《創世記》的作者。懷愛倫寫到摩西客居米甸時說:“摩西在這裡受聖靈感動，寫下了《創世記》。”（《先祖與先知》251頁）
**三、歷史背景**
《創世記》寫於公元之前1500年左右，希伯來人在埃及地為奴期間（《善惡之爭》第五章），概述了我們這個世界多世紀的歷史。《創世記》的頭幾章無法置於某一歷史背景之中，像我們在一般情況下探討歷史時那樣。除了摩西的著作以外，我們沒有任何洪水以前的歷史文物。我們也沒有考古的記錄，只有化石沉默而往往又是含糊的見證。
洪水以後情況就不一樣了，考古學家發掘出許多文物，涉及到《創世記後》較後章節時期的人民，風俗，政體等。例如我們對亞伯拉罕時代就瞭解得相當清楚。以色列人為奴時期的埃及歷史記錄可以相當準確地恢復起來。從亞伯拉罕到出埃及這段時期中，發展起高度的文明，特別是在米索不達米地區和尼羅河流域。在北方，赫人強盛起來。在巴勒斯坦，居住著好戰的民族，領導他們的是一些小國王。野蠻的習俗反映了所有這些民族黑暗的異教信仰。
牢固的種族紐帶把《創世記》先祖同上米索不大米和下米索不大米的閃米特各部族聯繫在一起。《創世記》詳細描述了先祖在一些古代重要歷史事件中所起的作用。如西訂谷列王之戰（14章），平原諸城的毀滅（18,19章）以及在大饑荒時期埃及人得蒙保護等。《創世記》裡面的人物有牧人也有戰士，有市民也有遊牧者，有政治家也有逃亡者，他們的故事使《創世記》的讀者瞭解那些經常與希伯來人接觸的較為次要的民族，和遠古的偉大民族。
《創世記》並沒有描寫產生於埃及和米索不大米的偉大文明。可是在先祖的經歷中，我們可以強烈地感受到這些文明的存在。上帝的子民並不是生活在世外桃源之中，脫離社會和政治。他們是人類社會的一部分。除了他們的宗教信仰以外，他們的文明和文化與周圍的民族沒有什麼顯著的區別。在真正敬拜耶和華的人中，他們是最重要的餘民，所以他們就成了聖經作者視野的中心。這種顯著的側重自然令人發問:摩西創作《創世記》的主要目的是什麼？
**四、主題**
每一個仔細研究《創世記》的人都注意到該書主題首先是敘述了上帝如何對待少數愛祂、事奉祂、忠於祂的人，其次是那些離棄上帝和祂訓誨的人墮落到多麼深的地步。《創世記》是上帝賜給人啟示的第一部永恆記錄。
就教義而言，這部書也很重要，其中記載了這個世界和一切生物的被造，罪的侵入，上帝救恩的應許。它告訴我們，人類擁有自由的判斷力和意志。干犯上帝的律法是一切災禍的根源。它教導我們當遵守聖安息日為休息和崇拜的日子，以及婚姻的神聖性，家庭的建立，順從的報賞，犯罪的懲罰等。
《創世記》的寫作文體風趣盎然，對青年人的思想富有感染力，其中高尚的道德主題又是成年人的精神食糧。《創世記》中的教誨對所有的人都有助益。任何基督徒都不應忽略研究這一卷書，其中那些光彩奪目的人物值得每一個上帝的兒女所效妨。
